items.title: Proposition 3.6.5 (preprint 3.52): the linearization at a zero is Fredholm of index $n - N$

book.label: §3.6, Proposition 3.6.5 (preprint 3.52), p. 135 (preprint p. 110)
book.statement: If $f$ is an sc-Fredholm section of the tame strong bundle $P : Y \to X$ and $f(x) = 0$, then $Tf(x) : T_xX \to Y_x$ is an sc-Fredholm operator (of the index $n - N$ of the basic germ, as the proof of Theorem 3.6.8 (preprint 3.54) uses).

lean.statement: For a section $f$ with $(f, x_0)$ an sc-Fredholm germ and $f(x_0) = 0$: in the chart of Definition 3.1.11 (preprint 3.11) centred at $x_0$, with the filling germ $g$ (a derivative family $Dg$ on a germ $G \subseteq U$) and the local sc$^+$-germ $s$, $Dg(0) : E \to F$ is an sc-Fredholm operator, $T_0O = Dr(0)E$ and $K_0 = \rho(0)F$ are sc-subspaces, and $Tf(x_0) = Dg(0)|_{T_0O} : T_0O \to K_0$ is an sc-Fredholm operator; for **every** conjugation of $g - s$ to a basic germ $h : O(\widetilde C \oplus W, 0) \to \mathbb R^N \oplus W$, $\widetilde C \subseteq \mathbb R^n$ (`ConjugationData`), both are Fredholm of index $n - N$ on every level. In particular $n - N$ does not depend on the conjugation. For an sc-Fredholm section the same holds in **every** strong bundle chart around a zero $y$: at the point $z$ over $y$, $T_zO = Dr(z)E$ and $K_z = \rho(z)F$ are sc-subspaces and $\mathrm{Lin}(z) : T_zO \to K_z$ is sc-Fredholm, of index $n - N$ on every level.

diff: Proved in sc form, in charts: $T_0O$, $K_0$ (and $T_zO$, $K_z$ in any chart) with the induced sc-structures stand for $T_xX$, $Y_x$, which carry no linear structure here (G.7). Two steps the text leaves out: that $D(g - s)(0) = \Gamma(0)^{-1}Dh(0)D\psi(0)$, the conjugate of the basic germ's linearization, is sc-Fredholm (the criterion of V1.8: $\Gamma(0)$ preserves the levels and $Dh(0)$ is regularizing), and the sc-structures of $T_0O$, $K_0$ (Definition 2.6.1 (preprint 2.47) at the smooth point $0$, the closed graph theorem). No tameness is assumed. In other charts the levels are transported by the chart change at smooth points (Findings, Chapter 3, items 235, 239). Formerly level $0$ only (G.22, Findings item 48); updated in the third addendum of this page.

The first formal statement (`proposition_3_52`, kept for the theorems that use it) gives the index as “$n - N$ for some $n, N \in \mathbb N$”, which every integer satisfies. `proposition_3_52_index` names the conjugation data and identifies $n$, $N$ with the dimensions of the conjugating basic germ, for every conjugation (Findings, Chapter 3, item 120). Updated after the first edition of this page.
In every other strong bundle chart around $x_0$ the linearization is Fredholm of the same index, and onto at a zero in good position (V3.96). Updated in the second addendum of this page.

**Germs.** The hypothesis is the text’s since the switch to the germ reading (phase 2): an sc-Fredholm germ whose filling and sc$^+$-section are germs whose levels may shrink with $m$ (V3.13); $Dg(0)$ is the value at $0$ of a derivative family of the filling germ, the same for every family on every germ. The forms for germ data on the whole chart are the `_wholeChart` declarations of the same names (Findings, Chapter 3, items 220–221, 289, 310, 331). Hence “restated” (formerly “narrower”, for that hypothesis): what remains is the reading in charts.

items.title: Definition 3.6.6 (preprint 3.53): good position of an sc-Fredholm germ

book.label: §3.6, Definition 3.6.6 (preprint 3.53), p. 136 (preprint p. 111)
book.statement: An sc-Fredholm germ $(f, x)$ of a tame strong bundle with $f(x) = 0$ is in good position if (1) $f'(x) : T_xX \to Y_x$ is surjective and (2) if $d_X(x) \ge 1$, $\ker f'(x)$ is in good position to the partial cone $C_xX$ in $T_xX$.

lean.statement: In the chart of Definition 3.1.11 (preprint 3.11) (`IsGoodPositionAtGerm`, at $Dg(0)$ for a derivative family $Dg$ of the filling germ $g$): $Tf(0) = Dg(0)|_{T_0O} : T_0O \to K_0$ is onto and $\ker Dg(0)$ is in good position to $C_0O = T_0O \cap C$ inside $T_0O$ (`IsInGoodPositionIn`); `IsGoodPositionAt` is the case of a whole-chart filled version. For a section (`StrongBundle.IsGoodPositionGerm f x₀`): the data of Definition 3.1.11 (preprint 3.11) at $x_0$ with the germ in good position in that chart. With the text’s sc-complement (`IsGoodPositionAtScGerm`; for a section `StrongBundle.IsGoodPositionGermSc`, in a tame chart): the kernel has a good sc-complement inside $T_0O$ ($T_m = N_m \oplus P_m$ on every level). At a zero of an sc-Fredholm section with tame germ data the two forms agree.

chips: sc-complement form: the same at zeros
diff: Stated in a chart centred at $x$, not in $T_xX$ (the transport of $C_xX$ to $T_xX$ is not formalized, Chapter 2 gap). The case distinction $d_X(x) \ge 1$ is dropped: at an interior point (2) holds trivially (Findings, Chapter 3, item 50), and for tame germ data good position in a tame chart at a zero with $d_X = 0$ is the surjectivity of the linearization (V3.100).

At a zero, the linearization and the two conditions do not depend on the chart (V3.78); Definition 3.6.6 (preprint 3.53) at a zero from a chart not centred there is V3.79, in any chart of the germ data V3.107. The form in a tame chart (`StrongBundle.IsGoodPositionGermTame`), which the theorems of §3.6 assume and conclude, is V3.103.

The sc form needs the kernel smooth and a closed good complement in $E$. At a zero $\ker Dg(0)$ is the image under $D\psi'(0)$ of the basic germ's smooth kernel, and the good position of the kernel in $E$ comes from the transport from $T_0O$, so V3.20 applies (Findings, Chapter 3, item 212). “$T = N \oplus P$ an sc-splitting of $T$” is written in $E$; its equivalence with an sc-splitting of the sc-Banach space $T_0O$ is not formalized, nor is the upgrade from good position inside $T$ alone (items 211, 214). Updated in the third addendum of this page.

**Germs.** Since the switch to the text’s germ reading (phase 2) the germ data are the text’s (V3.13), and the condition in the chart is read at $Dg(0)$, the value at $0$ of any derivative family of the filling germ (the same for all, `IsGoodPositionGerm.forall_isGoodPositionAtGerm`); the whole-chart forms are `IsGoodPositionGermWholeChart`, `IsGoodPositionGermScWholeChart` (Findings, Chapter 3, items 220–221, 280, 320, 330).

items.title: Theorem 3.6.8 (preprint 3.54): the solution set as a graph (part (3) of the proof)

book.label: §3.6, Theorem 3.6.8 (preprint 3.54), p. 136 (preprint p. 111) (proof pp. 136–140 (preprint pp. 111–115))
book.statement: Let $f$ be an sc-Fredholm section of a tame strong bundle with $f(x) = 0$ and $(f, x)$ in good position. There is an open $V \ni x$ such that $S = \{y \in V \mid f(y) = 0\}$ has: (1) at every $y \in S$, $(f, y)$ is in good position; (2) $S$ is a sub-M-polyfold whose induced structure is equivalent to a smooth manifold with boundary with corners. The proof shows (3): $\psi\varphi(S) = \{v + \sigma(v) \mid v \in V'\}$ for the $\sigma$ of Theorem 3.5.11 (preprint Corollary 3.47) applied to $\Psi_*(g) = h + t$.

lean.statement: For a section $f$ of a strong bundle, $f(x_0) = 0$ and $(f, x_0)$ in good position in a tame chart (V3.103): a tame chart $\varphi$ centred at $x_0$, the conjugating sc-diffeomorphism $\psi$ with its inverse, a basic germ $h' = h + (t_{\mathbb R^N}, 0)$ with the data of Theorem 3.4.2 (preprint 3.38) and $D(h + t)(0)$ surjective with kernel $K$ in good position, $K$ a smooth subspace; a **closed** good complement $Y$; $V'$ relatively open in $K \cap C'$, $\sigma : V' \to Y$ $C^1$ with values on level $1$, $\sigma(0) = 0$, $D\sigma(0) = 0$, every $v + \sigma(v)$ a zero of $h + t$, and $C^k$-lifts $\sigma_k : V_k \to E'_k$ near $0$ for every $k$ (Theorem 3.5.11 (1) (preprint Corollary 3.47)); and an open $V_x \ni x_0$ on which $\psi\varphi$ is injective, $f(y) = 0 \iff (h + t)(\psi\varphi(y)) = 0$, and $\psi\varphi(\{y \in V_x \mid f(y) = 0\}) = \{v + \sigma(v) \mid v \in V'\}$.

diff: This row is the graph description (3) of the proof. Conclusions (1) and (2) of the theorem are formalized since the first edition of this page: V3.82 (under an added hypothesis) and V3.85; the choice of $Y$ with the projection property is V3.77.

Tameness enters through $(1 - Dr(0))E \subseteq E_0$ (Proposition 2.5.3 (preprint 2.35)), for the base retraction of the chart at $x_0$; the text's $C' = T\psi(0)C$ is proved by the sign argument; the $\mathbb R^N$-component of $t$ is absorbed into $h$; $D(h + t)(0)$ is identified with $D(\Psi_*g)(0)$ by uniqueness on level $1$; the unspecified $V$ is made explicit (items 50, 85, 86). The closedness of $Y$, the smoothness of $K$ and the lifts of $\sigma$ are recorded for Definition 3.2.1 (preprint 3.25) (items 93, 94).

Updated after the repair of the tameness hypothesis: first proved with “the base retraction of every strong bundle chart compatible with the atlas is tame” (`htame`), which no strong bundle over a nonempty base satisfies (V3.104), so that form was vacuous; now with the hypotheses of V3.103 (Findings, Chapter 3, items 190–192).

items.title: Lemma 3.6.9 (preprint 3.55): good position along a graph

book.label: §3.6, Lemma 3.6.9 (preprint 3.55), p. 139 (preprint p. 114) (proof §3.8.4 (preprint §3.8.3), pp. 160–164 (preprint pp. 132–135))
book.statement: $C \subseteq E$ a partial quadrant, $N$ a finite-dimensional smooth subspace in good position with good complement $Y$, $V \subseteq N \cap C$ relatively open, $\tau : V \to Y_1$ of class $C^1$ with $\tau(0) = 0$, $D\tau(0) = 0$. Then for $v$ in a relatively open $V' \ni 0$: (1) $v + \tau(v) \in C_1$; (2) $Y$ is a topological complement of $N_v = \{n + D\tau(v)n\}$; (3) there is $\gamma_v > 0$ with $n \in C_x \iff n + y \in C_x$ for $n \in N_v$, $y \in Y$, $|y|_0 \le \gamma_v|n|_0$, $x = v + \tau(v)$.

lean.statement: In the model $E = \mathbb R^n \oplus W$, $C = [0, \infty)^n \oplus W$ (in coordinates for any $C$ cut out by functionals): for $N$ in good position with **closed** good complement $Y$ and $\tau : N \to E$ with values in $Y$, $C^1$ on $N \cap C$, $\tau(0) = 0$, $D\tau(0) = 0$: there is $\rho > 0$ such that for $v \in N \cap C$, $|v| < \rho$: $v + \tau(v) \in C$ and $Y$ is a good complement of $N_v$ with respect to $C_{v + \tau(v)}$ (so $E_0 = N_v \oplus Y$, both closed), with a constant independent of $v$.

diff: **Added hypothesis: $Y$ closed**, needed for \"$D\tau(v)n \in Y$\" (the text's topological complement is closed) (Findings, Chapter 3, item 49).

$\tau$ is a map on all of $N \cap C$ (the text: on a neighbourhood $V$). The form used in Theorem 3.6.8 (preprint 3.54) — $\sigma$ on a relatively open $V \subseteq N \cap C$, any presentation of $C$, and the good position of $N_v$ — is `lemma_3_55_relOpen` (V3.80): $\sigma$ is extended to the cone by a bump. The sc-level of the values plays no role ((1) is $v + \tau(v) \in C$). The constant $\gamma_v$ can be chosen uniformly; the case $v \notin N \cap W$ needs no normal form.

items.title: Theorem 3.6.10 (preprint 3.56): the global implicit function theorem, $\partial X = \emptyset$ (from the tangent germ property)

book.label: §3.6, Theorem 3.6.10 (preprint 3.56), p. 140 (preprint p. 115)
book.statement: If $P : Y \to X$ is a tame strong bundle over an M-polyfold with $\partial X = \emptyset$ and $f$ an sc-Fredholm section with surjective linearization at every point of $S = \{f = 0\}$, then $S$ is a sub-M-polyfold whose induced structure is equivalent to a smooth manifold without boundary.

chips: assumes the tangent germ property of $S$

items.title: Theorem 3.6.11 (preprint 3.57): the global implicit function theorem, boundary case (from the tangent germ property)

items.title: Lemma 3.7.2 (preprint 3.59): injectivity of $P_Y Df(b)$ on $X$ near $0$ (abstract form)

book.label: §3.7, Lemma 3.7.2 (preprint 3.59), p. 141 (preprint p. 117)
book.statement: In the setting of Theorem 3.7.1 (preprint 3.58) ($Y = Df(0)X$, $P_Y$ the projection along a finite-dimensional complement $A$), there is a relatively open neighbourhood $O$ of $0$ in $B \cap C$ such that $P_Y \circ Df(b) : X \to Y$ has trivial kernel for $b \in O$.

lean.statement: For a family $b \mapsto L(b)$ of sc-operators $X \to Y$ with $(b, h) \mapsto L(b)h$ continuous on $O \times X_0$ ($O \ni 0$), $L(0)$ injective on $X_0$, and the compactness property on level $0$ (`FamilyCompactness`: $b_j \to b$, $h_j$ bounded, $L(b_j)h_j \to 0$ imply a convergent subsequence of $h_j$): $L(b)$ is injective on $X_0$ for $b \in O$ near $0$.

In the proof of Theorem 3.7.1 (preprint 3.58) these hypotheses are derived from the theorem's (`familyCompactness_derivFamOp`, `continuousOn_derivFamOp`; V3.89; Findings, Chapter 3, item 73).

items.title: Lemma 3.7.3 (preprint 3.60): uniform lower bounds (abstract form)

book.label: §3.7, Lemma 3.7.3 (preprint 3.60), p. 142 (preprint p. 118)
book.statement: For a relatively open $\widetilde O \ni 0$ in $C \cap B$ with compact closure in $O$ (Lemma 3.7.2 (preprint 3.59)), for every $m$ there is $c_m > 0$ with $|P_Y \circ Df(b)h|_m \ge c_m|h|_m$ for $b \in \widetilde O$, $h \in X_m$.

diff: The injectivity of every $L(b)_m$ on $K$ is a hypothesis; in the proof of Theorem 3.7.1 (preprint 3.58) it comes from Lemma 3.7.2 (preprint 3.59) on level $0$ and `ScOperator.injective_lvl` (V3.89). items.title: Lemma 3.7.4 (preprint 3.61): the inverse of a family of sc-isomorphisms

book.label: §3.7, Lemma 3.7.4 (preprint 3.61), p. 142 (preprint p. 118) (quoted from [25, Proposition 4.8], no proof)
book.statement: Let $V$ be relatively open in a partial quadrant of a finite-dimensional $G$, $v \mapsto L(v)$ a family of sc-isomorphisms $E \to F$ with $(v, h) \mapsto L(v)h$ sc-smooth and $|L(v)h|_m \ge c_m|h|_m$ for $v \in V$, $h \in E_m$. lean.statement: For a germ $V$ of relatively open neighbourhoods of $0$ in a partial quadrant $\widetilde C$ of a finite-dimensional $G$ and sc-isomorphisms $L(v) : E \to F$ such that $\Phi(v, h) = L(v)h$ is an sc-smooth germ on $V \oplus E$ and $c_m\|h\| \le \|L(v)_mh\|$ for $v \in V_0$: $\Lambda(v, k) = L(v)^{-1}k$ is an sc-smooth germ on $V \oplus F$, with derivative $D\Lambda(v, k)(\delta v, \delta k) = L(v)^{-1}(\delta k - D_1\Phi(v, L(v)^{-1}k)\delta v)$.

items.title: Lemma 3.8.8 (preprint 3.65): good complements avoid the vanishing coordinates

items.title: Proposition 3.8.12 (preprint 3.69): the degeneracy index of $N \cap C$

book.label: §3.8.1, Proposition 3.8.12 (preprint 3.69), p. 153 (preprint p. 126)
book.statement: For $N$ smooth, finite-dimensional, in good position to $C = [0, \infty)^n \oplus W$ in $E = \mathbb R^n \oplus W$, and $x \in N \cap C$: (1) $d_{N \cap C}(x) = d_C(x)$ if $x \notin N \cap W$; (2) $d_{N \cap C}(x) = \dim N - \dim(N \cap W)$ if $x \in N \cap W$.

items.title: Lemma 3.8.13 (preprint 3.70): the degeneracy index along a graph

book.label: §3.8.1, Lemma 3.8.13 (preprint 3.70), p. 154 (preprint p. 127)
book.statement: For $N$ in good position to $C = [0, \infty)^n \oplus W$ with good complement $Y$ and $\tau : N \cap C \to Y_1$ of class $C^1$, $\tau(0) = 0$, $D\tau(0) = 0$: $d_{N \cap C}(v) = d_C(v + \tau(v))$ for $v \in N \cap C \setminus N \cap W$ close to $0$.

items.title: Theorem 3.8.15 (preprint 3.72): the quadrant inverse function theorem

items.title: Proposition 3.8.17 (preprint 3.73): the normalized inverse function theorem

book.label: §3.8.5 (preprint §3.8.4), Proposition 3.8.17 (preprint 3.73), p. 165 (preprint p. 137)
book.statement: $U \subseteq C$ relatively open, convex, $0 \in U$, $f : U \to C$ smooth with (1) $f(0) = 0$, (2) $|Df(x) - 1| \le \tfrac12$, (3) $d_C(x) = d_C(f(x))$. Then $V = f(U)$ is relatively open in $C$ and $f : U \to V$ is a diffeomorphism.

items.title: Lemma 3.8.18 (preprint 3.74): bi-Lipschitz estimate and openness

book.label: §3.8.5 (preprint §3.8.4), Lemma 3.8.18 (preprint 3.74), p. 165 (preprint p. 137) (proof pp. 165–167 (preprint pp. 137–139))
book.statement: Under the assumptions of Proposition 3.8.17 (preprint 3.73), $V = f(U)$ is relatively open and $f : U \to V$ open, with $\tfrac12|x - x'| \le |f(x) - f(x')| \le \tfrac32|x - x'|$.

items.title: Lemma 3.8.21 (preprint 3.77): the inverse is $C^1$

items.title: Theorem 3.8.22 (preprint 3.78): the implicit function theorem in partial quadrants

book.label: §3.8.6 (preprint §3.8.5), Theorem 3.8.22 (preprint 3.78), p. 169 (preprint p. 141)
book.statement: $U$ a relatively open neighbourhood of $0$ in $C = [0, \infty)^k \oplus \mathbb R^{n-k}$, $f : U \to \mathbb R^N$ of class $C^j$, $f(0) = 0$, $Df(0)$ onto, $K = \ker Df(0)$ in good position with good complement $Y$. Then there are $V$ open in $K \cap C$, a $C^j$ map $\tau : V \to Y$ and $\varepsilon, \sigma > 0$ with (1) $\tau(0) = 0$, $D\tau(0) = 0$, $k + \tau(k) \in U$; (2) $|\tau(k)| \le \sigma$ for $|k| \le \varepsilon$; (3) $f(k + y) = 0$, $|k| \le \varepsilon$, $|y| \le \sigma$ imply $y = \tau(k)$.

lean.statement: For a partial quadrant $C$ in a finite-dimensional $V$, $f : U \to F$ ($F$ any normed space) of class $C^j$, $j \ge 1$, with the hypotheses: $V'$ relatively open in $K \cap C$, $\tau : K \to Y$ of class $C^j$ on $V'$ with (1) $\tau(0) = 0$, $D\tau(0) = 0$, **$k + \tau(k) \in U$ and $f(k + \tau(k)) = 0$**; (2); (3) for $y \in Y$ with **$k + y \in U$**.

diff: **Two clauses the text omits are included**: $f(k + \tau(k)) = 0$ in (1) (the content of the theorem) and $k + y \in U$ in (3) (needed for $f(k + y)$ to be defined) (Findings, Chapter 3, item 22).
Only the convexity of $C$ and its nonempty interior are used (normalized form), the quadrant entering through good position (item 23); $\tau$ is $C^j$ on the whole $V_0$ without shrinking (item 24).

items.title: Lemma 3.8.23 (preprint 3.79): the contraction region

book.label: §3.8.6 (preprint §3.8.5), Lemma 3.8.23 (preprint 3.79), p. 170 (preprint p. 142)
book.statement: There are $a, b > 0$ such that on $(B_K(a) \oplus B_Y(b)) \cap C \subseteq U$ the map $B(k, \cdot)$ is a $\tfrac12$-contraction; so $f(k, y) = f(k, y')$ forces $y = y'$.

lean.statement: In the normalized data: constants $\varepsilon$, $a$, $b$ with $\varepsilon a \le b$, the region $R = \{|k| \le a, |y| \le b\} \cap C \subseteq U$ with $\|DB\| \le \varepsilon/(2(1 + \varepsilon))$ on it; the mean value inequality on $R$; a fixed point $y$ with $(k, y) \in R$ is $\tau(k)$.

diff: As in the text, with the constant $c_0 = \varepsilon/(2(1 + \varepsilon))$.

items.title: Lemma 3.8.24 (preprint 3.80): the fixed point set $X_k$

book.label: §3.8.6 (preprint §3.8.5), Lemma 3.8.24 (preprint 3.80), p. 170 (preprint p. 143)
book.statement: Replacing $a$ by a smaller number, $|B(k, y)| \le \varepsilon|k|$ for $|y| \le \varepsilon|k|$, so $B(k, \cdot)$ maps $X_k = \bar B_Y(\varepsilon|k|)$ into itself and has a unique fixed point $\tau(k)$; with $c(a) = (1 + \varepsilon)\max_{B((1+\varepsilon)a)}|DB|$.

lean.statement: $B(k, \cdot)$ maps $X_k = \{|y| \le \varepsilon|k|\}$ into itself for $k \in V_0 = \{k \in K \cap C : |k| < a\}$, and has a fixed point $\tau(k) \in X_k$ (Banach).

items.title: Lemma 3.8.25 (preprint 3.81): continuity of $\tau$

book.label: §3.8.6 (preprint §3.8.5), Lemma 3.8.25 (preprint 3.81), p. 171 (preprint p. 144)
book.statement: $\tau : B_K(a) \cap C \to B_Y(b)$ is continuous and satisfies $|\tau(k)| \le \varepsilon|k|/2$ and $|\tau(k) - \tau(k_0)| \le \varepsilon|k - k_0|$.

lean.statement: $|\tau(k)| \le \varepsilon|k|/2$ and $\tau$ is continuous on $V_0$; for all $k, k_0 \in V_0$, $|\tau(k) - \tau(k_0)| \le \frac{\varepsilon}{1 + \varepsilon}|k - k_0| \le \varepsilon|k - k_0|$, so $\tau$ is $\frac{\varepsilon}{1 + \varepsilon}$-Lipschitz on $V_0$. (An older form with the constant $1 + 2\varepsilon$ is kept for the proofs that use it.)

diff: The text's constant $\varepsilon$ holds on all of $V_0$; its proof omits a case distinction. It uses the point $(k, \tau(k_0))$, which lies in the region of the contraction when $|k_0| \le 2|k|$; otherwise $|k| < 2|k_0|$ and the same argument with $k$ and $k_0$ exchanged applies. Either way $|\tau(k) - \tau(k_0)| \le \tfrac12|\tau(k) - \tau(k_0)| + c_0|k - k_0|$ with $c_0 = \varepsilon/(2(1 + \varepsilon))$, which gives the sharper constant $\varepsilon/(1 + \varepsilon)$ (Findings, Chapter 3, item 216; revises item 25, which had only $1 + 2\varepsilon$). The older estimate is kept for `continuousOn_τ` and Lemma 3.8.26 (preprint 3.82) (item 217). Formerly narrower; updated in the third addendum of this page.

items.title: Lemma 3.8.26 (preprint 3.82): $\tau$ is of class $C^j$

book.statement: If $f$ is of class $C^j$, $j \ge 1$, then $\tau$ is of class $C^j$ on a possibly smaller neighbourhood of $0$, with $D\tau(k) = (1 - D_2B(k, \tau(k)))^{-1}D_1B(k, \tau(k))$.

items.title: Theorem 3.1.22 (preprint 3.19): the implicit function theorem, interior case (first form)

book.label: §3.1, Theorem 3.1.22 (preprint 3.19), p. 100 (preprint p. 74)
book.statement: Let $X$ be an M-polyfold with $d_X \equiv 0$, $f$ an sc-Fredholm section of a strong bundle and $f(x_0) = 0$. Then $f'(x_0) : T_{x_0}X \to Y_{x_0}$ is sc-Fredholm. If it is surjective, there is an open $U \ni x_0$ such that $S(f, U) = \{y \in U \mid f(y) = 0\}$ is a sub-M-polyfold whose induced structure is that of a smooth manifold of dimension the Fredholm index, $f'(y)$ is surjective at every $y \in S(f, U)$, and $\ker f'(y) = T_yS(f, U)$.

lean.statement: Let $d_X \equiv 0$, $f$ an sc-Fredholm section with tame germ data (V3.103), $f(x_0) = 0$, and $(f, x_0)$ in good position in a tame chart **with a filler satisfying condition (3) of Definition 3.1.4 (preprint 3.4) at its zeros near $0$** (`IsGoodPositionGermFilled`, V3.82). Then there are an open $U \ni x_0$ and $d \in \mathbb N$ such that every zero in $U$ is a smooth point with $(f, y)$ in good position in a tame chart, and $S(f, U)$ is a sub-M-polyfold whose induced structure is equivalent to a $d$-dimensional manifold with boundary with corners with degeneracy index $0$ everywhere. First clause: in the chart at $x_0$, $Dg(0)$ and $f'(x_0) = Tf(x_0) : T_0O \to K_0$ are sc-Fredholm operators and $Tf(x_0)$ is onto on every level (Proposition 3.6.5 (preprint 3.52), V3.46); in every strong bundle chart around $x_0$, $\mathrm{Lin}(z) : T_zO \to K_z$ is sc-Fredholm with the same index on every level (`StrongBundle.linAt_isScFredholm`, V3.96).

diff: **The filler condition at the nearby zeros**, through Theorem 3.6.8 (1) (preprint 3.54) (V3.82), was an added hypothesis when this form was proved; it holds whenever $(f, x_0)$ is in good position (V3.102), and the form with the text's hypotheses is V3.95 (Findings, Chapter 3, items 154, 174, 180).

The text's hypothesis “$f'(x_0)$ surjective” is read here as good position (Definition 3.6.6 (preprint 3.53) in the chart form); at $d_X = 0$ the two are the same (V3.100), and the form with “$f'(x_0)$ surjective” is V3.101.

The dimension $d$ is existentially quantified here; “the dimension agrees with the Fredholm index” is V3.97 and “$\ker f'(y) = T_yS$” in the chart V3.99. The proof is Theorem 3.1.26 (preprint 3.23) (V3.69) and Lemma 2.4.6 (preprint 2.26), $d_S \le d_X = 0$. Added after the first edition of this page; updated in the second addendum of this page.

Updated after the repair of the tameness hypothesis: first proved with “the base retraction of every strong bundle chart compatible with the atlas is tame” (`htame`), which no strong bundle over a nonempty base satisfies (V3.104), so that form was vacuous; now with the hypotheses of V3.103 (Findings, Chapter 3, items 190–192).

The first clause, “$f'(x_0)$ is sc-Fredholm”, is proved on every level: in the chart at $x_0$ by Propositions 3.1.10, 1.1.11 and 3.1.5 (preprint 3.10, 1.10 and 3.5) in sc form, and $Tf(x_0)$ is onto on every level because it is onto on level $0$ and regularizing (Findings, Chapter 3, items 235, 236); formerly level $0$ only. Updated in the third addendum of this page. The section-level sc form `theorem_3_19_linearization_sc` takes the text's sc-Fredholm section (germ reading). The clause with no chart singled out: in every strong bundle chart around $x_0$, $\mathrm{Lin}(z) : T_zO \to K_z$ is an sc-Fredholm operator with the same index on every level (`StrongBundle.linAt_isScFredholm`, V3.96); cited here since the fifth addendum of this page.

items.title: Theorem 3.1.26 (preprint 3.23): the implicit function theorem, boundary case

book.label: §3.1, Theorem 3.1.26 (preprint 3.23), p. 103 (preprint p. 77)
book.statement: Let $f$ be an sc-Fredholm section of a tame strong bundle, $f(x) = 0$, $f'(x)$ surjective with kernel in good position to $C_xX$. Then there is an open $U \ni x$ such that $S(f, U)$ consists of smooth points and is a tame sub-M-polyfold of $X$, with a uniquely determined structure of a smooth manifold with boundary with corners, the induced one of Proposition 2.3.19 (preprint 2.21).

lean.statement: Let $f$ be an sc-Fredholm section, $f(x) = 0$, $(f, x)$ in good position in a tame chart (V3.103), and let every zero in an open $V_{x_0} \ni x$ be in good position in a tame chart. Then there are an open $U$, $x \in U \subseteq V_{x_0}$, and $d \in \mathbb N$ such that every zero in $U$ is a smooth point and $S(f, U)$ is a sub-M-polyfold whose induced structure (Proposition 2.3.19 (preprint 2.21)) is tame and equivalent to that of a $d$-dimensional manifold with boundary with corners. `theorem_3_23`: the same for tame germ data under `IsGoodPositionGermFilled` at $x$ (V3.82) instead of the nearby good position, and then every zero in $U$ is in good position in a tame chart.

diff: Hypotheses of these two forms: the good position of the zeros near $x$ (which is Theorem 3.6.8 (1) (preprint 3.54), now a theorem, V3.94), or the filler condition at the nearby zeros (V3.82, a consequence of good position, V3.102). The form with the text's hypotheses is V3.95, with the dimension as the Fredholm index V3.97 (Findings, Chapter 3, items 153, 155, 170, 180).

Tameness of the bundle is read as Definitions 3.6.3, 3.6.4, 3.6.6 (preprint 3.50, 3.51, 3.53) read it: germ data and good position in tame charts (V3.103). The dimension $d$ is existentially quantified; the identification $d = \dim\ker f'(x)$ is in the proof. “Uniquely determined” is the equivalence of the atlas of the charts $\pi\varphi$ with the induced one, not stated separately. Added after the first edition of this page; updated in the second addendum of this page.

Updated after the repair of the tameness hypothesis: first proved with “the base retraction of every strong bundle chart compatible with the atlas is tame” (`htame`), which no strong bundle over a nonempty base satisfies (V3.104), so that form was vacuous; now with the hypotheses of V3.103 (Findings, Chapter 3, items 190–192).

items.title: Corollary 3.1.27 (preprint 3.24): the solution set when every zero is in good position

book.label: §3.1, Corollary 3.1.27 (preprint 3.24), p. 104 (preprint p. 78)
book.statement: If at every zero $x$ of the sc-Fredholm section $f$ of a tame strong bundle $f'(x)$ is surjective with kernel in good position to $C_xX$, then the solution set $S = \{f = 0\}$ is a sub-M-polyfold whose induced structure is tame and that of a smooth manifold with boundary with corners.

lean.statement: Let $f$ be an sc-Fredholm section with $(f, x)$ in good position in a tame chart (V3.103) at every zero $x$, and $S = \{f = 0\} \ne \emptyset$. Then $S$ is a sub-M-polyfold of $X$ whose induced structure is tame and equivalent to a manifold with boundary with corners of locally constant dimension (`IsManifoldWithCornersLoc`, V3.72). The same with good position in the text's sense (sc-complement, V3.47) at every zero, which for an sc-Fredholm section with tame germ data is the same hypothesis (`corollary_3_24_sc`).

diff: **No hypothesis is added** (Findings, Chapter 3, items 156, 157): the global hypothesis, good position at every zero, supplies at every point the nearby good position that the local theorems need. “Tame strong bundle” is read as Definitions 3.6.3, 3.6.6 (preprint 3.50, 3.53) read it, good position in a tame chart (V3.103); $S \ne \emptyset$ is needed by the formal charts (for $S = \emptyset$ the statement is empty). The text names no dimension; the formal one is locally constant (V3.87). Added after the first edition of this page.

Updated after the repair of the tameness hypothesis: first proved with “the base retraction of every strong bundle chart compatible with the atlas is tame” (`htame`), which no strong bundle over a nonempty base satisfies (V3.104), so that form was vacuous; now with the hypotheses of V3.103 (Findings, Chapter 3, items 190–192).

Corollary 3.1.27 (preprint 3.24) with the text's notion of good position is `corollary_3_24_sc`; for an sc-Fredholm section with tame germ data that hypothesis is equivalent to the project's (`forall_isGoodPositionGermSc_iff`; Findings, Chapter 3, item 213). Updated in the third addendum of this page.

items.title: Tameness is carried by sc-diffeomorphisms and by open subsets

book.label: §3.2, proof of Proposition 3.2.2 (preprint 3.26), p. 105 (preprint p. 80); §3.6, proof of Theorem 3.6.8 (preprint 3.54), preprint p. 114
book.statement: Used without statement: in the proof of Proposition 3.2.2 (preprint 3.26), “$X' = \psi(X)$ is tame”; in the proof of Theorem 3.6.8 (preprint 3.54), the chart $\psi \circ \varphi$ onto $\psi(O)$ is a chart of the tame M-polyfold $X$.

lean.statement: For an sc-diffeomorphism $\psi : U \to U'$ between relatively open subsets of partial quadrants and a tame retraction $r : U \to U$ onto $O$, $\psi \circ r \circ \psi^{-1}$ is a tame retraction of $U'$ onto $\psi(O)$, so $(\psi(O), C', E')$ is a tame retract; on the way $d_{C'} \circ \psi = d_C$, $Dr'(\psi(x)) = D\psi(x)Dr(x)D\psi^{-1}(\psi(x))$, and sc-isomorphisms carry sc-subspaces and sc-splittings. The restriction of a tame retraction to an open subset is tame; an open subset of a tame retract, and the model of a chart restricted to an open set, are tame retracts.

diff: Condition (1) of Definition 2.5.2 (preprint 2.34) is Theorem 1.3.5 (preprint 1.25); condition (2) is transported at the smooth points, where $D\psi(x)$ is an sc-isomorphism, using $D\psi(x)E_x \subseteq E'_{\psi(x)}$ (the one-sided sign argument) (Findings, Chapter 3, items 95, 151). Added after the first edition of this page.

items.title: Theorem 3.2.3 (preprint 3.27) with locally constant dimension

book.label: §3.2, Theorem 3.2.3 (preprint 3.27), p. 106 (preprint p. 81)
book.statement: Theorem 3.2.3 (preprint 3.27) for a fixed dimension $n$: a subset with the $n$-dimensional tangent germ property is a sub-M-polyfold whose induced structure is tame and equivalent to an $n$-dimensional manifold with boundary with corners, with the charts $\pi \circ \varphi$.

lean.statement: If $M \ne \emptyset$ has at every point regular data of Definition 3.2.1 (preprint 3.25) (`IsRegular`, V3.24) of some dimension, which may depend on the point, then $M$ is a sub-M-polyfold, its induced structure is tame, and the charts $\pi\varphi$ of all these data form an equivalent atlas of charts on relatively open subsets of partial quadrants of finite-dimensional spaces (`IsManifoldWithCornersLoc`); each of them is a chart of the induced structure containing its point.

diff: The regularity conditions of V3.24 are hypotheses, as there. The dimension may vary from point to point (the solution set of Theorem 3.6.11 (preprint 3.57) has locally constant, not constant, dimension; Findings, Chapter 3, item 152); the proof is that of V3.24. Added after the first edition of this page.

items.title: The re-centring lemma

book.label: §3.2, proof of Theorem 3.2.3 (preprint 3.27), preprint p. 84
book.statement: In the proof of Theorem 3.2.3 (preprint 3.27): $\delta$ is an sc$^\infty$-germ near every $v_0 \in V$. With the data $(\psi, N', Y', V', \tau)$ at $x_0 = \varphi^{-1}(v_0 + \delta(v_0))$, the map $w \mapsto \pi\varphi\psi^{-1}(w + \tau(w))$ has an invertible linearization at $0$, so it is a local diffeomorphism and $\delta$ is regular near $v_0$.

lean.statement: For two graph descriptions of one set $S$ — in a chart $\chi_1$ the graph of $\sigma_1 : V_1 \to Y_1$ over $K_1$ with $\sigma_1$ of class $C^1$ on all of $V_1$, in a chart $\chi_2$ centred at $y = \chi_1^{-1}(v_0 + \sigma_1(v_0))$ the graph of $\sigma_2$ over $K_2$ with $\sigma_2(0) = 0$, $D\sigma_2(0) = 0$ and $C^k$-lifts into level $k$ near $0$ ($K_i$ finite-dimensional, smooth, in good position, $Y_i$ closed complements) — $\dim K_1 = \dim K_2$, and for all $m$, $k$, $\sigma_1$ is $C^k$ into $E_{1,m}$ on a relatively open neighbourhood of $v_0$.

chips: onto by Sard, not by symmetry
diff: The text's step needs $\delta$ differentiable at $v_0$, which fails for general sets (V3.24, first counterexample); here $\sigma_1$ is $C^1$ on $V_1$, which V3.74 arranges by shrinking (Findings, Chapter 3, items 82, 150).

The linearization of $\beta = \pi_1 \circ \chi_1\chi_2^{-1} \circ (1 + \sigma_2)$ at $0$ is injective by the chain rule for the transition and its inverse on level $1$ and the tangency of the graph to the retract; its surjectivity comes from the dimension count by Sard's lemma in fixed dimension, since the symmetric argument would need $\sigma_1$ differentiable into level $1$ at $v_0$ (item 159). The inverse $\beta^{-1}$ is $C^k$ by Lemma 3.8.21 (preprint 3.77) with weak hypotheses (V3.90), not by Theorem 3.8.15 (preprint 3.72), which would need $d_C(x) = d_C(\beta(x))$. Added after the first edition of this page.

items.title: Condition (a) of the regularity conditions by re-centring

book.label: §3.2, proof of Theorem 3.2.3 (preprint 3.27), preprint p. 84; §3.6, proof of Theorem 3.6.8 (preprint 3.54), preprint p. 115
book.statement: The proof of Theorem 3.2.3 (preprint 3.27) shows that $\delta$ is an sc$^\infty$-germ near every point of $V$ (so that the charts $\pi\varphi$ are compatible); the proof of Theorem 3.6.8 (preprint 3.54) constructs the data at every zero “proceeding as above”.

lean.statement: Let $D$ be data of Definition 3.2.1 (preprint 3.25) of dimension $n$ for $M$ at $x$ with $\pi(O) \subseteq C$ (condition (b)), and let every point of $M$ in an open $U \ni x$ have data of Definition 3.2.1 (preprint 3.25) of some dimension. Then $M$ has at $x$ regular data (`IsRegular`) of dimension $n$ with chart domain in $U$, and every datum of Definition 3.2.1 (preprint 3.25) at a point of $M$ in that domain has dimension $n$. (The proof shrinks $D$ — same $N$, $Y$, $\delta$ — and applies V3.73 at every point.)

diff: Condition (b), $\pi(O) \subseteq C$, is a hypothesis. Read off the statement (not a separate Lean theorem): every point of a set with the tangent germ property has data, so for such a set data satisfying (b) can be shrunk to regular data; condition (a) of V3.24 is then not an independent hypothesis. For the solution set (b) holds by the choice of the good complement (V3.75, V3.77; Findings, Chapter 3, items 151, 152). Added after the first edition of this page.

items.title: Good complements whose projection maps the partial quadrant into itself

book.label: §3.2, proof of Theorem 3.2.3 (preprint 3.27), preprint p. 83
book.statement: In the proof of Theorem 3.2.3 (preprint 3.27) the set $\Sigma = \{v + y \in C \mid v \in V, y \in Y\}$ is asserted to be relatively open in $C$; the retraction $t(v + w) = v + \delta(v)$ is defined on it.

lean.statement: If the finite-dimensional $N$ is in good position to the partial quadrant $C$ of $E$, there is a continuous projection $\pi : E_0 \to N$ with $\pi(C) \subseteq N \cap C$ whose kernel $Y$ is a good complement of $N$; $Y$ is closed and `ProjectsInto C N Y` ($z \in C$, $k \in N$, $z - k \in Y$ imply $k \in C$). The property is carried by continuous linear isomorphisms respecting the cones.

chips: a case the obvious choice misses
diff: The text's claim fails for an arbitrary good complement (V3.24, second counterexample) and holds when $\pi(O) \subseteq C$; for the solution set the complement is chosen so (V3.77). The construction keeps the coordinates of a set $S$ of indices; when no coordinate vanishes at a nonzero point of $N \cap C$ and $N \cap C \ne N$ one coordinate is kept: for $C = [0, \infty)^2$, $N = \mathbb R(1, 1)$ the projection along the good complement $\mathbb R(1, 2)$ maps $(0, 1)$ to $-(1, 1)$ (Findings, Chapter 3, items 130, 131). Added after the first edition of this page.

items.title: Corollary 3.4.3 (preprint 3.39): composition with a given conjugation

book.label: §3.4, Corollary 3.4.3 (preprint 3.39), p. 116 (preprint p. 93)
book.statement: If the sc-germ $g$ is equivalent by a strong bundle isomorphism $\Phi$ to a basic germ and $s$ is an sc$^+$-germ, there is a strong bundle map $\Psi$ such that $((\Psi \circ \Phi)_*(g + s))^1$ is a basic germ.

lean.statement: Let $g : U \to F$ be sc-smooth and conjugated to a basic germ $h$ (conjugation data $\Phi$, V3.13, V3.46), and $s : U \to F_1$ sc-smooth into $F^1$ with $s(0) = 0$. chips: index raise of an iso: proved

items.title: The linearization at a zero in charts, and its chart independence

book.label: §3.6, Definition 3.6.6 (preprint 3.53), p. 136 (preprint p. 111); §2.5 (preprint §2.4), Definition 2.5.8 (preprint 2.38), p. 57 (preprint p. 42)
book.statement: Definition 3.6.6 (preprint 3.53) is stated with $f'(x) : T_xX \to Y_x$ and the partial cone $C_xX$; Definition 2.5.8 (preprint 2.38) asserts that $T^R_xX$ and $C_xX$ do not depend on the chart (Proposition 2.4.10 (preprint 2.30)). The linearization is defined at the centre of a chart, through a filler.

lean.statement: In a strong bundle chart, $\mathrm{Lin}(z) = D(\mathbf f \circ r)(z)|_{T_zO}$ at every level-$1$ point $z$ of the retract; at a zero it takes values in $K_z = \rho(z)F$ and equals $Dg(z)$ on $T_zO$ for every $g$ sc$^1$ on $U$ agreeing with $\mathbf f$ near $z$, and for every sc$^1$-germ $g$ agreeing with $\mathbf f$ near $z$ with $z$ in its germ, $Dg(z)$ the value of its derivative family (`linAt_eq_germDeriv`; at a centre: $Tf(0)$ of Proposition 3.1.5 (preprint 3.5), also for a filling germ). For two strong bundle charts of $P$ and an sc-smooth section, at a zero $y$ with level-$1$ points $z$, $z'$ over $\varphi(y)$, $\varphi'(y)$: isomorphisms $A : T_zO \to T_{z'}O'$, $\Gamma : K_z \to K'_{z'}$ with $\Gamma\,\mathrm{Lin}(z) = \mathrm{Lin}'(z')A$ and $A$ respecting the partial quadrants; so surjectivity, the Fredholm property and index, and the good position of the kernel do not depend on the chart.

diff: The text does not prove the chart independence of $f'(x)$ or of good position; this is its chart form at zeros (what gap G.13 of Chapter 2 leaves open). Only the fibre derivative of the transition survives at a zero, so away from zeros the linearization is not chart independent. Of Definition 2.6.4 (preprint 2.50) only the sc-smoothness of the transition on $[0]$ is used; level-$1$ points suffice; no tameness (Findings, Chapter 3, items 110–116). Added after the first edition of this page.

For filling germs (the germ reading of Definition 3.1.11 (preprint 3.11)) $Dg(z)$ is meaningful only for $z$ in the germ; the consumers use it at the centre and at the level-$1$ lifts of nearby zeros, which lie in the germ (Findings, Chapter 3, items 278, 284). Updated after the switch of Definition 3.1.11 (preprint 3.11) to the text’s germ reading (phase 2).

items.title: Definition 3.6.6 (preprint 3.53) at a zero, from a chart not centred there

items.title: Theorem 3.6.8 (1) (preprint 3.54) under the filler condition at the nearby zeros (first form)

items.title: The parameter extension of the proof of Proposition 6.2.2 (preprint 6.2): obstruction and tilted kernel

book.label: no counterpart in Chapter 3 (the perturbation argument of Proposition 6.2.2 (preprint 6.2))
book.statement: Not in Chapter 3. The proof of Proposition 6.2.2 (preprint 6.2) (index stability) extends the section by finitely many parameters, $F(\lambda, u) = g(u) + \sum\lambda_is_i(u)$, and applies the implicit function theorem to the extended problem.

lean.statement: (a) For a cone $C \ni 0$ closed under nonnegative scaling, the $V$-components of a good complement of $\mathbb R \times N$ with respect to $\mathbb R \times C$ lie in $C \cap (-C)$, so $\mathbb R \times N$ is in good position only if $N + (C \cap -C) = V$. items.title: Theorem 3.6.10 (preprint 3.56): the global implicit function theorem, $\partial X = \emptyset$

items.title: Theorem 3.7.1 (preprint 3.58), given the family of sc-isomorphisms

book.label: §3.7, proof of Theorem 3.7.1 (preprint 3.58), pp. 142–145 (preprint pp. 118–120)
book.statement: Second half of the proof of Theorem 3.7.1 (preprint 3.58): with $L(b) = P_Y \circ Df(b)|_X$ sc-isomorphisms with uniform lower bounds (Lemmas 3.7.2–3.7.4 (preprint 3.59–3.61)), the strong bundle isomorphism $\Phi((b, x), (c, y)) = ((b, x), (c, L(b)^{-1}y))$ makes $\Phi_*(f - f(0))$ a basic germ, the contraction estimate coming from condition (3).

lean.statement: In coordinates $E = \mathbb R^n \oplus X$, $C = \widetilde C \oplus X$, $F = \mathbb R^N \oplus Y$: for $f$ sc-smooth on $U$, an open $V_o \ni 0$ with $(b, 0) \in U$ for $b \in V_o \cap \widetilde C$, sc-isomorphisms $L(b)$ with $L(b)h = (Df(b, 0)(0, h))_Y$ and lower bounds $c_m$ on $V_o \cap \widetilde C$, and condition (3) (`DerivCondition`): on $U' = U \cap (V_o \oplus X)$ the push-forward $k = \Phi_*(f - f(0))$ is a basic germ with contraction $H(b, x) = x - L(b)^{-1}(f(b, x) - f(0))_Y$, $\Phi$ is a strong bundle isomorphism covering the identity, and $f - f(0)$ is conjugated to a basic germ.

chips: in the coordinates of the proof
diff: In the coordinates of the text's proof. The contraction estimate uses the mean value inequality along a segment with the derivative bound in the weaker norm of $X_m$ (the text's integral formula), first for $x, x' \in X_{m+1}$, then by density; the sc-smoothness of $(b, y) \mapsto L(b)^{-1}y$ is Lemma 3.7.4 (preprint 3.61) in set form (Findings, Chapter 3, item 73). Added after the first edition of this page.

items.title: Theorem 3.7.1 (preprint 3.58): the basic germ criterion

book.label: §3.7, Theorem 3.7.1 (preprint 3.58), p. 140 (preprint p. 116) (proof pp. 140–145 (preprint pp. 116–120))
book.statement: Under (1) $Df(x)$ sc-Fredholm of constant index at smooth points, (2) a splitting $E = B \oplus X$ with $B \supseteq \ker Df(0)$, $Y = Df(0)X$ and a compactness condition, (3) a uniform estimate on $D_2f$: $f - f(0)$ is conjugated near $0$ to a basic germ.

lean.statement: In coordinates $E = \mathbb R^n \oplus X$, $C = \widetilde C \oplus X$, $F = \mathbb R^N \oplus Y$: let $f$ be sc-smooth on $U$ with (1) $Df(b, 0)$ sc-Fredholm with the sc-index of $Df(0)$ at every $(b, 0) \in U$, $b \in \widetilde C$; (2) $h \mapsto (Df(0)(0, h))_Y$ bijective on level $0$ and `CompactnessCondition`; (3) `DerivCondition`. Then there are an open $V_o \ni 0$ and sc-isomorphisms $L(b) = P_Y Df(b, 0)|_X$ for $b \in V_o \cap \widetilde C$ with the conclusions of V3.88: $f - f(0)$ is conjugated to a basic germ.

chips: in the coordinates of the proof
diff: Proved in the coordinates of the text's proof; the reduction of a general sc-splitting $E = B \oplus X$, $F = A \oplus Y$ to them is not formalized. Condition (1) is used only at the points $(b, 0)$ (weaker than the text's); “$B \supseteq \ker Df(0)$, $Y = Df(0)X$” is replaced by the bijectivity it implies; the smallness of $b$ in the compactness condition is read as uniform in the level. The text's “injective sc-Fredholm of index $0$, hence an sc-isomorphism” is the block index formula $\mathrm{ind}\,T = \dim\mathbb R^n + \mathrm{ind}\,L - \dim\mathbb R^N$ on every level; Lemmas 3.7.2, 3.7.3 (preprint 3.59, 3.60) are applied with their hypotheses derived from (2) (Findings, Chapter 3, item 73). Added after the first edition of this page.

items.title: Proposition 3.8.17 (preprint 3.73) and Lemma 3.8.21 (preprint 3.77) with the hypotheses their proofs use

book.label: §3.8.5 (preprint §3.8.4), Proposition 3.8.17 (preprint 3.73) and Lemma 3.8.21 (preprint 3.77), preprint pp. 137, 140
book.statement: For $U$ relatively open and convex in a partial quadrant $C \subseteq \mathbb R^n$, $f : U \to C$ smooth with $\|Df - 1\| \le \tfrac12$, $f(0) = 0$ and $d_C(x) = d_C(f(x))$: $f(U)$ is relatively open and $f : U \to f(U)$ is a smooth diffeomorphism (Lemma 3.8.21 (preprint 3.77): the inverse is differentiable with $Dg = [Df \circ g]^{-1}$).

lean.statement: For $U$ convex in a finite-dimensional $V$ with unique differentiability, $f$ of class $C^j$ ($j \ge 1$) on $U$ with $\|Df(x) - 1\| \le \tfrac12$, and $f(U)$ with unique differentiability: $f$ is injective on $U$, its inverse is differentiable within $f(U)$ with $Dg(y) = [Df(g(y))]^{-1}$, and of class $C^j$ on $f(U)$.

diff: The partial quadrant is not used; the condition on the degeneracy index (in V3.59: interior points to interior points) is replaced by the unique differentiability of $f(U)$, which is what the bootstrapping uses; the relative openness of $f(U)$ is not concluded. Needed for the re-centring (V3.73), where $f(U)$ is relatively open in a cone for another reason (Findings, Chapter 3, item 158). Added after the first edition of this page.

items.title: Theorem 3.1.21 (preprint 3.18): parametrized perturbations

book.label: §3.1, Theorem 3.1.21 (preprint 3.18), p. 100 (preprint p. 74)
book.statement: Let $P : Y \to X$ be a tame strong bundle and $f$ an sc-Fredholm section. If $s_1, \dots, s_n \in \Gamma^+(P)$, then $(r, x) \mapsto f(x) + \sum_i r_is_i(x)$ defines an sc-Fredholm section of the pull-back bundle $\pi^*(P) : \pi^*Y \to \mathbb R^n \times X$.

lean.statement: For any strong bundle $P : Y \to X$, an sc-Fredholm section $f$ and sc$^+$-sections $s_1, \dots, s_n$: with $\mathbb R^n$ the M-polyfold with the constant sc-structure and the translation charts, $\pi(r, x) = x$, and $\pi^*P$ the pull-back strong bundle with the natural structure of Proposition 2.6.8 (preprint 2.54), $F(r, x) = f(x) + \sum_i r_is_i(x)$ (computed in $P^{-1}(x)$) is an sc-Fredholm section of $\pi^*P$. The paracompactness of $\mathbb R^n \times X$ and $\pi^*Y$ is supplied by Theorem 2.3.10 (preprint 2.16) (`theorem_3_18'`). On the way: $\tilde f = f \circ \pi$ is sc-Fredholm (product chart, the $\mathbb R^n$-extension of the basic germ), $\tilde s$ is sc$^+$ (scalar product rule), $F = \tilde f + \tilde s$, Theorem 3.1.18 (preprint 3.15); $\mathbb R^n \times X$ is tame when $X$ is.

diff: Tameness is not used, as for Theorem 3.1.18 (preprint 3.15); $\pi^*P$ is tame when $P$ is. The text's “readily verified” needs objects it does not construct: $\mathbb R^n$ as an M-polyfold with charts centred at every $r_0$, the product chart pulled back to $\pi^*Y$, the filler conditions for $(a, u) \mapsto g(u)$, and the $\mathbb R^n$-extension of the basic germ; that $\tilde s$ is sc$^+$ needs the product rule with a scalar factor, which Chapter 1 does not state (Findings, Chapter 3, items 160–164, 167). Added in the second addendum of this page.

items.title: The linearization of the parametrized section

book.label: §3.1, after Theorem 3.1.22 (preprint 3.19), p. 101 (preprint p. 75)
book.statement: The linearization of $\tilde f(r, x) = f(x) + \sum_i r_is_i(x)$ at $(0, x_0)$ is $(h, u) \mapsto f'(x_0)u + \sum_i h_ie_i$, $e_i = s_i(x_0)$.

lean.statement: In the product chart $(r \mapsto r - r_0) \times c$ of $\pi^*P$, $c$ a strong bundle chart of $P$ with $0$ in its retract, at the centre: $D(\hat F \circ (1 \times r))(0)(\delta a, \delta u) = D(\hat G \circ r)(0)\delta u + \sum_i\delta a_i\hat s_i(0)$, $\hat G = \hat f + \sum_i r_{0,i}\hat s_i$; in the chart form of the linearization, $\mathrm{Lin}_F(0)(\delta a, \delta u) = \mathrm{Lin}_{f + \sum r_{0,i}s_i}(0)\delta u + \sum_i\delta a_i\hat s_i(0)$, and at $r_0 = 0$, $\mathrm{Lin}_F(0)(\delta r, \xi) = \mathrm{Lin}_f(0)\xi + \sum_i\delta r_i\hat s_i(0)$.

diff: Stated in the chart form of the linearization (Definition 3.6.6 (preprint 3.53) is formalized in charts). At $(r_0, x)$ with $r_0 \ne 0$ the first term is the linearization of $f + \sum r_{0,i}s_i$, not $f'(x)$; the formula does not use $F(r_0, x) = 0$. The text's “sc$^1$-sections $s_i$” must be sc$^+$ for Theorem 3.1.21 (preprint 3.18) (Findings, Chapter 3, items 165, 166). Added in the second addendum of this page.

items.title: Theorem 3.6.8 (1) (preprint 3.54): the surjectivity at the nearby zeros, in the chart at $x_0$

book.label: §3.6, proof of Theorem 3.6.8 (preprint 3.54), property (4), preprint p. 114
book.statement: For every zero $y$ near $x$ the linearization $f'(y)$ is surjective; “property (4) follows from Corollary 3.41 and from Lemma 3.55”.

lean.statement: In the data of V3.48 at a zero $x_0$ in good position (chart centred at $x_0$, filling germ $g$, conjugation $\Psi$ covering $\psi$, $h' + \iota t$ with kernel $K \ne 0$, the graph $\sigma$ over $V'$, an open $N_2 \ni 0$ on which $\psi$ maps the zeros of $g$ in $O$ onto the graph), with condition (2) of Definition 3.1.4 (preprint 3.4) on $N_2$: there is an open $N_4 \subseteq N_2$ containing $0$ such that for every zero $z_0 \in O \cap N_4$ of $g$ and every smooth $k$, $\rho(z_0)k = Dg(z_0)x$ for some $x \in T_{z_0}O$. The curve $u(\mu)$ of zeros of $g + \mu\rho(r(\cdot))k$ through $z_0$ lies in $O$ (condition (2)) and in the germ of $g$; it comes from Theorem 3.3.3 (preprint 3.30) at the centre for the $k$-extended contraction germ of the normal form of Theorem 3.4.2 (preprint 3.38), whose regions in $a$ do not depend on $k$, and from a one-sided finite-dimensional implicit function theorem at $\theta(z_0)$ along an inward direction given by good position.

diff: Not the text's argument, which gives the surjectivity of the filled $Dg(z_0)$ only (V3.82). The perturbation argument of the text's Proposition 6.2.2 (preprint 6.2) applies the implicit function theorem at $x_0$ to a problem depending on the perturbation, with a neighbourhood depending on it (V3.83); here the finite-dimensional implicit function theorem is applied at the nearby zero, and Theorem 3.3.3 (preprint 3.30) at the centre to a germ whose $a$-regions are $k$-independent, so $N_4$ is determined by $g$, $r$, $\rho$, $\Psi$ and the normal form. The surjectivity of $D_aH$ at the nearby zero comes from a dimension count on level $0$, not from eliminating the $W$-block; Corollary 3.4.3 (preprint 3.39) is not used (Findings, Chapter 3, items 180–187). Added in the second addendum of this page.

In the germ reading the curve lies in the germ of the filling: its points come from the germ of the basic germ taken on the points that $\psi^{-1}$ maps into the germs of $g$ and $s$, so $g$ is differentiated within its germ (Findings, Chapter 3, items 276–278, 298). Updated after the switch of Definition 3.1.11 (preprint 3.11) to the text’s germ reading (phase 2).

items.title: Theorem 3.6.8 (1)–(2) (preprint 3.54) with the text's hypotheses

book.label: §3.6, Theorem 3.6.8 (1), (2) (preprint 3.54), p. 136 (preprint p. 111)
book.statement: Let $f$ be an sc-Fredholm section of a tame strong bundle, $f(x) = 0$, $(f, x)$ in good position. There is an open $V \ni x$ such that $S = \{y \in V \mid f(y) = 0\}$ satisfies: (1) $(f, y)$ is in good position at every $y \in S$; (2) $S$ is a sub-M-polyfold whose induced structure is equivalent to a smooth manifold with boundary with corners.

lean.statement: For an sc-Fredholm section with tame germ data (V3.103), $f(x_0) = 0$, $(f, x_0)$ in good position in a tame chart: an open $V_x \ni x_0$ such that $(f, y)$ is in good position in a tame chart at every zero $y \in V_x$ (`theorem_3_54_one'`), and $d$ with regular data of Definition 3.2.1 (preprint 3.25) of dimension $d$ for $S$ at $x_0$ with chart domain in $V_x$, every datum at a point of $S$ in that domain having dimension $d$ (`theorem_3_54'`). With the text's notion of good position (sc-complement, V3.47) in the conclusion, from either form at $x_0$: every zero $y \in V_x$ is in good position with an sc-complement (`theorem_3_54_one_sc_of_tame`, `theorem_3_54_one_sc`; with (2), `theorem_3_54_sc`).

diff: **No hypothesis is added.** (2) is stated as regular tangent germ data with locally constant dimension, from which Theorem 3.2.3 (preprint 3.27) gives the manifold structure of the local solution set (V3.95). The surjectivity in (1) is V3.93, carried to the chart centred at $y$ through V3.79 and read in the tame chart of the germ data at $y$ (V3.107); the kernel half is V3.81; for $\dim K = 0$ the only zero near $x_0$ is $x_0$. The text's statement is true, its proof incomplete; the same holds for the book's arXiv version (Findings, Chapter 3, items 157, 180, 189). Added in the second addendum of this page.

Updated after the repair of the tameness hypothesis: first proved with “the base retraction of every strong bundle chart compatible with the atlas is tame” (`htame`), which no strong bundle over a nonempty base satisfies (V3.104), so that form was vacuous; now with the hypotheses of V3.103 (Findings, Chapter 3, items 190–192).

The project's good position asks only for an algebraic good complement (V3.20), which as a conclusion is less than the text's; the sc form of (1) follows at each zero by the upgrade of V3.47, with no hypothesis added (Findings, Chapter 3, items 210, 213). The case distinction $d_X(x) \ge 1$ of Definition 3.6.6 (2) (preprint 3.53) is not made, which makes hypothesis and conclusion stronger (item 214). Updated in the third addendum of this page.

items.title: Theorems 3.1.26 and 3.1.22 (preprint 3.23 and 3.19) with the text's hypotheses

book.label: §3.1, Theorems 3.1.22, 3.1.26 (preprint 3.19, 3.23), preprint pp. 74, 77
book.statement: (3.23) For an sc-Fredholm section of a tame strong bundle and a zero $x$ with $f'(x)$ onto and kernel in good position to $C_xX$, there is an open $U \ni x$ such that $S(f, U)$ consists of smooth points and is a tame sub-M-polyfold with a uniquely determined structure of a manifold with boundary with corners. (3.19) For $d_X \equiv 0$ and $f'(x_0)$ onto, $S(f, U)$ is a smooth manifold.

lean.statement: For an sc-Fredholm section with tame germ data (V3.103), $f(x) = 0$, $(f, x)$ in good position in a tame chart: an open $U \ni x$ and $d$ such that every zero in $U$ is in good position in a tame chart and a smooth point, and $S(f, U)$ is a sub-M-polyfold with tame induced structure equivalent to a $d$-dimensional manifold with boundary with corners (`theorem_3_23'`); if $d_X \equiv 0$, with degeneracy index $0$ everywhere (`theorem_3_19'`). Theorem 3.1.26 (preprint 3.23) with the text's notion of good position (sc-complement, V3.47) at $x$ and, in the conclusion, at every zero in $U$: `theorem_3_23_sc`.

diff: No hypothesis is added; “tame strong bundle” is read as Definitions 3.6.3, 3.6.4, 3.6.6 (preprint 3.50, 3.51, 3.53) read it, germ data and good position in tame charts (V3.103). For Theorem 3.1.22 (preprint 3.19) “$f'(x_0)$ surjective” is read as good position, the same at $d_X = 0$ (V3.100, V3.101). The dimension as the Fredholm index is V3.97, $\ker f'(y) = T_yS$ in the chart V3.99; “uniquely determined” is the equivalence of atlases. Added in the second addendum of this page.

Updated after the repair of the tameness hypothesis: first proved with “the base retraction of every strong bundle chart compatible with the atlas is tame” (`htame`), which no strong bundle over a nonempty base satisfies (V3.104), so that form was vacuous; now with the hypotheses of V3.103 (Findings, Chapter 3, items 190–192).

The form of Theorem 3.1.26 (preprint 3.23) with the text's good complement in hypothesis and conclusion is `theorem_3_23_sc` (Findings, Chapter 3, item 213). Updated in the third addendum of this page.

items.title: The index of the linearization at a zero, in every chart

book.label: §3.6, Proposition 3.6.5 (preprint 3.52), p. 135 (preprint p. 110); Theorem 3.1.22 (preprint 3.19), p. 100 (preprint p. 74)
book.statement: If $f$ is an sc-Fredholm section and $f(x) = 0$, then $Tf(x) : T_xX \to Y_x$ is an sc-Fredholm operator (Proposition 3.6.5 (preprint 3.52)); “the linearization $f'(x_0)$ is a sc-Fredholm operator” (Theorem 3.1.22 (preprint 3.19)).

lean.statement: `IsSurjLinOfIndex f y d`: in every strong bundle chart around $y$, at the level-$1$ point over $\varphi(y)$, $\mathrm{Lin}(z) : T_zO \to K_z$ is onto, Fredholm, $\mathrm{ind} = \dim\ker = d$. For an sc-smooth section and the chart of Definition 3.1.11 (preprint 3.11) at a zero $x_0$ with conjugation data of $g - s$ to a basic germ $O(\widetilde C \oplus W, 0) \to \mathbb R^N \oplus W$, $\widetilde C \subseteq \mathbb R^n$: in every chart around $x_0$ the linearization is Fredholm of index $n - N$, onto if the germ is in good position; so `IsSurjLinOfIndex f x_0 (n − N)` at a zero in good position. For an sc-Fredholm section in good position, in the chart of Definition 3.6.6 (preprint 3.53): $\mathrm{ind}\,Dg(0) = \mathrm{ind}\,Tf(x_0) = \dim\ker Tf(x_0) = n - N$ for every conjugation. In sc form: for an sc-Fredholm section, a zero $y$ and **any** strong bundle chart around $y$, at the level-$1$ point $z$ over $\varphi(y)$ (a smooth point), $T_zO = Dr(z)E$ and $K_z = \rho(z)F$ are sc-subspaces and $\mathrm{Lin}(z) : T_zO \to K_z$ is an sc-Fredholm operator, Fredholm on every level of the index $n - N$ of every conjugation of every germ datum at $y$; under `IsSurjLinOfIndex f y d` it is onto on every level, of index $d$ on every level. In the chart of Definition 3.6.6 (preprint 3.53) at a zero in good position, $Dg(0)$ and $f'(x_0) = Tf(x_0)$ are sc-Fredholm and $Tf(x_0)$ is onto on every level.

chips: sc-Fredholm on every level, in charts
diff: Proved in sc form, in every chart: the level-$0$ conjugation between the linearizations in two charts (V3.78) is realised by bounded operators on the ambient spaces that preserve the levels at smooth points (derivatives of the sc-smooth transition maps, and the fibre part of the strong bundle transition, sc$^0$ on $Y[0]$), so the regularity of the linearization in the chart of the germ (V3.46) passes to every chart; then the criterion of V1.8. Tameness is not used. $T_xX$ itself carries no linear structure here (G.7), so the operator is read in charts. The passage to every chart is the chart independence at zeros, which the text does not state (Findings, Chapter 3, items 170, 236, 239). Added in the second addendum of this page with the level-$0$ Fredholm property only (G.22); updated in the third addendum.

**Germs.** The hypothesis is the text’s since the switch to the germ reading (phase 2): the germ data of the sc-Fredholm section are germs whose levels may shrink with $m$ (V3.13, V3.16), and Proposition 3.6.5 (preprint 3.52) enters at the centre of the chart of the germ datum, where $\mathrm{Lin}(0) = Dg(0)$ on $T_0O$ for the filling germ (Findings, Chapter 3, items 284, 310, 314, 330). `theorem_3_19_linearization_sc` gives the conclusions in the chart at $x_0$, and `linAt_isScFredholm_of_isSurjLinOfIndex` with `IsGoodPositionGerm.exists_isSurjLinOfIndex` in every chart. Hence “stronger” (formerly “narrower”, for the hypothesis): the index on every level, and the surjectivity on every level at a zero in good position, in every chart, go beyond the text’s statement.

items.title: The dimension of the solution set is the Fredholm index

book.label: §3.1, Theorem 3.1.22 (preprint 3.19), p. 100 (preprint p. 74); §3.6, proof of Theorem 3.6.8 (preprint 3.54), preprint p. 115
book.statement: The solution set $S(f, U)$ has the structure of a smooth manifold “whose dimension agrees with the Fredholm index” (Theorem 3.1.22 (preprint 3.19)); with $d = \dim\ker f'(x)$ the solution set has the $d$-dimensional tangent germ property (proof of Theorem 3.6.8 (preprint 3.54)).

lean.statement: For an sc-smooth section and a zero $x_0$ in good position in a tame chart (V3.103): the data of Definition 3.2.1 (preprint 3.25) at $x_0$ have a dimension $d$ with `IsSurjLinOfIndex f x_0 d`, also the regular data of Theorem 3.6.8 (2) (preprint 3.54). For an sc-Fredholm section with tame germ data: an open $U \ni x_0$ and $d$ with every zero $y \in U$ in good position in a tame chart, `IsSurjLinOfIndex f y d`, and $S(f, U)$ a tame $d$-dimensional manifold with boundary with corners (`theorem_3_23_index`; without boundary if $d_X \equiv 0$, `theorem_3_19_index`); under the hypotheses of Theorem 3.6.11 (preprint 3.57), regular data at every zero whose dimension is the index at the zeros of their chart domain (`theorem_3_57_index`). For an sc-Fredholm section, at a zero $y$ with `IsSurjLinOfIndex f y d`, in every chart $\mathrm{Lin}(z)$ is moreover sc-Fredholm and onto on every level, of index $d$ on every level.

chips: at every zero, in every chart
diff: $d = \dim\ker D(h + t)(0) = n - N$ for the conjugation from which the chart of the tangent germ data is built, and $n - N$ is the index of $f'(x_0)$ for the same conjugation (Proposition 3.6.5 (preprint 3.52)); the proofs of Theorem 3.6.8 (preprint 3.54) had to expose that conjugation (`_conj` forms). The index is stated at every zero near the point and in every chart; the text states no dimension in Theorems 3.1.26 and 3.6.11 (preprint 3.23 and 3.57) (Findings, Chapter 3, item 170). Added in the second addendum of this page.

Updated after the repair of the tameness hypothesis: first proved with “the base retraction of every strong bundle chart compatible with the atlas is tame” (`htame`), which no strong bundle over a nonempty base satisfies (V3.104), so that form was vacuous; now with the hypotheses of V3.103 (Findings, Chapter 3, items 190–192).
That $d$ is the index on every level of $f'(y)$ as an sc-Fredholm operator, in every chart, is V3.96 (Findings, Chapter 3, item 239). Updated in the third addendum of this page.

items.title: The Fredholm index along the solution set and along paths (Definition 6.2.1 (preprint 6.1), Proposition 6.2.2 (preprint 6.2))

book.label: Definition 6.2.1 (preprint 6.1), pp. 237–240 (preprint pp. 200–201); Proposition 6.2.2 (preprint 6.2), p. 240 (preprint p. 201)
book.statement: Definition 6.2.1 (preprint 6.1): at a smooth point $x$, $\mathrm{ind}(f, x)$ is the Fredholm index of $(f - s)'(x)$ for a local sc$^+$-section $s$ with $s(x) = f(x)$; it does not depend on $s$. In Chapter 3 the statement along the solution set is implicit in Theorem 3.6.8 (1) (preprint 3.54).

diff: **Proposition 6.2.2 (preprint 6.2) is proved with the text’s hypotheses** (fifth addendum of this page; in the fourth, with bump functions), by the text’s device run on the restriction $P|V$ of $P$ to the domain $V$ of a strong bundle chart around $\varphi(t_0)$ (`StrongBundle.restrictOpen`), for each $t_0$: an sc$^+$-section $S$ of the pull-back to $\mathbb R \times V$ with $\tilde f + S = 0$ along the graph of the path near $t_0$ (the text’s $s(t, x) = R(x, f(\varphi(t)))$ in the chart, with no cut-off, since the chart covers $V$), the local constancy of the index of $\tilde f + S$ along its zero set (stabilizing sections $R(\cdot, e_i)$ in the product chart, again without cut-off, and the implicit function theorem), the index count $\mathrm{ind}(\tilde f + S)'(t, x) = \mathrm{ind}(f, x) + 1$ through the slice $S(t, \cdot)$ (`isIndexAt_of_pullback_isLinOfIndex`), and the connectedness of $\mathbb R$ (`proposition_6_2_local`). No bump functions are assumed (“we do not need a sc-smooth partition of unity”, preprint p. 202); tame germ data are the project’s reading of the text’s tameness (V3.103), as in V3.94, where they are no narrowing. With bump functions the proposition holds for the global reading of Definition 6.2.1 (preprint 6.1) as well (`proposition_6_2`, the form of the fourth addendum, whose section along the path is cut off by a bump; `exists_isScPlusSection_pullback_of_path`) (Findings, Chapter 3, items 340–349, 360–367).

**Why still “narrower”.** The path is $\varphi : \mathbb R \to X$, not $[0, 1] \to X$: $\mathbb R \times X$ is the product of Theorem 3.1.21 (preprint 3.18) and has no boundary, and the text’s tame M-polyfold $[0, 1] \times X$ is not used. A path on $[0, 1]$ that extends sc-smoothly to $\mathbb R$ is covered; a path sc-smooth on $[0, 1]$ only, in the sense of M-polyfolds with boundary, is not, and the project has no M-polyfold $[0, 1]$. This is the one narrowing left: the bump functions are gone, Definition 6.2.1 (preprint 6.1) has the text’s local sections, and the hypotheses on $f$ are the text’s in the project’s reading of tameness.

Definition 6.2.1 (preprint 6.1) has no row of its own. It is `IsIndexAtLocal`: the text’s locally defined sc$^+$-section is a section of the restriction $P|V$ to an open $V \ni x$ — the restriction of a strong bundle to an open set, which the text uses without comment, is constructed (`StrongBundle.restrictOpen`, whose atlas consists of the charts of $P$ inside $V$) — and the text’s $f - s$, $s(x) = f(x)$, is written $f + s$, $(f + s)(x) = 0$. It is well defined, two local sections being compared on the intersection of their domains (`IsIndexAtLocal.unique`), and it exists at every smooth point without bump functions, through the section $-R(\cdot, f(x))$ on a chart domain (`exists_isIndexAtLocal`). The global reading `IsIndexAt` of the fourth addendum implies it, and when $X$ admits bump functions the two agree, the local section being cut off (`isIndexAtLocal_iff_isIndexAt`). Along the solution set the formal proof combines the good position of the nearby zeros (V3.94), the local constancy of the dimension (V3.85) and dimension = index at each zero (V3.97); the text’s proof of Proposition 6.2.2 (preprint 6.2) uses the step of V3.82 for an extended section, which along solution sets is repaired by V3.93 (Findings, Chapter 3, items 171, 188). Updated after the repair of the tameness hypothesis: first proved with “the base retraction of every strong bundle chart compatible with the atlas is tame” (`htame`), which no strong bundle over a nonempty base satisfies (V3.104), so that form was vacuous; now with the hypotheses of V3.103 (Findings, Chapter 3, items 190–192).

The sc form (the index of $f'(y)$ as an sc-Fredholm operator, on every level, in every chart) is proved as well; that $\mathrm{Lin}(z)$ is sc-Fredholm at every zero in every chart, with the level-$0$ index on every level, is `StrongBundle.linAt_isScFredholm` (V3.96), cited here since the fifth addendum. **The local constancy without good position holds with the text’s hypotheses** (tame germ data, no bump functions; `index_locally_constant_tame`, in sc form `theorem_3_54_index_locally_constant_general_tame`), by the text’s device for Proposition 6.2.2 (preprint 6.2) on the restriction $P|V$ to a chart domain: finitely many sc$^+$-sections $R(\cdot, e_i)$, which on $P|V$ need no cut-off, put the parametrized section of Theorem 3.1.21 (preprint 3.18) into general position at $(0, x_0)$, its index is constant along its solution set (the case above), at $(0, y)$ it is $k + \operatorname{ind} f'(y)$, and the index at a zero is the same for $P$ and $P|V$, through the germ datum (Findings, Chapter 3, items 240–242, 360–363). The first proof, for M-polyfolds admitting bump functions (Lemma 5.3.3 (preprint 5.11) for the sections), is kept (`index_locally_constant_of_admitsBumpFunctions`). The candidate counterexample of items 188 and 243 is excluded under tame germ data by Theorem 3.6.8 (1) (preprint 3.54). items.title: Definitions 3.6.3, 3.6.4 and 3.6.6 (preprint 3.50, 3.51 and 3.53) in a tame chart

book.label: §3.6, Definitions 3.6.3, 3.6.4 (preprint 3.50, 3.51), p. 135 (preprint p. 110); Definition 3.6.6 (preprint 3.53), p. 136 (preprint p. 111)
book.statement: (3.50) For an sc-smooth section $f$ of the tame strong bundle $P : Y \to X$ and a smooth point $x$: $(f, x)$ is an sc-Fredholm germ if there is a strong bundle chart $\Phi : \Phi^{-1}(V) \to K$ around $x$ covering $\varphi : (V, x) \to (O, 0)$, “where $K \to O$ is a tame strong local bundle”, in which the local section has a filling $g$ near $0$ and a local sc$^+$-section $s$ with $s(0) = g(0)$ and $g - s$ conjugated near $0$ to a basic germ. (3.51) An sc-smooth section of the tame strong bundle is sc-Fredholm if it is regularizing and an sc-Fredholm germ at every smooth point. (3.53) Good position is defined for an sc-Fredholm germ of a tame strong bundle. A strong bundle retraction is tame when its base retraction $r$ is (preprint p. 49).

lean.statement: `StrongBundle.IsTameChart`: a strong bundle chart compatible with the atlas whose base retraction $r : U \to U$ is tame (Definition 2.5.2 (preprint 2.34)). `IsScFredholmGermTame f x` (“tame germ data”): $x$ smooth and the data of Definition 3.1.11 (preprint 3.11) in the text’s germ reading (V3.13) in a tame chart. `IsGoodPositionGermTame f x`: the same data with the germ in good position in that chart (V3.47). `IsScFredholmSectionTame f`: an sc-Fredholm section (V3.16) with tame germ data at every smooth point. Each implies the form without tameness; good position in a tame chart gives tame germ data; `IsGoodPositionGermFilled` (V3.82) is stated in a tame chart. A retraction agreeing on its domain with a tame one is tame, so a compatible chart whose base retraction is the identity of $U$ is tame.

chips: tame chart of the germ data
diff: These are the hypotheses of the implicit function theorems of §3.6 (V3.48, V3.68–V3.70, V3.80–V3.82, V3.84–V3.87, V3.94–V3.102). They were first proved with “tame strong bundle” read as: the base retraction of **every** strong bundle chart compatible with the atlas is tame. No strong bundle over a nonempty base satisfies that (V3.104), so those first statements were vacuous; the proofs used the tameness only for particular charts, and the repair changed the statements, not the arguments (Findings, Chapter 3, items 190–192, 198).

Whether germ data in some chart (V3.13) can be moved to some compatible tame chart when the atlas consists of tame charts (Definition 3.1.11 (preprint 3.11) $\Rightarrow$ Definition 3.6.3 (preprint 3.50)) is open. It cannot be done by re-centring a chart of the tame atlas: whether a filling exists in a chart depends on the chart ($\ker Dr(0) \cong \ker\rho(0)$ is necessary, `IsFillingGerm.nonempty_kerEquiv`), and the trivial bundle with the one-chart tame atlas of `evenBundleChart` has sc-Fredholm sections with tame germ data in compatible charts but none in the atlas chart (`tame_atlas_no_germData_in_atlas_chart`). The text builds the tame chart into Definition 3.6.3 (preprint 3.50), and so do the theorems (Findings, Chapter 3, items 199, 350–353). Updated in the fourth addendum of this page.

**Germs.** Since the switch to the text’s germ reading (phase 2) the three notions carry the germ data of the text (V3.13, V3.45); the earlier whole-chart forms are `IsScFredholmGermTameWholeChart`, `IsGoodPositionGermTameWholeChart`, `IsScFredholmSectionTameWholeChart`, and the non-vacuity witnesses satisfy both readings (Findings, Chapter 3, items 220–221, 304, 330). items.title: A non-tame retraction onto a product with a point: the earlier tameness hypothesis cannot be met

book.label: no counterpart in the text (Definitions 2.5.2, 2.6.4 (preprint 2.34, 2.50), pp. 53–54, 67–68 (preprint pp. 39–40, 51–52))
book.statement: Not in the text. Definition 2.5.2 (1) (preprint 2.34) asks a tame retraction to preserve the degeneracy index, $d_C(r(x)) = d_C(x)$; Definition 2.6.4 (preprint 2.50) asks of compatible strong bundle charts only that their transition maps be sc-smooth.

lean.statement: For an sc-Banach space $W$, the constant retraction $c : (a, w) \mapsto (1, 0)$ of the partial quadrant $[0, \infty) \oplus W$ of $\mathbb R \oplus W$ (sc-smooth, with retract $\{(1, 0)\}$), and every sc-smooth retraction $r$ of a nonempty relatively open $U$ in a partial quadrant $C$: the product retraction $c \times r$, with retract $\{(1, 0)\} \times r(U)$, is not tame. At $((0, 0), u)$, $u \in r(U)$, the degeneracy index is $1 + d_C(u)$, at its image $((1, 0), u)$ it is $d_C(u)$.

diff: The retraction-level half of the argument that the hypothesis under which the theorems of §3.6 were first proved, “the base retraction of every compatible strong bundle chart is tame”, fails for every strong bundle over a nonempty base: from a compatible chart $(\varphi, U, R, \Phi)$, the chart $(1, \varphi)$ onto $\{1\} \times O$ with base retraction $(a, u) \mapsto (1, r(u))$ on $[0, \infty) \times U$ (the retraction above with $W = 0$) has the transition maps of the first composed with affine maps, hence is compatible with every chart the first one is. That chart and its compatibility are not formalized (sc-calculus for affine maps). So the earlier statements were vacuous, and they are replaced by those with the hypotheses of V3.103 (Findings, Chapter 3, items 190, 199). Added after the repair of the tameness hypothesis.

items.title: Closed convex cones and extreme rays (p. 145)

book.label: §3.8.1.3, p. 145 (new in the 2021 edition)
book.statement: A closed convex cone $P$ in a finite-dimensional $N$: closed, convex, $P \cap (-P) = \{0\}$, $\mathbb R_+P = P$; an extreme ray is $\mathbb R_+x$, $x \in P \setminus \{0\}$, with $y, x - y \in P$ implying $y \in \mathbb R_+x$.

lean.statement: The same definitions, with witnesses; and for $N$ in good position with $N \cap C$ pointed, $N \cap C$ is carried onto $[0, \infty)^{\dim N}$ by a linear isomorphism.

items.title: Lemma 3.8.4

book.label: §3.8.1.3, Lemma 3.8.4, p. 147 (new in the 2021 edition)

items.title: Definition 4.1.1 (preprint 4.1): corner charts and corner structures

book.label: §4.1, Definition 4.1.1 (preprint 4.1), p. 175 (preprint p. 147)
book.statement: An M-polyfold $X$ has a compatible smooth manifold structure with boundary with corners if it admits an atlas of sc-smoothly compatible charts $(V, \varphi, (U, C, \mathbb R^n))$, $\varphi : V \to U$ an sc-diffeomorphism from an open $V \subseteq X$ onto a relatively open subset $U$ of a partial quadrant $C$ in $\mathbb R^n$ (or in a finite-dimensional vector space).

lean.statement: A corner chart (`MChart.IsCornerChart`) is a chart whose model is $(U, C, V)$ with $V$ finite-dimensional, the constant sc-structure, $U$ relatively open in the partial quadrant $C$, and the identity retraction. `HasCornerStructure`: an atlas of corner charts equivalent to the atlas of $X$; equivalently every point lies in a corner chart that is a chart of $X$. The dimension may vary. Corner models are tame retracts and sc⁺-retracts; a corner structure makes $X$ tame.

diff: "Sc-smoothly compatible" and "$\varphi$ an sc-diffeomorphism" are read as compatibility with the atlas of $X$, as for tameness (Findings, Chapter 4, item 50).
The classical manifold structure is represented by the corner atlas; local constancy of the dimension is neither stated nor formalized.

items.title: Definition 4.1.1 (preprint 4.1): the transition maps are $C^\infty$

book.label: §4.1, after Definition 4.1.1 (preprint 4.1), p. 175 (preprint p. 147)
book.statement: The transition maps between the charts are sc-diffeomorphisms between relatively open subsets of partial quadrants in finite-dimensional spaces, and therefore classically smooth, of class $C^\infty$; the atlas defines the structure of a smooth manifold with boundary with corners.

lean.statement: For compatible corner charts $\chi$, $\chi'$ the overlap $\chi(V \cap V')$ is relatively open and the transition map $\chi' \circ \chi^{-1}$ is $C^\infty$ on it (derivatives within the set).

items.title: Finite-dimensional sc-Banach spaces have the constant structure

book.label: §1.1, after Definition 1.1.1 (preprint 1.1), p. 5 (preprint p. 6) (used in Definition 4.1.1 (preprint 4.1))
book.statement: A finite-dimensional Banach space $E$ has precisely one sc-structure, namely the constant structure $E_m = E$.

lean.statement: If $E_0$ is finite-dimensional, every level is finite-dimensional, every inclusion $E_m \to E_0$ is onto, $E$ is sc-isomorphic to $E_0$ with the constant structure through the inclusions, and every point is smooth.

items.title: Definition 4.1.1 (preprint 4.1) with arbitrary finite-dimensional models; Chapter 3's manifolds with corners

items.title: Theorem 4.1.2 (preprint 4.2): the characterization

book.label: §4.1, Theorem 4.1.2 (preprint 4.2), p. 176 (preprint p. 147) (proof pp. 183–186 (preprint pp. 156–157))
book.statement: For a tame M-polyfold $X$ the following are equivalent. (i) $X$ has a compatible smooth manifold structure with boundary with corners. (ii) $X_0 = X_\infty$ and $1_0^1 : X \to X^1$ is sc-smooth; every $x$ lies in a tame chart $(V, \psi, (O, C, E))$ with $\psi(x) = 0$ whose tangent space $T_0O$ is finite-dimensional and in good position to $C$.

items.title: Remark 4.1.3 (preprint 4.3): $1_1^0$, $1_0^1$, and the constant structure

book.label: §4.1, Remark 4.1.3 (preprint 4.3), p. 176 (preprint p. 148)
book.statement: If $X_0 = X_\infty$, $1_0^1 : X \to X^1$ has the inverse $1_1^0$, which is always sc-smooth; so if $1_0^1$ is sc-smooth it is an sc-diffeomorphism. It is possible that $X^1 \ne X$ as M-polyfolds although the underlying sets agree. A finite-dimensional space with the constant structure has $X = X^1$.

lean.statement: $1_1^0 : X^1 \to X$ is sc-smooth (in charts the sc-operator $\iota : E^1 \to E$). If $X = X_1$ as sets and $1_0^1$ is sc-smooth, it is an sc-diffeomorphism with inverse $1_1^0$. For a finite-dimensional $V$: $(\mathrm{const}\,V)^1 = \mathrm{const}\,V$, the lift is the identity, every retract is an sc⁺-retract. **The example** (`remark_4_3_example`): an M-polyfold with $X_0 = X_\infty$ for which $1_0^1 : X \to X^1$ is not sc-smooth, so $X^1 \ne X$ as M-polyfolds; it is a retract $O = O_\infty \subseteq \mathbb R \oplus X$ that is not an sc⁺-retract (`remark_4_3_retract_example`), the image of the retraction $(t, z) \mapsto (t, L(t)z)$ of moving rank-one projections on a weighted sequence space, sc-smooth by a criterion for parameter families of level operators with one level of loss (`IsLossFamily.isScSmooth`). $(X^1)_m = X_{m+1}$ as sets (`MPolyfold.mem_shift_levelSet_iff`).

diff: “It is possible that $X^1 \ne X$ as M-polyfolds although the sets agree” is proved by an example the preprint and 2017 texts do not give (fourth addendum of this page; formerly gap G.31); the 2021 edition (p. 176) gives a different one, the space of its Subsection 1.4.4, which is not formalized (Findings, Chapter 4, item 159). By Proposition 4.1.8 (preprint 4.8) an example is a retract $O = O_\infty$ that is not an sc⁺-retract; it cannot come from a retraction whose level maps are $C^1$ (an argument, not formalized), so its retraction loses a level in its first derivative, as the splicings of HWZ do, and its sc-smoothness rests on a criterion with loss proved for it, not on Proposition 1.2.4 (preprint 1.19). In the example $X$ and $X^1$ even have different topologies on the same set (Findings, Chapter 4, items 140–146).

“$X^1 \ne X$” is read as “$1_0^1$ is not sc-smooth”, equivalently (by `remark_4_3_isScDiffeo`) “the identity is not an sc-diffeomorphism $X \to X^1$”. The sc-diffeomorphism clause needs only $X = X_1$, not $X_0 = X_\infty$. “$(X^1)_m = X_{m+1} = X_i$” misprints $X_0$; $(X^1)_m = X_{m+1}$ holds as sets and with the topologies of the iterated levels (`MPolyfold.shiftLevelHomeomorph`, V2.93; gap G.6, closed) (Findings, Chapter 4, items 5, 125). Hence “stronger” (formerly “narrower”, for the missing example).

items.title: Definition 4.1.4 (preprint 4.4): sc⁺-retractions

book.statement: An sc-smooth retraction $r : U \to U$ is an sc⁺-retraction if $r(U_m) \subseteq U_{m+1}$ for all $m$ and $r : U \to U^1$ is sc-smooth; on an open $V \subseteq X$, if $r : V \to V^1$ is sc-smooth.
