diff: $Y^i \to X^i$ is never defined in the text (it defines $Y[i]$ for $i = 0, 1$). $Y^1$ is read as $Y_{1,1}$ with $(Y^1)_{m,k} = Y_{m+1,k+1}$, the convention of $E^1$ and of $(U \triangleleft F)^1 = U^1 \triangleleft F^1$; it is forced by “$f^i$ is obtained by raising the index”: an sc-smooth section maps $X_1$ into $Y_{1,1}$, in general not into $Y_{1,2}$. “It is a priori clear” hides condition (3) of the filling on level $1$ ($\ker Dr^1(0) \to \ker\rho^1(0)$ a topological isomorphism), which does not follow from level $0$ alone: an sc-operator can be bijective on level $0$ and not onto on level $1$. No hypothesis beyond the text’s is added.

Tameness is not used. The tame form (germ data of $f^1$ in tame charts of $P^1$) is not stated: the tameness of the index raise of a tame chart is not proved, and no counterexample is known (Findings, Chapter 5, item 145). $i \ge 2$ by iteration: V5.13. items.title: $\Gamma^{+,1}_U(P)$, the allowable sections, and the metric $\rho$

book.label: §5.3, preprint p. 174
book.statement: $\Gamma^{+,1}_U(P)$: the $s \in \Gamma^+(P)$ with $\operatorname{supp}(s) \subseteq U$ and $N(s(x)) \le 1$ for all $x$, a metric space for $\rho(s, s') = \sup_xN(s(x) - s'(x))$, not complete.

lean.statement: `allowableSections N U`; `sectionDistAt`: $N(s(x) - s'(x))$ in the fibre $(Y_{0,1})_x$. `allowableDist`: $\rho(s, s') = \sup_xN(s(x) - s'(x))$, finite ($\rho \le 2$); for an auxiliary norm $N$ a metric on $\Gamma^{+,1}_U(P)$ (`allowableMetric`), with $\rho(s, s') \le \varepsilon$ iff $N(s(x) - s'(x)) \le \varepsilon$ for all $x$. Not complete for the trivial bundle $\mathbb R \times \mathbb R \to \mathbb R$ with $N(x, v) = |v|$ and $U = \mathbb R$ (`TrivialBundle.not_completeSpace_allowableSections`); complete for $U = \emptyset$, for every bundle and auxiliary norm (`completeSpace_allowableSections_empty`), and over a point with fibre $\mathbb R^k$ (`TrivialBundle.completeSpace_allowableSections_point`).

diff: The text’s “$(\Gamma^{+,1}_U(P), \rho)$ is not complete” is false without a hypothesis: for $U = \emptyset$ the space is a point, and over a point with finite-dimensional fibre it is the closed unit ball of $\mathbb R^k$. It is read as “not complete in general” and proved by an example: the allowable sections $s_j(x) = (x, \sqrt{x^2 + 1/(j+1)^2}/(2\sqrt{1 + x^2}))$ form a $\rho$-Cauchy sequence whose pointwise limit has fibre part $|x|/(2\sqrt{1 + x^2})$, not differentiable at $0$, while the fibre part of an sc⁺-section of the trivial bundle is $C^1$. That non-completeness holds whenever $U$ contains a non-isolated point over which $Y_{0,1}$ is nonzero (the text’s setting) is expected by the same mechanism and not formalized (Findings, Chapter 5, items 150–153; gap G.42).

Only Definition 5.1.1 (1) (preprint 5.1) is used for the metric axioms (symmetry and subadditivity of the fibre norms, $N$ vanishing only at $0_x$); the density statements of Theorems 5.3.5 and 5.3.10 (preprint 5.13 and 5.18) are $\rho(s, s') \le \varepsilon$ (`allowableDist_le_iff`; V5.30, V5.39). Hence still “restated”; before the fourth addendum of this page $\rho$ was used pointwise only and the metric space was not formalized (Findings, Chapter 5, item 47).

items.title: The determinant lines $\lambda(E)$, $\lambda^*(E)$ and the maps $\lambda(\Phi)$

For $\dim E = \dim F$, `maxPowMap` is $\lambda(\Phi)$ on wedges (`maxPowMap_wedge`), with $\lambda(\Psi\Phi) = \lambda(\Psi)\lambda(\Phi)$ (`maxPowMap_comp`), nonzero iff $\Phi$ is bijective (`maxPowMap_ne_zero_iff`); `maxPowDualMap` is its dual.

book.statement: The proofs of Lemmas 6.6.8, 6.6.10 (preprint 6.33, 6.34) and of Theorem 6.6.11 (preprint 6.35) use that "as $\tau$ varies, the bundle varies continuously", and that the data of the exact sequences at the end points vary continuously.

lean.statement: `exists_subspaceFamily_ker`: the kernels of a norm-continuous family of surjective Fredholm operators over a connected base form a continuous family of subspaces. `SubspaceFamily.exists_map`, `SubspaceFamily.isLineOrientation_map`: so do the images of a continuous family under a jointly continuous family of linear maps injective on its members, and orientations are carried along. `SubspaceFamily.exists_inf_ker`: cutting a continuous family by the kernel of a fixed $\ell$ that is onto on every member gives one.

diff: "Varies continuously" is read in the operator norm, and for maps into a model space as joint continuity.

items.title: The stabilized section in a product chart

book.label: §6.6 (preprint §6.5), $F$, preprint p. 221; $F_t$, $L_t$ and (96), pp. 264–266 (preprint pp. 222–223)
book.statement: $F_t(y, \lambda) = F(t, y, \lambda)$ on $X \times \mathbb R^k$, $L_t = \ker F_t'(\varphi(t), 0)$, and the exact sequence (96) relates $\ker((f - s(\cdot, t))'(\varphi(t)))$, $\ker F_t'(\varphi(t), 0)$, $\mathbb R^k$ and $Y_{\varphi(t)}/R((f - s(\cdot, t))'(\varphi(t)))$.

lean.statement: In the product chart $(\lambda \mapsto \lambda) \times ((q \mapsto q) \times \varphi)$ at $(0, (q, z))$ the linearization of $F$ is $(\lambda, (\sigma, v)) \mapsto D(\hat g_q \circ r)(z)v + \sum\lambda_i\hat s_i(q, \cdot)(z) + D_q\sigma$, with $g_q = f + S(q, \cdot)$ (`StrongBundle.scDeriv_paramSection_ofProd_ofProd`, with the chart lemmas `PullbackChartData.ofProd_scDeriv_r_apply`, `StrongBundle.scDeriv_ofProd_slice_apply`, `StrongBundleChart.paramDerivAt`). Its kernel cut by $\sigma = 0$ (`sliceProj`, `sliceIncl`) is the image of $\ker(T \oplus \varphi)$, with $T = g_q'(x) \in \mathrm{Lin}(f, x)$ (`mem_linSet_sectionAdd_pullbackSlice`) and $\varphi(\lambda) = \sum\lambda_is_i(q, x)$ (`linKer_inf_ker_sliceProj_eq_map`, `exists_sliceOps`, `exists_sliceKernel`); $T \oplus \varphi$ is onto when $F$ is in general position at $(0, (q, \Phi(q)))$ (`surjective_coprod_of_isLinSurjAt`).

diff: $\ker F_t'(\varphi(t), 0)$ is read as the kernel of the linearization of the whole $F$ cut by $\sigma = 0$; in the product chart the linearization of the slice is $(v, \lambda) \mapsto Tv + \varphi\lambda$ (Findings, Chapter 6, item 49).

items.title: Lemma 6.6.6 (preprint 6.31): the sequence (96) is exact

items.title: Continuation and the isomorphisms $\Phi_{E_t}$

book.label: §6.6 (preprint §6.5), pp. 265–269 (preprint pp. 223–224), after Lemma 6.6.6 (preprint 6.31)
book.statement: $\Phi_{E_t} : \det((f - s(\cdot, t))'(\varphi(t))) \to \lambda(L_t) \otimes \lambda^*(\mathbb R^k)$. An orientation $o_0$ of $\mathrm{DET}(f, \varphi(0))$ orients $\det((f - s(\cdot, 0))'(\varphi(0)))$; $\Phi_{E_0}$ turns it into an orientation of $\lambda(L_0) \otimes \lambda^*(\mathbb R^k)$, continuation extends it to $t = 1$, and $(\Phi_{E_1})^{-1}$ gives an orientation of $\det((f - s(\cdot, 1))'(\varphi(1)))$, hence $o_1$.

lean.statement: `SubspaceFamily.cont`: over a simply connected, locally path-connected base, the continuation of a ray of $\lambda(L_{q_0})$ to $\lambda(L_{q_1})$, a bijection (`SubspaceFamily.contEquiv`, `cont_eq`), compatible with composition and pull-back (`cont_self`, `cont_trans`, `cont_comp`), and along $[0, 1]$ the continuation of V6.35 (`cont_eq_transport`). For a stabilization $T \oplus \varphi$ onto and an identification of its kernel with $L$, the rays of $\det(T)$ and of $\lambda(L)$ correspond (`stabRayEquiv`, through $\iota_\varphi$ of V6.18 and $\det(T \oplus \varphi) \cong \lambda(\ker(T \oplus \varphi))$, `detEquivOfSurjective`); `propagate`: $\Phi_{E_0}$, continuation and $\Phi_{E_1}^{-1}$ composed, a bijection of the rays of $\det(T_0)$ and $\det(T_1)$ (`propagate_self`, `propagate_trans`, `propagate_comp`).

items.title: The stabilization sign $(-1)^{\dim\operatorname{coker}T}$

book.label: §6.4 (preprint §6.3), formula (94), p. 256 (preprint p. 212), as it is used on pp. 265–272 (preprint pp. 223–226)
book.statement: The orientations carried by $\Phi_{E_t}$ along $t$, and those of the bundles $\tilde L_\tau$ along $\tau$, are used as varying continuously with the parameter (Lemmas 6.6.8, 6.6.10 (preprint 6.33, 6.34) and the homotopy argument before Theorem 6.6.11 (preprint 6.35)).

lean.statement: `coord_stabIota`: in a local determinant chart with projection $P$, the chart coordinate of $\iota_\psi(x) \in \det(S \oplus \psi)$ is $(-1)^{k\dim F/R(P) + \dim\operatorname{coker} S}D(S, \psi)$ times that of $x$, with $D$ (`stabD`) continuous and nowhere zero near the centre (`continuousOn_stabD`, `stabD_ne_zero`). `isLineOrientation_stabRay`: for a continuous orientation $o$ of $\mathrm{DET}$, a norm-continuous family $T_q$ and a continuous stabilization $\varphi_q$ with $T_q \oplus \varphi_q$ onto, the rays $(-1)^{\dim\operatorname{coker} T_q}\,\Phi(o(T_q))$ (`stabSign`) of $\lambda(\ker(T_q \oplus \varphi_q))$ form an orientation. `not_isLineOrientation_stabRay_uncorrected`: without the sign they need not ($E = F = \mathbb R$, $k = 1$, $T_q = q/(1 + |q|)$, $\varphi(r) = r_0$).

diff: As we read it, the orientations carried by $\Phi_E$ of (94) along a continuous family are not continuous where $\dim\operatorname{coker} T$ changes parity: the first exponent is constant on a chart, the second is not. The propagation uses the sign-normalized $(-1)^{\dim\operatorname{coker} T}\Phi_E$, which on each operator carries the text's orientation or its opposite (Findings, Chapter 6, item 50).

items.title: The push-forward $o_1 = \varphi_*o_0$ along stabilized kernels

book.label: §6.6 (preprint §6.5), the push-forward, preprint p. 224
book.statement: The orientation $o_1$ of $\mathrm{DET}(f, \varphi(1))$ obtained from $o_0$ by $\Phi_{E_0}$, continuation and $(\Phi_{E_1})^{-1}$ is the push-forward orientation $o_1 = \varphi_*o_0$; a priori it might depend on the choices of $s(y, t)$ and $s_1, \dots, s_k$.

lean.statement: At a chart point, `ChartPoint.stabT` is $T = (f + S)'(x) \in \mathrm{Lin}(f, x)$ (`ChartPoint.stabT_mem_linSet`) and `ChartPoint.stabPhi` is $\varphi(\lambda) = \sum\lambda_i\hat s_i(x)$. `IsStabKernels`: a continuous family $\Lambda$, over a parameter space, of the subspaces $\ker(T_q \oplus \varphi_q)$ of $E_0 \times \mathbb R^k$ at points $y(q)$, read in one chart. `IsStabKernels.push`: $\mathrm{Or}^f_{x_0} \to \mathrm{Or}^f_{x_1}$, $o \mapsto o(T_a) \mapsto (-1)^{\dim\operatorname{coker} T_a}\Phi_{E_a}(o(T_a))$, continued to $\lambda(\Lambda_b)$ and carried back in the same way at $T_b$. It depends only on the data (`IsStabKernels.push_congr`), is compatible with pull-back (`IsStabKernels.comp`, `IsStabKernels.push_comp`) and with concatenation (`IsStabKernels.push_trans`), and along a path with continuously varying data continuation carries the rays read at one parameter to those read at the next (`IsStabKernels.orRay`, `IsStabKernels.push_eq_orRay`, `IsStabKernels.cont_orRay_path`).

diff: The sign of V6.40 is used at both end points; for given end-point operators the result differs from the text's by $(-1)^{\dim\operatorname{coker} T_a + \dim\operatorname{coker} T_b}$. The sections enter pointwise, and the continuity in the parameter is that of $\Lambda$ (Findings, Chapter 6, item 50).

items.title: Lemma 6.6.5 (preprint 6.30) for the push-forward: the stabilized kernels exist

book.label: §6.6 (preprint §6.5), Lemma 6.6.5 (preprint 6.30) and the bundle $L$ after it, pp. 264–266 (preprint pp. 222–223)
book.statement: Along the path the kernels $L_t = \ker F_t'(\varphi(t), 0)$, tangent spaces of the solution manifold $S_t$ of Lemma 6.6.5 (preprint 6.30), form the smooth vector bundle $L$ over $[0, 1]$.

items.title: Push-forward data along paths

book.label: §6.6 (preprint §6.5), the choices along the path, preprint pp. 221, 224
book.statement: Along an sc-smooth $\varphi : [0, 1] \to X$, "assuming $X = U$", one chooses by Proposition 6.6.3 (preprint 6.28) an sc⁺-section $s$ with $s(\varphi(t), t) = f(\varphi(t))$, adds sections $s_1, \dots, s_k$ on $X \times [0, 1]$ with (P), and builds the push-forward from these choices.

lean.statement: `IsPush`: $e$ is a push-forward along an sc-smooth path $\gamma$ in a chart if there are global sc⁺-sections $S, s_1, \dots, s_k$ of $\pi^*P \to \mathbb R \times X$ with $(f + S)(t, \gamma(t)) = 0$ for $t$ near $[0, 1]$ (`isZeroAt_sectionAdd_reparamSection`) and a family of stabilized kernels of their slices along $\gamma$ whose push-forward is $e$. A push-forward along $\gamma$ is the composite of push-forwards along its two halves (`IsPush.split`, `isPush_reparam`), and along every sc-smooth path in a set with property (3) of Proposition 6.6.3 (preprint 6.28) there is one (`exists_isPush`).

diff: Global sections of the pull-back in place of sections over $U \times [0, 1]$; property (P) is used only to construct a push-forward (Findings, Chapter 6, item 46).

items.title: Proposition 6.6.7 (preprint 6.32): the push-forward does not depend on the choices

book.label: §6.6 (preprint §6.5), Proposition 6.6.7 (preprint 6.32), p. 267 (preprint p. 224) (proof pp. 266–272 (preprint pp. 224–226))
book.statement: For $U$ as in Proposition 6.6.3 (preprint 6.28) and an sc-smooth $\varphi : [0, 1] \to U$, $o \mapsto \varphi_*o$ does not depend on the choices as long as the hypotheses of Lemma 6.6.4 (preprint 6.29) hold. The proof adds sections to both data so that they have the same number and (P) holds along a convex homotopy, and applies Lemmas 6.6.8 and 6.6.10 (preprint 6.33 and 6.34).

lean.statement: `proposition_6_32` ($X$ tame, bump functions, $f$ with tame germ data): two push-forwards (`IsPush`) along the same sc-smooth path in the domain of a chart agree. The proof uses one square: $S^\tau = (1 - \tau)S^0 + \tau S^1$ with the two families of sections interpolated (`isZeroAt_sectionAdd_combo`, `linAt_principal_combo`, `continuous_principal_pullbackSlice`) and the sections of Lemma 6.6.4 (preprint 6.29) on the square appended (`IsStabKernels.push_eq_of_prefix`, `IsStabKernels.congr_data`, `IsStabKernels.push_congr_data`).

diff: "Does not depend on the choices" is read as the agreement of any two data. Lemmas 6.6.8 and 6.6.10 (preprint 6.33 and 6.34) are combined over one square: at $\tau = 0$ the sections $s^0$ are the first $k^0$ of the family and at $\tau = 1$ the sections $s^1$ are the first $k^1$, so Lemma 6.6.8 (preprint 6.33) applies on both edges without reordering; along the edges $t = 0, 1$ the operators are affine in $\tau$, hence continuous (Findings, Chapter 6, item 52).

items.title: Lemma 6.6.8 (preprint 6.33): adding sections does not change the push-forward

book.label: §6.6 (preprint §6.5), Lemma 6.6.8 (preprint 6.33), p. 267 (preprint p. 224) (proof preprint p. 225)
book.statement: If $F$ has property (P), the section $F(t, y, \lambda) + \sum\mu_j\bar s_j(y, t)$ on $[0, 1] \times X \times \mathbb R^{k+l}$ defines the same propagation along $\varphi$. The proof passes through the homotopy $\tilde F(\tau, \cdot)$, and at $\tau = 0$ "one verifies by a simple computation" that $\tilde L_0 = L \oplus ([0, 1] \times \mathbb R^l)$ defines the same propagation.

lean.statement: `detEquiv_stabIota_append`: with the appended sections last (`appendStab`, `kerAppend`), the stabilization isomorphism of $(\varphi, \psi)$ is that of $\varphi$ followed by `wedgeExt`, $w \mapsto (w, 0) \wedge \ell_1 \wedge \dots \wedge \ell_d$, for any $\ell_j \in \ker(T \oplus (\varphi, \psi))$ with $\psi$-coordinates the standard basis (`wedgeExt_wedge`, `wedgeExt_congr`, `wedgeExt_bijective`); this map carries continuous orientations along the family (`isLineOrientation_wedgeExt`, with `SubspaceFamily.exists_continuous_lifts`, `kerEquivMap`). Hence appending sections does not change the push-forward (`stabRayEquiv_append`, `propagate_append`, `IsStabKernels.push_append`).

diff: The homotopy $\tilde F(\tau, \cdot)$ of the text's proof is not needed: with the appended sections last the two isomorphisms agree exactly, with no sign. The comparison is made directly between $T \oplus \varphi$ and $T \oplus (\varphi, \psi)$, at the end points by Proposition 6.4.15 (preprint 6.15) and along the family by `isLineOrientation_wedgeExt` (Findings, Chapter 6, item 51).

items.title: Theorem 6.6.11 (preprint 6.35): local propagation

book.label: §6.6 (preprint §6.5), the homotopy argument, pp. 271–273 (preprint pp. 226–227), and Theorem 6.6.11 (preprint 6.35), p. 272 (preprint p. 227)
book.statement: For a strong bundle over a tame $X$ and a smooth $x$ there is an open sc-smoothly contractible $U(x)$ such that along every sc-smooth path $\varphi : [0, 1] \to U$ there is a well-defined propagation $o \mapsto \varphi_*o$ of orientations of $\mathrm{DET}(f, \varphi(0))$, and $\varphi_{0*}o = \varphi_{1*}o$ for two such paths with the same end points. The proof homotopes $\varphi_0$ to $\varphi_1$ in $U$, using that $U$ is sc-smoothly contractible.

lean.statement: `theorem_6_35` ($X$ tame, bump functions, $f$ with tame germ data): every smooth $x$ has an open $U \ni x$ and a chart $c$ of the atlas with `HasLocalPropagation`: push-forwards exist along the sc-smooth paths in $U$ with smooth end points and depend only on their end points. `push_eq_of_homotopy`: push-forwards along two paths related by an sc-smooth homotopy with fixed end points agree.

diff: The statement does not introduce the section $f$ (possible omission); it is read for an sc-Fredholm section with tame germ data, under the standing hypotheses (Findings, Chapter 6, item 53).

$U$ is not shown to be sc-smoothly contractible (gap G.61); what the proof uses is (1′) of V6.32. Since the homotopy of (1′) meets its edge conditions only on $[0, 1]$, while a push-forward datum needs $f + S = 0$ near $[0, 1]$, the proof passes through the reparametrized paths $\gamma_i \circ \kappa$, with three homotopies whose edges are exact (Findings, Chapter 6, item 53).

items.title: Sc-smooth paths in a chart and their concatenation

book.label: §6.6 (preprint §6.5), the paths after Theorem 6.6.11 (preprint 6.35), p. 272 (preprint p. 227), and the concatenation, preprint p. 228
book.statement: For $y \in U$ one takes an sc-smooth path $\varphi : [0, 1] \to U$ from $x$ to $y$. The composition of paths is $\varphi(\beta(s))$ for $s \in [0, 1/2]$ and $\psi(\beta(s))$ for $s \in [1/2, 1]$, for a smooth $\beta$ with $\beta([0, 1/2]) = [0, 1]$, $\beta([1/2, 1]) = [1, 2]$, constant near $1/2$. On preprint p. 201 the text recalls that an M-polyfold is locally path connected and that smooth points of one path component are joined by an sc⁺-smooth path.

lean.statement: `exists_nhds_scPath`: for an open $U$ in the domain of a chart and $x \in U$ there is an open $V \ni x$ in $U$ whose smooth points are pairwise joined by sc-smooth paths in $U$. `concatPath`: $\gamma_1(\kappa(3s))$ for $s \le 1/2$ and $\gamma_2(\kappa(3s - 2))$ for $s > 1/2$, $\kappa$ the smooth transition function, is sc-smooth (`isScSmoothMap_concatPath`), with the right end points and halves (`concatPath_zero`, `concatPath_one`, `concatPath_half₁`, `concatPath_half₂`); reparametrizing by a $C^\infty$ map keeps sc-smoothness (`isScSmoothMap_reparam`); push-forwards compose along concatenations (`HasLocalPropagation.eq_trans`).

items.title: Definition 6.6.12 (preprint 6.36): orientable neighbourhoods and continuous orientations

book.label: §6.6 (preprint §6.5), the paragraph after Theorem 6.6.11 (preprint 6.35) and Definition 6.6.12 (preprint 6.36), p. 273 (preprint p. 227)
book.statement: Fixing $o_x$, $o_y = \varphi_*o_x$ for a path $\varphi$ in $U$ from $x$ to $y$ does not depend on the path, and $\psi_*o_{y_1} = o_{y_2}$ for paths in $U$. An open contractible $U(x)$ on which the local propagation can be carried out is an orientable neighbourhood of $(f, x)$; a choice of orientations of $\mathrm{DET}(f, y)$, $y \in U_\infty$, with the propagation property is a continuous orientation, and an orientable neighbourhood has precisely two.

lean.statement: `IsOrientableNbhd`: a pair $V \subseteq U$, $U$ open with the local propagation property in a chart, $V \ni x$ open with any two smooth points joined by an sc-smooth path in $U$; every smooth point has one (`exists_orientableNbhd`, `exists_isOrientableNbhd`). `IsContinuousOrientation`: a choice $y \mapsto o_y$ on $V_\infty$ carried into itself by the push-forwards along paths in $U$; there are exactly two (`exists_two_isContinuousOrientation`).

items.title: Reparametrization homotopies

book.label: §6.6 (preprint §6.5), the homotopy classes $[\varphi]$, pp. 272–274 (preprint pp. 227–228)
book.statement: $[\varphi]$ is the sc-smooth homotopy class of $\varphi : [0, 1] \to X$ with the end points fixed, with source $\varphi(0)$ and target $\varphi(1)$; the composition of classes is defined through a reparametrization $\beta$.

lean.statement: `isScHomotopyRel_reparam`: for a $C^\infty$ $\theta$ with $\theta(0) = 0$ and $\theta(1) = 1$, $\gamma \circ \theta$ is sc-smoothly homotopic to $\gamma$ with the end points fixed, inside every set containing $\gamma([0, 1])$ when $\theta([0, 1]) \subseteq [0, 1]$ (`reparam_mem`); the concatenation of the two halves of $\gamma$ is such a reparametrization (`leftHalf`, `rightHalf`, `halvesReparam`, `concatPath_halves`).

items.title: The path category $PX$

book.label: §6.6 (preprint §6.5), the classes $[\varphi]$, their composition and the category $PX$, pp. 272–274 (preprint pp. 227–228)
book.statement: For $t([\varphi]) = s([\psi])$, $[\psi] * [\varphi]$ is the class of $\gamma$, equal to $\varphi(\beta(s))$ on $[0, 1/2]$ and $\psi(\beta(s))$ on $[1/2, 1]$; this gives a category $PX$ whose objects are the smooth points of $X$ and whose morphisms $x \to y$ are the classes with source $x$ and target $y$.

lean.statement: `ScHomotopic`: sc-smooth homotopy with the end points fixed, an equivalence relation on the sc-smooth paths `ScPath` between two points (`ScHomotopic.refl`, `ScHomotopic.symm`, `ScHomotopic.trans`). `ScPath.concat` is well defined on classes (`ScPath.concat_congr`), associative (`ScPath.concat_assoc`, via `assocReparam`, `isScHomotopyRel_triHomotopy`), with the classes of the constant paths as units (`ScPath.const_concat`, `ScPath.concat_const`) and the reversed paths as inverses (`ScPath.concat_reverse`, `ScPath.reverse_concat`). `PathCat`: the smooth points with the classes `ScPathClass` form a category (`PathCat.category`), indeed a groupoid (`PathCat.groupoid`).

With $\beta([1/2, 1]) = [1, 2]$ the second piece $\psi(\beta(s))$ leaves $[0, 1]$; it is read as $\psi(\beta(s) - 1)$ (possible misprint). Mathlib's $[\varphi] \gg [\psi]$ is the text's $[\psi] * [\varphi]$ (Findings, Chapter 6, item 55).

items.title: Transferring orientations between chart points

book.label: §6.6 (preprint §6.5), preprint p. 219, and the proof of Theorem 6.6.13 (preprint 6.37), p. 273 (preprint p. 228)

items.title: Transport along paths from local push-forwards

book.label: §6.6 (preprint §6.5), the proof of Theorem 6.6.13 (preprint 6.37), p. 273 (preprint p. 228)
book.statement: For a path $\varphi$ and $t_0 \in [0, 1]$ one chooses an orientable neighbourhood $U(\varphi(t_0))$ and an open interval $I(t_0)$ on which orientations propagate; using the compactness of $[0, 1]$ and a finite covering, $o_0$ is transported to $o_1$; "by a covering argument" $\varphi_*$ depends only on $[\varphi]$, and the uniqueness of $\Gamma_f$ is called obvious.

lean.statement: `LocalTransport`: local data (good open sets covering $X_\infty$ and push-forwards along paths in a good set, compatible with concatenation and independent of the good set; `LocalTransport.push_eq_refl`, `LocalTransport.push_eq_push`, `LocalTransport.push_congr`). `LocalTransport.transportN`: the composite of the push-forwards along the $2^N$ dyadic pieces of a path (`vSeg`, `hSeg`, `dSeg`), the same for every $N$ at which every piece lies in a good set (`LocalTransport.IsFine`, `LocalTransport.transportN_eq_of_isFine`); such $N$ exist by the Lebesgue number lemma (`LocalTransport.exists_isLebesgueNumber`). `LocalTransport.transport` is the push-forward on a path in a good set (`LocalTransport.transport_eq_push`), homotopy invariant (`LocalTransport.transport_eq_of_isScHomotopyRel`, on dyadic squares: `LocalTransport.transportN_square`, `equiv_paste_squares`), compatible with concatenation and reparametrization, the identity on constant paths, and the only family with these properties (`LocalTransport.transport_unique`).

items.title: Theorem 6.6.13 (preprint 6.37): the functor $\Gamma_f$

book.label: §6.6 (preprint §6.5), Theorem 6.6.13 (preprint 6.37) and its proof, preprint p. 228
book.statement: For a strong bundle over a tame $X$ and an sc-Fredholm $f$ there is a uniquely determined functor $\Gamma_f : PX \to \mathcal O_f$, $x \mapsto \mathrm{Or}^f_x$, $[\varphi] \mapsto \Gamma_f([\varphi]) : \mathrm{Or}^f_x \to \mathrm{Or}^f_y$, with property (∗): for every sc-smoothly contractible open $U(x)$ on which $f$ has the local propagation property, $\varphi_* = \Gamma_f([\varphi])$ for every sc-smooth path $\varphi$ in $U$.

lean.statement: `theorem_6_37` ($X$ tame, bump functions, $f$ with tame germ data, $P$ with sc⁺-sections through the smooth fibre points): there is exactly one family of bijections $\Gamma_f([\varphi]) : \mathrm{Or}^f_x \to \mathrm{Or}^f_y$ on the morphisms of $PX$ that takes identities to identities and compositions to composites and has (∗) (`IsStarProperty`, `IsStarPropertyOn`): for every chart $c$, every open $U$ with the local propagation property in $c$ (`IsPropagationNbhd`) and every sc-smooth path $\varphi$ in $U$, $\Gamma_f([\varphi])$ is every push-forward along $\varphi$ in $c$ (`orPush`), read through $\mathrm{Or}^f$ of the chosen charts. `orFunctor`: the functor $PX \to$ Type, $x \mapsto \mathrm{Or}^f_x$ (`orFunctorMap`, `orFunctorMap_id`, `orFunctorMap_comp`); the uniqueness needs (∗) only on a family of such open sets covering $X_\infty$ (`orFunctorMap_unique_of_cover`).

items.title: Definition 6.6.16 (preprint 6.40): orientations of sc-Fredholm sections

book.statement: An orientation of $f$ assigns to every smooth $y$ an orientation $o^f_y$ of $\mathrm{DET}(f, y)$ such that, for every smooth $x$ and every orientable neighbourhood $U(x)$, the restriction to $U_\infty$ is one of the two continuous orientations.

items.title: Theorem 6.6.18 (preprint 6.41): the natural orientation of the solution set

book.label: §6.6 (preprint §6.5), Theorem 6.6.18 (preprint 6.41) and its proof, preprint p. 229; the paragraph after it, pp. 274–276 (preprint pp. 229–230)
book.statement: Over a tame $X$, for a proper sc-Fredholm section $f$ with $(f, x)$ in general position to $\partial X$ at every zero and an orientation $o^f$ of $f$, the solution set $S = f^{-1}(0)$ is a smooth compact manifold with boundary with corners with a natural orientation. Proof: $T_xS = \ker f'(x)$ is oriented by $o^f_x$ since $f'(x)$ is onto, and the local prolongation of this orientation on $S$ is the Fredholm one. For $f$ not generic, a small perturbation $s$ supported near the zero set orients $S_{f+s}$.

lean.statement: `theorem_6_41_solutionSet` ($X$ tame, $f$ with tame germ data, `StrongBundle.IsProper`, general position (Definition 5.3.9 (preprint 5.17)) at every zero): $S$ is compact, a smooth submanifold in general position with the induced structure of a tame manifold with boundary with corners (the conclusions of Theorem 5.3.10 (preprint 5.18); Lemma 4.2.8 (preprint 4.19) for good position, `MPolyfold.IsGeneralPositionAt.isGoodPositionAt`), and $T_xS = \ker f'(x)$ in a chart (`tangentSpace_solutionSet_eq_linKer`). At a zero, $f'(x)$ (`ChartPoint.linZero`) lies in $\mathrm{Lin}(f, x)$ and is onto (`ChartPoint.linZero_mem_linSet`, `ChartPoint.linZero_surjective`, `ChartPoint.map_ker_linZero`), so $o_x \in \mathrm{Or}^f_x$ gives a ray of $\det f'(x) \cong \lambda(\ker f'(x)) = \lambda(T_xS)$, the tangent orientation (`ChartPoint.tangentOr`, `tangentOrAt`). `theorem_6_41`: moreover, for an orientation $o$ of $f$ (Definition 6.6.16 (preprint 6.40)) and every sc-smooth path $\gamma$ of zeros in an orientable neighbourhood $V \subseteq U$, the kernels $\ker f'(\gamma_q)$ form a continuous family of subspaces (`tangentFamily`, `exists_tangentFamily`), and the tangent orientations of $o$ form an orientation of its line bundle (`isLineOrientation_tangentOr`, `isLineOrientation_tangentOr_of_isSectionOrientation`). The Fredholm side is the push-forward for the datum $S = 0$, $k = 0$ (`isStabKernels_zero`, `stabSign_of_surjective`, `stabRayEquiv_zero`), which along a path of zeros is the continuation between tangent orientations (`IsStabKernels.orRay_eq_tangentOr`, `ChartPoint.stabRayEquiv_eq_tangentOr`, `cont_tangentOr`).

chips: on $S$ as a manifold: gap G.67
diff: "A natural orientation" is read as the tangent orientations with their continuity along the sc-smooth paths of zeros in a chart, and "the local prolongation of the orientation on $S$ is the Fredholm one" as the identity of continuation and push-forward along such paths; intermediate points are reached by the paths $s \mapsto \gamma(t\kappa(s))$, which stay in $\gamma([0, t])$ (Findings, Chapter 6, item 91).

Not formalized: an orientation of $S$ as an abstract manifold, of its tangent bundle in the charts of the induced structure (gap G.67), the compatibility of the tangent orientations read in two charts at one zero (gap G.68), and the perturbation paragraph after the theorem, with $S_{f+s}$ and $\mathrm{Lin}(f + s, x) = \mathrm{Lin}(f, x)$ (gap G.69) (Findings, Chapter 6, items 92, 93).

Tame germ data is the standing hypothesis of Chapter 5; the orientation $o$ exists iff $f$ is orientable (V6.60). "Proper" is the text's hypothesis; the proof uses only the compactness of $S$, which for sc-Fredholm sections is equivalent to it (V5.10), so nothing of the hypothesis is lost (Findings, Chapter 6, item 90).

items.title: Remark 6.6.19 (preprint 6.42): the orientation over $X \times [0, 1]$, at a point

book.label: §6.6 (preprint §6.5), Remark 6.6.19 (preprint 6.42), p. 276 (preprint p. 230)
book.statement: For an oriented $(f, o)$ and an sc⁺-section $s$ of $Y \to X \times [0, 1]$, $\hat f(x, t) = f(x) + s(x, t)$ has a natural orientation from $o$ and the standard orientation of $[0, 1]$: for $L = (f - t)'(x)$ oriented by $h = (a_1 \wedge \dots \wedge a_n) \otimes (b_1 \wedge \dots \wedge b_l)^*$, the operator $\tilde L(a, b) = La$ on $T_{(x,t)}(X \times [0, 1])$ is oriented by $\tilde h = (a_1 \wedge \dots \wedge a_n \wedge e) \otimes (b_1 \wedge \dots \wedge b_l)^*$, $e$ the standard orientation of $[0, 1]$, and $\tilde L$ lies in the linearization space of $\hat f$ at $(x, t)$.

lean.statement: `extOp`: for Fredholm $L$, $\tilde L = L \oplus 0 : E \times \mathbb R \to F$ is Fredholm (`isFredholm_extOp`) with $\ker\tilde L = \ker L \times \mathbb R$ and $\operatorname{coker}\tilde L = \operatorname{coker}L$ (`finrank_ker_extOp`, `extE`, `range_extOp`, `extCoker`). `extDet`: $h \mapsto \tilde h$, $(a_1 \wedge \dots \wedge a_n) \otimes d^* \mapsto ((a_1, 0) \wedge \dots \wedge (a_n, 0) \wedge e) \otimes d^*$ with $e = (0, 1)$, an isomorphism $\det(L) \cong \det(\tilde L)$ (`extDet_wedge_tmul`); in local determinant charts its coordinate is $(-1)^{\dim F/R(P) + \dim\operatorname{coker}L}$ times a continuous nowhere-zero function (`coord_extDet`). `extDetN` $= (-1)^{\dim\operatorname{coker}L}$ `extDet` pulls continuous orientations back along $L \mapsto \tilde L$ (`coord_extDetN`, `isLineOrientation_extPull`, `LineOrientation.extPull`) and agrees with `extDet` for $L$ onto (`extDetN_eq_of_surjective`); `extConjOp`, `extConjDet`, `existsUnique_extConjOr`: the same after the swap of the factors. In charts: for $\hat f = \tilde f + S$, $\tilde f(t, y) = f(y)$, $S$ an sc⁺-section of $\pi^*P \to \mathbb R \times X$, and the product chart point (`ChartPoint.prodPt`, `ChartPoint.prodT`, `ChartPoint.prodK`), $\hat L(\sigma, v) = Lv$ (`ChartPoint.prodLin`) lies in $\mathrm{Lin}(\hat f, (t, x))$ for every $L \in \mathrm{Lin}(f, x)$ (`ChartPoint.prodLin_mem_linSet`, through the $t$-constant lift `constLift`); an orientation $o$ of $\mathrm{DET}(f, x)$ gives exactly one orientation $\hat o$ of $\mathrm{DET}(\hat f, (t, x))$ with $\hat o(\hat L)$ the image of $o(L)$ for **every** $L$ (`ChartPoint.existsUnique_prodOr`, `ChartPoint.prodOr`, `ChartPoint.prodOr_apply`), and $o \mapsto \hat o$ is injective (`ChartPoint.prodOr_injective`).

diff: As we read it, the literal $h \mapsto \tilde h$ is not continuous in $L$ where the parity of $\dim\operatorname{coker}L$ changes, so the orientation of $\mathrm{DET}(\hat f, (x, t))$ it defines could depend on the choice of $L$; the sign $(-1)^{\dim\operatorname{coker}L}$ (the sign of V6.40) is used, which agrees with the text's map when $L$ is onto (Findings, Chapter 6, item 95).

$X \times [0, 1]$ is read as $\mathbb R \times X$ (decision D2), with the parameter first, so $\tilde L(a, b) = La$ is conjugated by the swap of the factors. Only an orientation of $\mathrm{DET}(f, x)$ at the one point and $\mathrm{Lin}(f, x) \ne \emptyset$ (bump functions, V6.1) are used, not an orientation of $f$ (Findings, Chapter 6, item 96).

That $(t, y) \mapsto \hat o$ is an orientation of $\hat f$ in the sense of Definition 6.6.16 (preprint 6.40), built from an orientation of $f$, is not formalized (gap G.66; Findings, Chapter 6, item 97).

items.title: Definition 7.1.1 (2017: 7.1): groupoids, $\mathrm{mor}(x, y)$ and the orbit space $|X|$

book.label: §7.1, Definition 7.1.1 (2017: 7.1) and the paragraph after it, pp. 287–288 (2017 pp. 225–226)
book.statement:
A *groupoid* $X = (X, \mathbf X)$ is a small category consisting of the set $X$ of objects, denoted by $x$, and the set $\mathbf X$ of morphisms (arrows), which are assumed to be invertible, and the following five structure maps $(s, t, m, u, \iota)$. (1) The source and target maps $s, t : \mathbf X \to X$ assign to every morphism $\varphi : x \to y$ in $\mathbf X$ its source $s(\varphi) = x$ and its target $t(\varphi) = y$. (2) The associative multiplication (composition) map $m : \mathbf X\,{}_s{\times}_t\,\mathbf X \to \mathbf X$, $m(\varphi, \psi) = \varphi \circ \psi$, is defined on the fibered product $\mathbf X\,{}_s{\times}_t\,\mathbf X = \{(\varphi, \psi) \in \mathbf X \times \mathbf X \mid s(\varphi) = t(\psi)\}$, so that if $\psi : x \to z$ and $\varphi : z \to y$, then $\varphi \circ \psi : x \to y$. (3) For every object $x \in X$ there exists the unit morphism $1_x : x \to x$ in $\mathbf X$, a 2-sided unit for the composition: $\varphi \circ 1_x = \varphi$ and $1_x \circ \psi = \psi$ for all $\varphi, \psi \in \mathbf X$ satisfying $s(\varphi) = x = t(\psi)$; these define the unit map $u : X \to \mathbf X$, $u(x) = 1_x$. (4) For every morphism $\varphi : x \to y$ there exists the inverse morphism $\varphi^{-1} : y \to x$, a 2-sided inverse: $\varphi \circ \varphi^{-1} = 1_y$ and $\varphi^{-1} \circ \varphi = 1_x$; these define the inverse map $\iota : \mathbf X \to \mathbf X$, $\iota(\varphi) = \varphi^{-1}$.

After the definition: $\mathrm{mor}(x, y) \subset \mathbf X$ is the set of all morphisms $\varphi$ with $s(\varphi) = x$ and $t(\varphi) = y$. The *orbit space* $|X| = X/\sim$ is the quotient of the set of objects by the equivalence relation $x \sim y$ if and only if there exists a morphism $\varphi : x \to y$; the class of $x$ is $|x| := \{y \in X \mid y \sim x\}$, and $\pi : X \to |X|$, $\pi(x) = |x|$, is the quotient map.

lean.statement: `GroupoidStr Obj Mor`: types of objects and morphisms with the maps `src`, `tgt`, `comp`, `unit`, `inv` and the laws `src_comp`, `tgt_comp`, `comp_assoc` on composable pairs $s(\varphi) = t(\psi)$, `src_unit`, `tgt_unit`, `comp_unit` ($\varphi \circ 1_{s(\varphi)} = \varphi$), `unit_comp` ($1_{t(\varphi)} \circ \varphi = \varphi$), `src_inv`, `tgt_inv`, `comp_inv` ($\varphi \circ \varphi^{-1} = 1_{t(\varphi)}$), `inv_comp` ($\varphi^{-1} \circ \varphi = 1_{s(\varphi)}$) (fields of the structure). `mor x y` and `morOn A` (the morphisms with source and target in $A$) are sets of morphisms; `Isomorphic x y` is the existence of $\varphi : x \to y$, `orbitSetoid` the equivalence relation, `OrbitSpace` $= |X|$ its quotient and `π` the projection, with $\pi(x) = \pi(y) \iff x \sim y$ (`π_eq_π_iff`). `saturation A` $= \pi^{-1}(\pi(A))$, `IsSaturated A`, equivalent to: $s(\varphi) \in A \Rightarrow t(\varphi) \in A$ (`isSaturated_iff`). `Ob`, `instGroupoid`: the same data as a Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Groupoid`, whose isomorphism relation is `orbitSetoid` (`orbitSetoid_eq`).

diff: A structure of maps on types; the laws are required on the composable pairs $s(\varphi) = t(\psi)$, and the composition of a non-composable pair is a junk value, never used (Findings, Chapter 7, item 1).

Not in the definition: the saturation $\pi^{-1}(\pi(A))$, used from Definition 7.1.21 (2017: 7.10) on, and the bridge to Mathlib's `CategoryTheory.Groupoid`, so that "full" and "faithful" (2017 p. 232, Proposition 7.1.19 (2017: 7.6)) are Mathlib's `Functor.Full`, `Functor.Faithful`.

items.title: Definition 7.1.3 (2017: 7.3): ep-groupoids

book.label: §7.1, Definition 7.1.3 (2017: 7.3), pp. 288 ff. (2017 pp. 226–227)
book.statement: An *ep-groupoid* $X = (X, \mathbf X)$ consists of a groupoid equipped with M-polyfold structures on the object set $X$ and the morphism set $\mathbf X$ having the following properties. (1) (étale) The source and target maps $s, t : \mathbf X \to X$ are local sc-diffeomorphisms. (2) The unit map $u$ and the inverse map $\iota$ are sc-smooth. (3) (Properness) Every point $x \in X$ possesses an open neighborhood $V(x)$ of $x$ in $X$ such that the map $t : s^{-1}(\mathrm{cl}_X(V(x))) \to X$ is proper. Since $s$ is a local sc-diffeomorphism, the fibered product $\mathbf X\,{}_s{\times}_t\,\mathbf X$ is in a natural way an M-polyfold in view of Lemma 2.8 in [38], and we require (4) the multiplication map $m : \mathbf X\,{}_s{\times}_t\,\mathbf X \to \mathbf X$ is sc-smooth. In particular, all the structure maps $(s, t, m, u, \iota)$ are sc-smooth maps.

lean.statement: `EpGroupoid Obj Mor` extends `GroupoidStr` by M-polyfold structures `PObj`, `PMor` on the Hausdorff paracompact spaces $X$, $\mathbf X$ and the conditions (1) `isLocalScDiffeo_src`, `isLocalScDiffeo_tgt`; (2) `isScSmoothMap_unit`, `isScSmoothMap_inv`; (3) `exists_isProperMap`: every $x$ has an open $V \ni x$ such that $t : s^{-1}(\mathrm{cl}\,V) \to X$ is a proper map (Mathlib's `IsProperMap` of the restriction); (4) `isScSmoothComp`, i.e. `IsScSmoothComp`: $m$ is sc-smooth on $\mathbf X\,{}_s{\times}_t\,\mathbf X$ with the sub-M-polyfold structure of Part I (`MPolyfold.isSubMPolyfold_fibredProduct`). (4) is equivalent to the sheet form `IsScSmoothCompSheet`: for every sheet $\sigma$ of $s$ over $V$, $\psi \mapsto m(\sigma(t(\psi)), \psi)$ is sc-smooth on $t^{-1}(V)$ (`isScSmoothComp_iff_sheet`, `EpGroupoid.isScSmoothCompSheet`); $s$ and $t$ are sc-smooth (`isScSmoothMap_src`, `isScSmoothMap_tgt`).

diff: As for every M-polyfold of the project (Part I, Definition 2.3.4 (2017: 2.8)), $X$ and $\mathbf X$ are Hausdorff and paracompact (a standing hypothesis).

(3) is existential per point. The universal form "for every open $V \ni x$" does not hold for the pair groupoid of $\mathbb Z$, while every smaller open neighbourhood of a good one works (V7.4, V7.59) (Findings, Chapter 7, items 3, 103).

"Lemma 2.8 in [38]" cites the paper *A General Fredholm Theory III*, an external reference, not a misprint; its statement in the book is Part I's Proposition 2.5.20 (2017: 2.15; preprint 2.46), which the formalization uses. The proofs use the equivalent sheet form of (4) (Findings, Chapter 7, item 4).

items.title: Properness and its sequential form

book.label: §7.1, Definition 7.1.3 (3) (2017: 7.3), 2017 p. 227; used on pp. 292–346 (2017 pp. 230–254)
book.statement: Definition 7.1.3 (3) (2017: 7.3) asks that $t : s^{-1}(\mathrm{cl}_X(V(x))) \to X$ be proper. The proofs use this in the form: if $s(\varphi_k) \in \mathrm{cl}_X(V(x))$ and $t(\varphi_k)$ converges in $X$, then, "after perhaps taking a subsequence", $(\varphi_k)$ converges in $\mathbf X$ (Proposition 7.1.10 (2017: 7.3), 2017 p. 230; Lemma 7.1.11 (2017: 7.1), p. 292 (2017 p. 230); Proposition 7.1.22 (2017: 7.7), p. 307 (2017 p. 238); Proposition 7.3.9 (2017: 7.11), 2017 p. 248; Lemma 7.6.2 (2017: 7.8), 2017 p. 254), or through the compactness of preimages of compact sets (Proposition 7.5.9 (2017: 7.13), p. 342 (2017 p. 251)). items.title: Definition 7.1.4 (2017: 7.4): the local sc-diffeomorphism $\hat\varphi$ and the tangent $T\varphi$

book.label: §7.1, Definition 7.1.4 (2017: 7.4) and the paragraph before it, 2017 p. 227
book.statement: Since $s, t : \mathbf X \to X$ are local sc-diffeomorphisms, every morphism $\varphi : x \to y$ of an ep-groupoid has an extension to a local sc-diffeomorphism $\hat\varphi$ satisfying $\hat\varphi(x) = y$, defined as follows: there exist open neighborhoods $\mathbf U(\varphi) \subset \mathbf X$ and $U(x), U(y) \subset X$ such that $s : \mathbf U(\varphi) \to U(x)$ and $t : \mathbf U(\varphi) \to U(y)$ are sc-diffeomorphisms, and $\hat\varphi = t \circ (s|\mathbf U(\varphi))^{-1} : U(x) \to U(y)$. In the case that $\varphi$ is smooth, i.e. $\varphi \in \mathbf X_\infty$, there is an associated sc-isomorphism $T\varphi : T_{s(\varphi)}X \to T_{t(\varphi)}X$ defined by $T\varphi := T\hat\varphi(x)$; more generally $T\hat\varphi : TU(s(\varphi)) \to TU(t(\varphi))$. $T\varphi$ can be defined for $\varphi$ on level at least $1$ and gives a bounded linear isomorphism on level $0$; only in the case that $\varphi$ is smooth is $T\varphi$ an sc-operator. Definition 7.1.4 (2017: 7.4): associated to a smooth morphism $\varphi$ we have the so-called associated local sc-diffeomorphism $\hat\varphi$, as well as its tangent $T\varphi$.

lean.statement: `Sheet`: an open set `carrier` $= \mathbf U(\varphi)$ of morphisms with sc-diffeomorphisms $s : \mathbf U \to U(x)$ (`srcSet`) and $t : \mathbf U \to U(y)$ (`tgtSet`) and their inverses; every morphism lies in one (`exists_sheet`, `sheetAt`, `mem_sheetAt`). `Sheet.hat` $= t \circ (s|\mathbf U)^{-1}$ is an sc-diffeomorphism $U(x) \to U(y)$ with inverse $s \circ (t|\mathbf U)^{-1}$ (`Sheet.isScDiffeoOn_hat`); for a morphism, `hat φ` is that of `sheetAt φ`, an sc-diffeomorphism (`isScDiffeoOn_hat`) with $\hat\varphi(s(\varphi)) = t(\varphi)$ (`hat_src`). `tangentMor φ` defines $T\varphi$ on the tangent space of $X$ through a tangent vector of $\mathbf X$ at $\varphi$; no property of it is proved.

items.title: The levels of an ep-groupoid and the filtration of $|X|$

book.label: §7.1, pp. 289–291 (2017 pp. 227–228)
book.statement: The M-polyfolds $X$ and $\mathbf X$ are equipped with the filtrations $X = X_0 \supset X_1 \supset X_2 \supset \dots \supset X_\infty = \bigcap_{k \ge 0} X_k$ and similarly for $\mathbf X$; $X_\infty$ is dense in every $X_k$. For $x$ in the M-polyfold $X$, $ml(x) \in \mathbb N \cup \{\infty\}$ is the largest non-negative integer $m$, or $\infty$, such that $x \in X_m$. Since the source and target maps are local sc-diffeomorphisms and therefore preserve the levels, $ml(x) = ml(y) = ml(\varphi)$ for every morphism $\varphi : x \to y$; consequently the filtration of $X$ induces the filtration $|X| = |X_0| \supset |X_1| \supset \dots \supset |X_\infty| = \bigcap_{k \ge 0}|X_k|$ of the orbit space. The degeneracy indices $d_X : X \to \mathbb N$ and $d_{\mathbf X} : \mathbf X \to \mathbb N$ are invariant under local sc-diffeomorphisms (Proposition 2.4.4 (2017: 2.7)), so $d_X(s(\varphi)) = d_{\mathbf X}(\varphi) = d_X(t(\varphi))$ for every morphism $\varphi$; in particular $d_X(x) = d_X(x')$ if $x \sim x'$.

lean.statement: `mem_levelSet_src_iff`, `mem_levelSet_tgt_iff`: $s(\varphi) \in X_m \iff \varphi \in \mathbf X_m \iff t(\varphi) \in X_m$. `MPolyfold.maxLevel` is $ml$, preserved by local sc-diffeomorphisms (`MPolyfold.IsLocalScDiffeo.maxLevel_eq`), as is the degeneracy index (`MPolyfold.IsLocalScDiffeo.degIndex_eq`), so $d_{\mathbf X}(\varphi) = d_X(s(\varphi)) = d_X(t(\varphi))$ (`degIndex_src`, `degIndex_tgt`). `orbitLevel k` $= \pi(X_k) = |X_k|$.

The density of $X_\infty$ in every $X_k$, which the text states without proof, is not formalized; Part I proves it only for sc-Banach spaces, not for M-polyfolds (gap G.73) (Findings, Chapter 7, items 112, 116).
Proposition 2.4.4 (2017: 2.7) is the preprint's Proposition 2.24.

items.title: Theorem 7.1.13 (2017: 7.1): the natural representation of $G_x$

items.title: Proposition 7.1.15 (2017: 7.5): natural representations of finitely many isomorphic objects

book.label: §7.1, Proposition 7.1.15 (2017: 7.5), pp. 297–298 (2017 pp. 233–234) (proof pp. 297–305 (2017 pp. 234–236))
book.statement: Let $(X, \mathbf X)$ be an ep-groupoid and $Y = \{y_1, \dots, y_k\}$ a finite set of distinct objects in $X$ which are mutually isomorphic. Denote by $\mathbf Y = (Y, \mathbf Y)$ the full subcategory associated with $Y$, whose morphism set is $\mathbf Y$. Then, given a neighborhood $V$ of $Y$ in $X$, there exists a functor $f$, which associates with the objects $y$ in $Y$ mutually disjoint connected open neighborhoods $U(y)$ contained in $V$, and with a morphism $\psi : y \to y'$ in $\mathbf Y$ an sc-diffeomorphism $f(\psi) : U(y) \to U(y')$. The set of morphisms $\mathbf U = \{\varphi \in \mathbf X \mid s(\varphi) \text{ and } t(\varphi) \in \bigcup_{y \in Y}U(y)\}$ decomposes into the union of connected components $\mathbf U(\psi)$, $\psi \in \mathbf Y$, and the following holds true. (1) The isotropy group $G_y$ for $y \in Y$ acts via the natural action on $U(y)$. (2) For $\psi \in \mathbf Y$ the maps $s : \mathbf U(\psi) \to U(y)$ and $t : \mathbf U(\psi) \to U(y)$ are sc-diffeomorphisms. (3) If $\psi : y \to y'$ and $z \in U(y)$, then $f(\psi)(z) = t \circ (s|\mathbf U(\psi))^{-1}(z)$.

book.label: §7.1, Proposition 7.1.19 (2017: 7.6), p. 304 (2017 p. 236) (proof pp. 299–306 (2017 pp. 236–237))
book.statement: Let $X$ be an ep-groupoid and $z \in |X|$. We fix $x \in X$ satisfying $z = |x|$, denote the isotropy group of $x$ by $G_x$ and take an open neighborhood $U(x)$ of $x$ on which we have the natural $G_x$-action $\Phi$, which we abbreviate as $g \ast y := \Phi(g)(y)$ for $g \in G_x$ and $y \in U(x)$. items.title: The subgroup $T_x$ of the elements acting trivially

book.statement: Given an ep-groupoid $X$, an object $x_0 \in X$, and an open neighborhood $V \subset X$ of $x_0$. items.title: The proof of Theorem 7.5.7 (2017: 7.4)

book.label: §7.6.2 (2017 §7.5.2), proof of Theorem 7.5.7 (2017: 7.4), pp. 346–347 (2017 pp. 255–256)
book.statement: Consider the open covering $(|U_\lambda|)_{\lambda \in \Lambda}$ of $|X|$. For every $x \in X$ take an open neighborhood $V(x)$ with: (1) there exists an open neighborhood $W(x)$ equipped with the natural $G_x$-action such that $V(x) \subset \mathrm{cl}_X(V(x)) \subset W(x)$ and $V(x)$ is invariant; (2) $t : s^{-1}(\mathrm{cl}_X(V(x))) \to X$ is proper; (3) there exists a $\lambda$ with $V(x) \subset U_\lambda$; (4) $(\pi^{-1}(|V(x)|) \setminus V(x)) \cap W(x) = \emptyset$. Take a locally finite refinement $(V'_i)_{i \in I}$ of $(|V(x)|)_{x \in X}$, with $V'_i \subset |V(x_i)|$, open $V''_i$ with $V''_i \subset \mathrm{cl}_{|X|}(V''_i) \subset V'_i$ and $|X| = \bigcup_i V''_i$; $U''_i = V(x_i) \cap \pi^{-1}(V''_i)$ is invariant under the $G_{x_i}$-action, with saturation $U_i = \pi^{-1}(V''_i)$. Take a continuous partition of unity $(\beta_i)$ subordinate to $(V''_i)$; $(\beta_i \circ \pi)|V(x_i)$ has support in $U''_i \subset V(x_i)$. Using the sc-smooth partitions of unity of $X$, approximate $(\beta_i \circ \pi)|V(x_i)$ by Lemma 7.6.5 (2017: 7.10) by an sc-smooth $f_i$ supported in $V(x_i)$ with $f_i \ge (\beta_i \circ \pi)|V(x_i)$; average using the $G_{x_i}$-action, extend to the saturation of $V(x_i)$ and then by $0$ outside, which gives a function $h_i$ compatible with morphisms. The sum $h$ of all $h_i$ is locally finite and always bigger than $0$, and $(h_i/h)$ is the desired partition of unity for the ep-groupoid $X$.

book.statement: (7.3): an open neighbourhood $W(x)$ and, for $g \in G_x$, open neighbourhoods $U^s(g)$, $U^t(g)$ of $g$ on which $s_g = s|U^s(g)$ and $t_g = t|U^t(g)$ are sc-diffeomorphisms onto $W(x)$. items.title: The tangent data (8.1)–(8.9): $T(X, \mathbf X)$ and its structure maps

book.label: §8.1, (8.1)–(8.9), pp. 357–359 (2017 pp. 257–258)
book.statement: The tangent of the ep-groupoid $(X, \mathbf X)$ is the pair $T(X, \mathbf X) = (TX, T\mathbf X)$ (8.1), to be equipped with the structure of an ep-groupoid with object M-polyfold $TX$ and morphism M-polyfold $T\mathbf X$. A tangent vector $(\varphi, h) \in T_\varphi\mathbf X$ is viewed as a morphism $(\varphi, h) : Ts(\varphi)(h) \to Tt(\varphi)(h)$ (8.2), so that $s_{T\mathbf X}(\varphi, h) = Ts(\varphi)(h)$ and $t_{T\mathbf X}(\varphi, h) = Tt(\varphi)(h)$ (8.3). If $s_{T\mathbf X}(\psi, k) = Ts(\psi)(k) = Tt(\varphi)(h) = t_{T\mathbf X}(\varphi, h)$ (8.4), which implies $s(\psi) = t(\varphi)$, the multiplication is $(\psi, k) \circ (\varphi, h) = (\psi \circ \varphi, Ts(\psi \circ \varphi)^{-1}(Ts(\varphi)(h))) \in T_{\varphi \circ \psi}\mathbf X$ (8.5), where $k = Ts(\psi)^{-1}(Tt(\varphi)(h))$; with the projection $\mathbf p : T\mathbf X \to \mathbf X^1$, shorter, $k \circ h = Ts(\mathbf p(k) \circ \mathbf p(h))^{-1}Ts(\mathbf p(h))(h)$ (8.6). The unit at $a \in T_xX$ is $1_a = (1_x, h_a)$ with $Ts(1_x)(h_a) = a = Tt(1_x)(h_a)$ (8.7), so $u_{T\mathbf X}(a) = (1_x, Ts(1_x)^{-1}(a))$ (8.8), and the inverse map is $\iota_{T\mathbf X}(\varphi, k) = (\varphi^{-1}, T\iota_X(\varphi)(k))$ (8.9).

lean.statement: `tSrc` $= Ts$, `tTgt` $= Tt$, `tUnit` $= Tu$ and `tInv` $= T\iota$ are Part I's tangent maps (`MPolyfold.tangentMap`) of the structure maps, and `tBase` $= \mathbf p$ is the base point (`MPolyfold.tangentProj`). `tComp k h` is defined by choice: if $Ts(k) = Tt(h)$ (then $s(\mathbf p(k)) = t(\mathbf p(h))$, `src_tBase_eq`), it is the vector over $\mathbf p(k) \circ \mathbf p(h)$ with $Ts(k \circ h) = Ts(h)$ (`tComp_spec`, `tBase_tComp`, `tSrc_tComp`), which exists (`exists_tSrc_eq`) and is unique, since two vectors with the same base point and the same image under $Ts$ are equal (`tangent_ext`); `tComp_eq` characterizes it, which is (8.5). `tUnit_eq`: $Tu(a)$ is the vector over $1_x$ with $Ts(Tu(a)) = a$, which is (8.8).

book.statement: If the ep-groupoid $(X, \mathbf X)$ is tame, so is the ep-groupoid $(TX, T\mathbf X)$. (Proof: if $\varphi : U \to O$, $O = (O, C, E)$, is a tame chart of the object M-polyfold and $O = r(U) \subset C$ a tame retract, then $Tr : TU \to TU$ is also a tame retraction; so $TX$ has a tame object space.)

lean.statement: `ScRetraction.IsTameWith.tangent`, `ScRetraction.IsTame.tangentRetraction`: the tangent $Tr$ of a tame retraction is tame, proved for one presentation of $TC$ (`ScIso.tangentPres`, `tangentSet_eq_tangentPres`, `degIndex_tangentSet`, `mem_minimalSubspaceWith_tangentPres`) with the derivatives `ScRetraction.scDeriv_tangentRetraction_fst`, `ScRetraction.scDeriv_tangentRetraction_inr`, and passed to every presentation (`ScRetraction.IsTameWith.isTame`). `IsTameRetract.tangent`, `MPolyfold.IsTame.tangent`: the tangent of a tame retract and of a tame M-polyfold is tame. `lemma_8_8`: if $X$ is tame, so is $TX$. `isTame_tangentEpGroupoid_trivial_rn`: the tangent of the trivial ep-groupoid of $\mathbb R^n$ is tame.

items.title: Remark 8.1.10 (2017: 8.1): the morphisms of $T\mathbf X$ as pairs $(T\varphi, a)$

book.label: §8.1, Remark 8.1.10 (2017: 8.1), pp. 364 ff. (2017 pp. 264–265)
book.statement: There are equivalent ways to turn $T\mathbf X$ into an ep-groupoid. A morphism $\varphi : x \to y$ with $x \in X_1$ has a well-defined associated linear isomorphism $T\varphi : T_xX \to T_yY$, the tangent map of $t \circ (s|\mathbf U(\varphi))^{-1}$ at $x$; $(T\varphi, h)$ is a morphism from $h$ to $T\varphi(h)$, and $(T\psi, h) \circ (T\varphi, l) = (T\psi \circ T\varphi, l) = (T(\psi \circ \varphi), l)$ for $h = T\varphi(l)$. The map $G : (\varphi, h) \mapsto (T\varphi, Ts(h))$ is compatible with the functorial structures, and $G : T\mathbf X \to \{(T\varphi, a) \mid \varphi \in \mathbf X_1, a \in T_{s(\varphi)}X\}$ is a bijection; the right-hand side can be given an M-polyfold structure making $G$ an sc-diffeomorphism, and the pairs $(T\varphi, a)$ can be identified with the triples $(a, T\varphi, b)$, $b = T\varphi(a)$. Finally, $Tt(\varphi) \circ Ts(\varphi)^{-1} : T_xX \to T_yX$ is the linearization of $t \circ (s|\mathbf U(\varphi))^{-1}$ at $\varphi$, hence equal to $T\varphi$, and $t_{T\mathbf X} \circ (s_{T\mathbf X}|T_xX)^{-1} = T\varphi : T_xX \to T_yX$ is a linear isomorphism.

lean.statement: $T\varphi$ is Chapter 7's `tangentMor` (V7.5) and $G$ is `remarkG`, $G(v) = (\mathbf p(v), Ts(v))$. `remark_8_1`: $T\varphi(Ts(v)) = Tt(v)$ for every $v$ over $\varphi$, i.e. $t_T \circ (s_T|T_\varphi\mathbf X)^{-1} = T\varphi$ (`tangentMor_tSrc`); $T(\psi \circ \varphi) = T\psi \circ T\varphi$ on $T_{s(\varphi)}X$ for $\varphi \in \mathbf X_1$ (`tangentMor_comp`); $G$ is injective, with range the pairs $(\varphi, a)$ with $\varphi \in \mathbf X_1$ and $a \in T_{s(\varphi)}X$; $Ts(k) = Tt(h)$ iff $Ts(k) = T\mathbf p(h)(Ts(h))$; and $G(k \circ h) = (\mathbf p(k) \circ \mathbf p(h), Ts(h))$ with $T(\mathbf p(k) \circ \mathbf p(h)) = T\mathbf p(k) \circ T\mathbf p(h)$, so that $G$ is compatible with the compositions.

diff: **Narrower.** The first entry of $G$ is read as $T\varphi$ labelled by $\varphi$, i.e. as $\varphi$ itself: as a bare map, $(\varphi, h) \mapsto (T\varphi, Ts(h))$ need not be injective (Findings, Chapter 8, item 10).

Not formalized: that $T\varphi$ and $t_T \circ (s_T|T_xX)^{-1}$ are linear isomorphisms, and that $T\varphi = T\hat\varphi(x)$ (gaps G.7, G.70); the M-polyfold structure transported along $G$ and the triples $(a, T\varphi, b)$, which have no gap since nothing depends on them. The well-definedness and functoriality of $T\varphi$ close gap G.70 in part (Findings, Chapter 8, items 112, 113).
The remark writes "$T\varphi : T_xX \to T_yY$" for $T_yX$, and calls $T\varphi$ the linearization "at $x$" and later "at $\varphi$" (possible misprints).

items.title: Theorem 8.1.11 (2017: 8.2): the tangent of an sc-smooth functor

book.label: §8.1, Theorem 8.1.11 (2017: 8.2) and its proof, pp. 365–367 (2017 pp. 265–266)
book.statement: If $(\Phi, \boldsymbol\Phi) : (X, \mathbf X) \to (Y, \mathbf Y)$ is an sc-smooth functor between two ep-groupoids, then the tangent map $(T\Phi, T\boldsymbol\Phi) : T(X, \mathbf X) \to T(Y, \mathbf Y)$ is an sc-smooth functor between the tangent ep-groupoids. (Proof: $T\Phi$ and $T\boldsymbol\Phi$ are sc-smooth; differentiating $\boldsymbol\Phi(m_X(\psi, \varphi)) = m_Y(\boldsymbol\Phi(\psi), \boldsymbol\Phi(\varphi))$ and using Lemma 8.1.2 (2017: 8.1) gives $T\boldsymbol\Phi(\psi \circ \varphi)(k \circ h) = (T\boldsymbol\Phi(\psi)(k)) \circ (T\boldsymbol\Phi(\varphi)(h))$; that $T\Phi$ preserves the units is left to the reader; differentiating $s(\boldsymbol\Phi(\alpha)) = \Phi(s(\alpha))$ and $t(\boldsymbol\Phi(\alpha)) = \Phi(t(\alpha))$ gives the compatibility with sources and targets.)

lean.statement: `EpFunctor.tangent` is $(T\Phi, T\boldsymbol\Phi)$, an ep-functor $T(X, \mathbf X) \to T(Y, \mathbf Y)$. `theorem_8_2`: its maps are Part I's tangent maps of $\Phi$ and $\boldsymbol\Phi$, sc-smooth, compatible with the sources and targets, with the composition of composable pairs, and with the units.

chips: units, left to the reader, proved
diff: As in the text; the compatibility with the composition comes from the injectivity of $Ts$ on the fibres rather than from differentiating the identity, and the units, left to the reader, are proved (Findings, Chapter 8, items 4, 11).

items.title: Theorem 8.1.12 (2017: 8.3): the functor $T : \mathcal{EP} \to \mathcal{EP}$

book.label: §8.1, Theorem 8.1.12 (2017: 8.3), p. 366 (2017 p. 266)
book.statement: The tangent gives rise to a functor $T : \mathcal{EP} \to \mathcal{EP}$, associating with an ep-groupoid $X$ its tangent $TX$ and with a smooth functor $\Phi : X \to Y$ the tangent functor $T\Phi$. In particular, $T\Phi$ preserves the composition and the other structure maps. Furthermore, $T$ preserves tameness: if $X$ is a tame ep-groupoid, so is $TX$.

lean.statement: `EP.tangent`, `tangentFunctor`: a functor `EP.{max u 1} ⥤ EP.{max u 1}` on Chapter 7's category $\mathcal{EP}$ (V7.9). `theorem_8_3`: it maps $A$ to its `tangentEpGroupoid` and $\Phi$ to `EpFunctor.tangent` $\Phi$, and preserves identities and composites. `theorem_8_3_tame`: $TA$ is tame if $A$ is.

diff: A functor on the ep-groupoids in `Type (max u 1)`, since $TX$ lives there for $X$ in `Type u`; the functor laws are Part I's chain rule, and the tameness sentence is `theorem_8_3_tame` (Findings, Chapter 8, items 2, 11).

items.title: Definition 8.1.13 (2017: 8.1): natural transformations and natural equivalence

book.label: §8.1, Definition 8.1.13 (2017: 8.1), p. 367 (2017 p. 266)
book.statement: If $F, G : X \to Y$ are two sc-smooth functors between the ep-groupoids $X$ and $Y$, then $F$ is naturally equivalent to $G$, $F \simeq G$, if there exists an sc-smooth map $\tau : X \to \mathbf Y$ which associates with every object $x \in X$ a morphism $\tau(x) : F(x) \to G(x)$ in $\mathbf Y$ such that $\tau(x') \circ F(h) = G(h) \circ \tau(x)$ for every morphism $h : x \to x'$ in $\mathbf X$. The sc-smooth map $\tau$ is called a natural transformation $\tau : F \to G$.

lean.statement: `EpNatTrans F G`: a map `app` $: X \to \mathbf Y$, sc-smooth, with $s(\tau(x)) = F(x)$, $t(\tau(x)) = G(x)$ and $\tau(t(h)) \circ F(h) = G(h) \circ \tau(s(h))$ for every morphism $h$ (fields of the structure). `EpFunctor.NaturallyEquivalent F G`: a natural transformation $F \to G$ exists.

diff: As in the text (Findings, Chapter 8, item 12).

book.statement: The relation $F \simeq G$ between sc-smooth functors $F, G : X \to Y$ of ep-groupoids is an equivalence relation. (Stated without proof.)

lean.statement: `EpNatTrans.refl`, `EpNatTrans.symm` ($x \mapsto \tau(x)^{-1}$), `EpNatTrans.trans` ($x \mapsto \tau'(x) \circ \tau(x)$, sc-smooth by `EpNatTrans.isScSmoothMap_comp_app`); `EpFunctor.NaturallyEquivalent.refl`, `.symm`, `.trans`, and `naturallyEquivalent_equivalence`: $\simeq$ is an `Equivalence`. Not in the text: whiskering (`EpNatTrans.whiskerLeft`, `EpNatTrans.whiskerRight`), and $\simeq$ is preserved by composition on either side (`NaturallyEquivalent.comp_left`, `NaturallyEquivalent.comp_right`).

items.title: Proposition 8.1.14 (2017: 8.1): the tangent of a natural transformation

book.label: §8.1, Proposition 8.1.14 (2017: 8.1) and its proof, pp. 367–372 (2017 pp. 267–268)
book.statement: If $\tau : \Phi \to \Psi$ is a natural transformation between two sc-smooth functors $\Phi, \Psi : X = (X, \mathbf X) \to Y = (Y, \mathbf Y)$ between ep-groupoids, then the tangent $T\tau : TX \to T\mathbf Y$ is a natural transformation $T\tau : T\Phi \to T\Psi$ between the two tangent functors $T\Phi, T\Psi : (TX, T\mathbf X) \to (TY, T\mathbf Y)$. (Proof: differentiating $\Phi(x) = s(\tau(x))$ and $\Psi(x) = t(\tau(x))$ shows that $T\tau(x_0)(h)$ is a morphism $T\Phi(x_0)(h) \to T\Psi(x_0)(h)$; differentiating the naturality square along the morphisms $\alpha$ near $\alpha_0$ gives the naturality of $T\tau$.)

lean.statement: `EpNatTrans.tangent`: Part I's tangent $T\tau$ of $\tau$ is a natural transformation $T\Phi \to T\Psi$. `proposition_8_1`: there is a natural transformation $T\Phi \to T\Psi$ whose map is $T\tau$, and $\Phi \simeq \Psi$ implies $T\Phi \simeq T\Psi$.

diff: As in the text; the naturality comes from the injectivity of $Ts$ on the fibres instead of differentiating the naturality square (Findings, Chapter 8, items 4, 13).
The proof has "$T\tau(x_0(h))$" (possible misprint), and labels the lower arrow of the last diagram $T\tau(x_0)h$ for $T\tau(x_0')h'$ (possible misprint or extraction artefact).

items.title: Theorem 8.1.15 (2017: 8.4): the orbit space $|TX|$

book.label: §8.1, Theorem 8.1.15 (2017: 8.4) and its proof, 2017 p. 268
book.statement: If $X$ is an ep-groupoid with paracompact orbit space $|X|$, then the tangent ep-groupoid $TX$ has a paracompact orbit space $|TX|$ as well. (Proof: $|X^1|$ is paracompact; for $z \in |X^1|$ with representative $x_z$ take $U(x_z)$ with the natural $G_{x_z}$-action such that $TU(x_z)$ is, as a bundle over $U(x_z)_1$, sc-isomorphic to a local bundle model $TO \to O^1$ with an sc-smooth bundle action of $G_{x_z}$; then $|TU(x_z)|$ and $|U(x_z)_1|$ are metrizable. A locally finite closed subcover $(A_z)$ of $(|U(x_z)_1|)$ gives a locally finite covering $(\tilde A_z)$ of $|TX|$ by closed paracompact sets, and $|TX|$, a regular Hausdorff space, is paracompact by the topological Proposition 2.7.4 (2017: 2.17).)

lean.statement: `theorem_8_4`: if $|X|$ is paracompact, so is $|TX|$; `metrizableSpace_tangent_orbitSpace`: $|TX|$ is then **metrizable**. The proof: the map $|p| : |TX| \to |X^1|$ (`tangentOrbitProj`, `continuous_tangentOrbitProj`, `preimage_tangentOrbitProj_image`); for a natural representation, the action of $G_x$ on $TU(x)$ (`NaturalRep.tangentU`, `NaturalRep.tΦ`, `NaturalRep.isScDiffeoOn_tΦ`, `NaturalRep.tangentMulAction`, `NaturalRep.tΓ`, `NaturalRep.tangent_π_eq_iff`), the open embedding $G_x\backslash TU(x) \to |TX|$ (`NaturalRep.isOpenEmbedding_tangentOrbitQuotientMap`, `NaturalRep.range_tangentOrbitQuotientMap`), the metrizable $|TU(x)| = |p|^{-1}(|U(x)_1|)$ (`NaturalRep.image_tangentU_eq_preimage`, `NaturalRep.metrizableSpace_image_tangentU`, `NaturalRep.metrizableSpace_image_liftU`), and Smirnov's theorem pulled back along $|p|$ (Part I's `metrizableSpace_of_pullback`). `hasParacompactOrbitSpace_tangent_trivial`: the tangent of the trivial ep-groupoid of an M-polyfold.

diff: **Stronger**: $|TX|$ is metrizable. The proof differs from the text's: Smirnov's theorem pulled back along $|p| : |TX| \to |X^1|$, as for Proposition 7.5.3 (2017: 7.12) (V7.54); the closed paracompact $\tilde A_z$, the regularity of $|TX|$ and Part I's Proposition 2.7.4 (2017: 2.17; preprint 2.57) are not used (Findings, Chapter 8, item 20).

The open embedding $G_x\backslash TU(x) \to |TX|$, left implicit, is proved. The local bundle model $TO \to O^1$ is not used, and the linearity of the action of $G_x$ on $TU(x)$ is not formalized (gap G.7) (Findings, Chapter 8, items 21, 104).

items.title: Strong bundle maps over M-polyfolds and the pull-back along $s$

book.label: §8.3, 2017 p. 270; used in Definitions 8.3.1–8.3.3 and 8.5.9 (2017: 8.4–8.6 and 8.10), pp. 373–396 (2017 pp. 270–285)
book.statement: Not stated as such. Definitions 8.3.1–8.3.3 and 8.5.9 (2017: 8.4–8.6 and 8.10) use strong bundle maps between strong bundles over M-polyfolds, and the fibred product $\mathbf X\,{}_s{\times}_P\,W = \{(\psi, w) \in \mathbf X \times W \mid s(\psi) = P(w)\}$, which, $s$ being a local sc-diffeomorphism, is an M-polyfold and, as the pull-back of a strong M-polyfold bundle, a strong bundle $\pi_1 : \mathbf X\,{}_s{\times}_P\,W \to \mathbf X$ (2017 p. 270). Part I defines strong bundle maps only between local models (its Definition 2.6.1 (2017: 2.22), the preprint's Definition 2.47) and the pull-back in its Proposition 2.6.8 (2017: 2.16; preprint 2.54).

items.title: Definition 8.3.1 (2017: 8.4): strong bundles over ep-groupoids

book.label: §8.3, Definition 8.3.1 (2017: 8.4), p. 375 (2017 p. 271)
book.statement: A strong bundle over the ep-groupoid $X$ is a pair $(P, \mu)$ in which $P : W \to X$ is a strong bundle over the object M-polyfold $X$ and $\mu : \mathbf X\,{}_s{\times}_P\,W \to W$ is a strong bundle map covering the target map $t : \mathbf X \to X$, so that $P \circ \mu(\psi, w) = t(\psi)$, such that (1) $\mu$ is a surjective local sc-diffeomorphism and linear on the fibres $W_x$; (2) $\mu(1_x, w) = w$ for all $x \in X$ and $w \in W_x$; (3) $\mu(\psi \circ \gamma, w) = \mu(\psi, \mu(\gamma, w))$ for all $\psi, \gamma \in \mathbf X$ and $w \in W$ with $s(\gamma) = P(w)$ and $t(\gamma) = s(\psi) = P(\mu(\gamma, w))$.

lean.statement: `EpStrongBundle X B`, for Part I's strong bundle `B` over the object M-polyfold: the map `μ` on Part I's pull-back $\mathbf X\,{}_s{\times}_P\,W$ (`pullbackSpace`), a strong bundle map covering $t$ in the sense of V8.19 (`isStrongBundleMap`, which contains the linearity on the fibres), `surjective`, a local sc-diffeomorphism on level $[0]$ (`isLocalScDiffeo`), with `μ_unit`: $\mu(1_x, w) = w$ (through `EpGroupoid.unitPair`) and `μ_comp`: (3) (fields of the structure). `P_μ`: $P \circ \mu = t \circ \pi_1$; `continuous_μ`. `EpStrongBundle.trivial`: every strong bundle over an M-polyfold is one over its trivial ep-groupoid, with $\mu(z, w) = w$.

diff: On Part I's pull-back strong bundle, with the strong bundle maps of V8.19. The surjectivity in (1) is kept as a field, although it follows from (2) (Findings, Chapter 8, items 32, 102).

items.title: The fibre maps $\mu(\psi, \cdot) : W_x \to W_y$

book.label: §8.3, after Definition 8.3.1 (2017: 8.4), p. 375 (2017 p. 271)
book.statement: Given a strong bundle $(P, \mu)$ over the ep-groupoid $X$, $\mu(\psi, \cdot) : W_x \to W_y$ is a linear isomorphism if $\psi : x \to y$ is a morphism in $\mathbf X$; the data of a strong bundle over an ep-groupoid prescribe how to lift morphisms to linear isomorphisms compatibly with compositions.

lean.statement: `fiberMor ψ` is $\mu(\psi, \cdot) : W_{s(\psi)} \to W_{t(\psi)}$ (`fiberMor_apply`), additive and homogeneous (`μ_add`, `μ_smul`), with inverse $\mu(\psi^{-1}, \cdot)$ (`μ_inv_μ`, `μ_μ_inv`). `fiberMorEquiv ψ`: a **topological** linear isomorphism $W_{s(\psi)} \simeq W_{t(\psi)}$ (Mathlib's `≃L[ℝ]`).

items.title: The functorial picture: the ep-groupoid $(W, \mathbf W)$

book.label: §8.3, after Definition 8.3.1 (2017: 8.4), pp. 375–377 (2017 pp. 271–272)
book.statement: With $\mathbf W = \mathbf X\,{}_s{\times}_P\,W$ one defines the ep-groupoid $\mathcal W = (W, \mathbf W)$: $s_{\mathbf W}(\psi, w) = w$ and $t_{\mathbf W}(\psi, w) = \mu(\psi, w)$, fibrewise linear local sc-diffeomorphisms covering $s_X$, $t_X$; the identity at $w \in W_x$ is $(1_x, w)$, the inverse of $(\psi, w)$ is $(\psi^{-1}, \mu(\psi, w))$, and $(\psi, w') \circ (\gamma, w) = (\psi \circ \gamma, w)$ whenever $w' = \mu(\gamma, w)$. The projections $P : W \to X$ and $\mathbf P := \pi_1 : \mathbf W \to \mathbf X$ define an sc-smooth functor $(P, \mathbf P) : (W, \mathbf W) \to (X, \mathbf X)$, and, since the orbit of $w$ covers the orbit of $P(w)$, $P$ induces a surjective continuous map $|P| : |W| \to |X|$.

lean.statement: `toGroupoidStr`, with `morInv` and `morComp` (`morComp_val`: $(\psi, w') \circ (\gamma, w) = (\psi \circ \gamma, w)$; `μ_morComp`), is the groupoid, and `toEpGroupoid` an ep-groupoid on $W$ and `pullbackSpace`, with the properness property (`exists_isProperMap_tgt`) and (4) in sheet form (`isScSmoothCompSheet_toGroupoidStr`). `isStrongBundleMap_src`, `isStrongBundleMap_tgt`: $s_{\mathbf W}$, $t_{\mathbf W}$ are strong bundle maps covering $s$, $t$. `projFunctor`: $(P, \pi_1)$ is an ep-functor. `exists_isomorphic_of_isomorphic`, `surjective_orbitMap_projFunctor`, `continuous_orbitMap_projFunctor`: $|P|$ is surjective and continuous.

items.title: Definition 8.3.2 (2017: 8.5): strong bundle maps over ep-groupoids

book.label: §8.3, Definition 8.3.2 (2017: 8.5) and the paragraph after it, 2017 p. 273
book.statement: Let $(P : W \to X, \mu)$ and $(P' : W' \to X', \mu')$ be strong bundles over ep-groupoids. A strong bundle map (or strong bundle functor) between them consists of a strong bundle map $\Phi : W \to W'$ covering an sc-smooth functor $\varphi : X \to X'$ between ep-groupoids such that $\Phi(\mu(\gamma, w)) = \mu'(\varphi(\gamma), \Phi(w))$ for all $\gamma \in \mathbf X$ and $w \in W$ with $s(\gamma) = P(w)$. (The relation is well defined, since $\varphi$ maps $\gamma : s(\gamma) \to t(\gamma)$ to $\varphi(\gamma) : \varphi(s(\gamma)) \to \varphi(t(\gamma))$.)

lean.statement: `EpStrongBundle.IsMap E E' ϕ Φ`: $\Phi$ is a strong bundle map (V8.19) covering the object map of the ep-functor $\phi$ (`isStrongBundleMap`), and $\Phi(\mu(\gamma, w)) = \mu'(\phi(\gamma), \Phi(w))$ whenever $P(w) = s(\gamma)$ (`map_μ`) (fields of the structure). `isMap_id`: the identity is one.

diff: As in the text (Findings, Chapter 8, item 34).

items.title: Definition 8.3.3 (2017: 8.6): strong bundle functors

book.label: §8.3, Definition 8.3.3 (2017: 8.6), p. 378 (2017 p. 274)
book.statement: A strong bundle functor $\Phi : P \to P'$ between the strong bundles $P : W \to X$ and $P' : W' \to X'$ over the ep-groupoids $X$ and $X'$ consists of a functor $\Phi : \mathcal W = (W, \mathbf W) \to \mathcal W' = (W', \mathbf W')$ between ep-groupoids which is linear on the fibres and covers an sc-smooth functor $(\varphi, \boldsymbol\varphi) : (X, \mathbf X) \to (X', \mathbf X')$. Moreover, $\Phi$ induces strong bundle maps $\Phi : W \to W'$ and $\boldsymbol\Phi : \mathbf W \to \mathbf W'$ between the object sets and the morphism sets, such that $P' \circ \Phi = \varphi \circ P$.

lean.statement: `IsStrongBundleFunctor E E' ϕ Φ`, for an ep-functor $\Phi$ between the ep-groupoids of V8.22: the object map is a strong bundle map $W \to W'$ covering $\phi$ (for $P$, $P'$; `isStrongBundleMap_obj`), and the morphism map is one $\mathbf W \to \mathbf W'$ covering $\boldsymbol\phi$ (for the pull-backs $\mathbf W \to \mathbf X$, $\mathbf W' \to \mathbf X'$; `isStrongBundleMap_mor`) (fields). `IsStrongBundleFunctor.projFunctor_comp`: $P' \circ \Phi = \phi \circ P$ as functors; `IsStrongBundleFunctor.mor_val`: $\Phi(\gamma, w) = (\phi(\gamma), \Phi(w))$; `isStrongBundleFunctor_id`: the identity is one.

items.title: Definitions 8.3.2 and 8.3.3 (2017: 8.5 and 8.6) are equivalent

items.title: Definition 8.3.4 (2017: 8.7): section functors

book.label: §8.3, Definition 8.3.4 (2017: 8.7), pp. 379 ff. (2017 pp. 274–275)
book.statement: Let $(P : W \to X, \mu)$ be a strong bundle over the ep-groupoid $X$. (1) An sc-smooth section functor $f$ is an sc-smooth section $f : X \to W$ of $P$ satisfying the functorial condition $f(y) = \mu(\varphi, f(x))$ for morphisms $\varphi : x \to y$; $\Gamma(P, \mu)$ is the vector space of sc-smooth section functors. (2) An sc⁺-section functor is an $f \in \Gamma(P, \mu)$ with $f(x) \in W_{0,1}$ for all $x$ which, viewed as a section of $W[1] \to X$, is sc-smooth; $\Gamma^+(P, \mu) \subset \Gamma(P, \mu)$ is the vector subspace of sc⁺-section functors. (3) An sc-Fredholm section functor is an $f \in \Gamma(P, \mu)$ which, as a section of $W \to X$, is an sc-Fredholm section; $\mathrm{Fred}(P, \mu)$ is the collection of these.

items.title: Definition 8.5.1 (2017: 8.8): proper covering functors

book.label: §8.5 (2017 §8.4), Definition 8.5.1 (2017: 8.8), p. 383 (2017 p. 275)
book.statement: An sc-smooth functor $F : Y \to X$ between ep-groupoids is a proper covering functor if (1) the sc-smooth map $F : Y \to X$ between the objects is a surjective local sc-diffeomorphism; (2) for every object $x \in X$ the preimage $F^{-1}(x)$ is finite, and there exist an open neighborhood $U(x)$ and mutually disjoint open neighborhoods $U(y)$ of the points $y \in F^{-1}(x)$ such that $F : U(y) \to U(x)$ is an sc-diffeomorphism and $F^{-1}(U(x)) = \bigcup_{y \in F^{-1}(x)} U(y)$; (3) the map $\mathbf Y \to \mathbf X\,{}_s{\times}_F\,Y$, $\varphi \mapsto (F(\varphi), s(\varphi))$, is an sc-diffeomorphism.

lean.statement: `EpFunctor.IsProperCovering F`: (1) `surjective`, `isLocalScDiffeo`; (2) `finite_fiber`, and `evenlyCovered`: an open $U \ni x$ and pairwise disjoint $V(y) \ni y$ with sc-diffeomorphisms $F : V(y) \to U$ (inverses $\sigma(y)$) and $F^{-1}(U) = \bigcup_y V(y)$; (3) `isScDiffeo_fibredMap`: `fibredMap`, $\varphi \mapsto (F(\varphi), s(\varphi))$, is an sc-diffeomorphism onto Part I's fibred-product sub-M-polyfold of $\mathbf X \times Y$ (`MPolyfold.isSubMPolyfold_fibredProduct`) (fields of the structure). `isProperCovering_id`: the identity functor of every ep-groupoid is one.

items.title: The degeneracy index of $\mathbf X\,{}_s{\times}_F\,Y$ (after Definition 8.5.1 (2017: 8.8))

book.label: §8.5 (2017 §8.4), after Definition 8.5.1 (2017: 8.8), pp. 383 ff. (2017 pp. 275–276)
book.statement: The sc-diffeomorphism $\mathbf Y \to \mathbf X\,{}_s{\times}_F\,Y$, $\varphi \mapsto (F(\varphi), s(\varphi))$, preserves the degeneracy index, so $d_{\mathbf Y}(\varphi) = d_{\mathbf X\,{}_s{\times}_F\,Y}(F(\varphi), s(\varphi))$. The fibred product is a sub-M-polyfold of $\mathbf X \times Y$, which has the degeneracy index $d_{\mathbf X \times Y}(\varphi, y) = d_{\mathbf X}(\varphi) + d_Y(y)$. Since $F$ and $s$ are local sc-diffeomorphisms, $d_{\mathbf X \times Y}(F(\varphi), s(\varphi)) = d_{\mathbf X}(F(\varphi)) + d_Y(s(\varphi)) = 2\,d_{\mathbf Y}(\varphi)$, hence $d_{\mathbf X\,{}_s{\times}_F\,Y}(F(\varphi), s(\varphi)) = \tfrac12\,d_{\mathbf X \times Y}(F(\varphi), s(\varphi))$: the fibred product lies in a particular position in the full product.

lean.statement: `IsProperCovering.degIndex_fibredMap`: $d_{\mathbf Y}(\varphi) = d_{\mathbf X\,{}_s{\times}_F\,Y}(F(\varphi), s(\varphi))$, by Part I's invariance of the degeneracy index under sc-diffeomorphisms (`proposition_2_24`); `IsProperCovering.degIndex_mor`: $d_{\mathbf X}(F(\varphi)) = d_{\mathbf Y}(\varphi)$. In general, `IsProperCovering.degIndex_prod_fibredMap_le`: $d_{\mathbf X \times Y}(F(\varphi), s(\varphi)) \le 2\,d_{\mathbf Y}(\varphi)$, from Part I's `MPolyfold.degIndex_prod_le`. **For tame $X$ and $Y$**, `IsProperCovering.degIndex_prod_fibredMap`: $d_{\mathbf X \times Y}(F(\varphi), s(\varphi)) = 2\,d_{\mathbf Y}(\varphi)$ and $2\,d_{\mathbf X\,{}_s{\times}_F\,Y}(F(\varphi), s(\varphi)) = d_{\mathbf X \times Y}(F(\varphi), s(\varphi))$, from Part I's product formula for tame M-polyfolds (`MPolyfold.isTame_prod`).

diff: **Hidden hypothesis**: the product formula $d_{\mathbf X \times Y} = d_{\mathbf X} + d_Y$, which Part I proves for tame M-polyfolds; Part I's Proposition 2.5.20 (2017: 2.15; preprint 2.46) states its formula $d = \tfrac12 d_{X \times Y}$ for tame $X$, $Y$ (Findings, Chapter 8, item 51).

items.title: Definition 8.5.5 (2017: 8.9): $\mathrm{Diff}_{sc}$, covering functors and geometric lifts

book.label: §8.5 (2017 §8.4), Definition 8.5.5 (2017: 8.9) and the category $\mathrm{Diff}_{sc}$ before it, pp. 387–389 (2017 pp. 279–280)
book.statement: $\mathrm{Diff}_{sc}$ is the category whose objects are M-polyfolds and whose morphisms are sc-smooth diffeomorphisms between M-polyfolds. Let $D$ and $C$ be two categories with finitely many objects and morphisms, all morphisms isomorphisms, $C$ with only one object $x$. A covering functor $f : D \to C$ is a functor such that $\mathbf D \to \mathbf C\,{}_s{\times}_f\,D$, $\psi \mapsto (f(\psi), s(\psi))$, is a bijection. items.title: Theorem 8.5.8 (2017: 8.6) (Proper Covering II): the local model of a proper covering functor

items.title: Definition 8.5.9 (2017: 8.10): proper strong bundle covering functors

book.label: §8.5 (2017 §8.4), Definition 8.5.9 (2017: 8.10), p. 394 (2017 p. 285)
book.statement: Let $(W, \mu)$ and $(V, \tau)$ be strong bundles over the ep-groupoids $Y$ and $X$, $P : W \to Y$ and $Q : V \to X$. A proper strong bundle covering functor is a strong bundle map $A$ (in particular fibrewise linear) with $Q \circ A = F \circ P$ and (1) $A$ is surjective and a local strong bundle isomorphism covering an sc-smooth proper covering functor $F : Y \to X$; (2) $F^{-1}(x)$ is finite for every $x \in X$, and there are open neighborhoods $U(x)$ and mutually disjoint $U(y)$, $y \in F^{-1}(x)$, such that $A : W|U(y) \to V|U(x)$ is a strong bundle isomorphism for every $y \in F^{-1}(x)$ and $F^{-1}(U(x)) = \bigcup_{y \in F^{-1}(x)} U(y)$; (3) the map $\mathbf W \to \mathbf V\,{}_s{\times}_A\,W$, $(\psi, w) \mapsto ((F(\psi), A(w)), w)$, is a strong bundle isomorphism covering the sc-diffeomorphism $\mathbf Y \to \mathbf X\,{}_s{\times}_F\,Y$, $\psi \mapsto (F(\psi), s(\psi))$, where the strong bundle projection $\mathbf V\,{}_s{\times}_A\,W \to \mathbf X\,{}_s{\times}_F\,Y$ is $((\varphi, v), w) \mapsto (\varphi, P(w))$.

Witnesses: `isProperStrongBundleCovering_id`, `TrivialBundle.epBundle_isProperStrongBundleCovering`.

items.title: Lemma 8.6.2 (2017: 8.10): the isomorphism classes over isomorphic objects

book.label: §8.6.1 (2017 §8.5.1), Lemma 8.6.2 (2017: 8.10) and the paragraph before it, 2017 p. 287
book.statement: Given a proper covering functor $F : Y \to X$ and isomorphic $x$, $x'$, there is a one-to-one correspondence between the isomorphism classes of $F^{-1}(x)$ and of $F^{-1}(x')$: if $F^{-1}(x) = \bigsqcup_{j=1}^q \Theta_j$ is the decomposition into isomorphism classes, there is a decomposition $F^{-1}(x') = \bigsqcup_{j=1}^q \Theta'_j$ such that, if $y \in F^{-1}(x)$ and $y' \in F^{-1}(x')$ are connected by an isomorphism, there is a uniquely determined $j$ with $y \in \Theta_j$ and $y' \in \Theta'_j$. items.title: §8.6.2 (2017 §8.5.2): the structure of strong bundle coverings

items.title: Definition 9.1.2 (2017: 9.1), branched ep⁺-subgroupoids

book.label: §9.1, Definition 9.1.2, p. 402 (2017: Definition 9.1, p. 292)
book.statement: A branched ep⁺-subgroupoid of the ep-groupoid $X$ is a functor $\Theta : X \to \mathbb Q^+$ with (1) $\mathrm{supp}(\Theta) = \{\Theta > 0\}$ contained in $X_\infty$ and $|\mathrm{supp}(\Theta)|$ paracompact in the topology induced from $|X|$; and, at every $x \in \mathrm{supp}(\Theta)$, (2) an open $U(x)$ and finitely many submanifolds $M_i \subseteq U(x)$ through $x$ with proper inclusions, (3) weights $\sigma_i \in \mathbb Q$, $\sigma_i > 0$, and (4) $\Theta(y) = \sum_{y \in M_i} \sigma_i$ for $y \in U(x)$: a local branching structure.

lean.statement: A branched ep⁺-subgroupoid is a functor $\Theta \ge 0$ whose support lies in the smooth set, whose orbit support $|\mathrm{supp}(\Theta)|$ is paracompact, and which at every $x \in \mathrm{supp}(\Theta)$ has a local branching structure: an open $U(x)$, finitely many smooth submanifolds $M_i \subseteq U(x)$ through $x$ with proper inclusions, weights $\sigma_i > 0$, and $\Theta(y) = \sum_{y \in M_i} \sigma_i$ on $U(x)$. The zero functor and the indicator of a smooth point of $\mathbb R^n$ are examples.

items.title: Remark 9.1.1 (2017: 9.1) and the last paragraph of Definition 9.1.2, the dimension of a submanifold and $n$-dimensional $\Theta$

book.label: §9.1, Remark 9.1.1, p. 402 (2017: Remark 9.1, p. 291), and Definition 9.1.2, last paragraph, p. 402
book.statement: The dimension of $T_mM$ is locally constant in $m \in M$, the local dimension of $M$. $\Theta$ is $n$-dimensional if at every point of its support the manifolds of a local branching structure can be taken $n$-dimensional (2017: are $n$-dimensional); by a footnote (new in 2021) an $n$-dimensional $\Theta$ is not $m$-dimensional for $m \ne n$; $\Theta$ is locally equidimensional if small structures have sheets of one dimension.

lean.statement: A submanifold has dimension $k$ at $a$ if the tangent space of its sub-retract at the chart image of $a$ has dimension $k$; the value does not depend on the data and the chart, is unique, exists at every point, and is invariant under restriction to open sets and under sc-diffeomorphisms. $\Theta$ is $n$-dimensional if at every point of its support some local branching structure has only $n$-dimensional $M_i$; the zero functor is $n$-dimensional for every $n$.
