book.label: §9.2, Remark 9.2.4, p. 411 (2017: Remark 9.4, p. 300)
book.statement: (a) Being a good point is intrinsic. (b) Near a good point $y$, $\Theta$ is represented by one submanifold with weight $\Theta(y)$.

lean.statement: (a) A point good for some structure is good for every structure whose domain contains it. (b) Near a good point $y$, $\Theta = \Theta(y) \cdot 1_M$ for one submanifold $M$ properly embedded in an open $V \ni y$.

diff: (b) with $M = M_i \cap V(y)$ for any $i$ with $y \in M_i$ (Findings, Chapter 9, item 23).

items.title: Lemma 9.2.5 (2017: 9.4), good points are preserved by morphisms

book.label: §9.2, Lemma 9.2.5, p. 411 (2017: Lemma 9.4, p. 300)
book.statement: For an equidimensional $\Theta$ and a morphism $\varphi$, $s(\varphi)$ is good iff $t(\varphi)$ is good.

lean.statement: For every morphism $\varphi$, $s(\varphi)$ is good iff $t(\varphi)$ is.

diff: For every branched ep⁺-subgroupoid, not only equidimensional ones; the transport of structures is replaced by $\Theta \circ \hat\varphi = \Theta$ on the sheet of $\varphi$ (Findings, Chapter 9, item 23).

items.title: Definition 9.2.6 (2017: 9.5), the good and the bad set

book.label: §9.2, Definition 9.2.6, p. 411 (2017: Definition 9.5, p. 300)
book.statement: $S^g_\Theta$ is the set of good points of $\mathrm{supp}(\Theta)$, $S^b_\Theta$ the set of bad points; by Remark 9.2.4 (c) being good is a property of $|x|$.

lean.statement: $S^g_\Theta$ is the set of points of $\mathrm{supp}(\Theta)$ good for some structure whose domain contains them, $S^b_\Theta = \mathrm{supp}(\Theta) \setminus S^g_\Theta$; both are saturated, so they descend to $|X|$.

diff: The text cites "Remark 9.2.4 (c)" for the descent; Remark 9.2.4 has (a) and (b) only, and Lemma 9.2.5 is what is used (possible misprint) (Findings, Chapter 9, item 23).

items.title: Lemma 9.2.7 (1) (2017: 9.5 (1)), the good set is open and dense

book.label: §9.2, Lemma 9.2.7 (1), p. 412 (2017: Lemma 9.5 (1), p. 300)
book.statement: For an equidimensional $\Theta$, $S^g_\Theta$ is open and dense in $\mathrm{supp}(\Theta)$ and $S^b_\Theta$ is closed and nowhere dense; the text derives the density from (2).

lean.statement: In $\mathrm{supp}(\Theta)$ the good set is open and dense and the bad set is closed and nowhere dense.

diff: For every branched ep⁺-subgroupoid, without equidimensionality and without (2), from a topological covering argument (Findings, Chapter 9, item 24).

items.title: Lemma 9.2.7 (2) (2017: 9.5 (2)), good points accumulate on every sheet

book.label: §9.2, Lemma 9.2.7 (2), p. 412 (2017: Lemma 9.5 (2), p. 301)
book.statement: For a bad point $x$ and a local branching structure on $U(x)$, every $M_i$ contains a sequence of good points converging to $x$.

lean.statement: For an $n$-dimensional local branching structure at $x$ and every $i$ there is a sequence of good points in $M_i$ converging to $x$, under invariance of domain for $n$-dimensional submanifolds on $U(x)$, which holds on $\mathbb R^m$; on $\mathbb R^m$ the statement has no hypothesis. In Remark 9.1.3 (b) the origin is bad and is approached by good points of the graph of $\beta_1$.

chips: at every $x$, not only bad points
diff: Hidden hypotheses: invariance of domain (`HasDomainInvarianceAt`) on a general M-polyfold.
The statement holds at every $x$, not only at bad points (gap G.98) (Findings, Chapter 9, item 24).

items.title: Proposition 9.2.8 and Lemmas 9.2.9–9.2.11 (2017: Proposition 9.3, Lemmas 9.6–9.8), the graph representation and tangent slices

book.label: §9.2, Proposition 9.2.8, p. 413 (2017: Proposition 9.3, p. 302), and Lemmas 9.2.9–9.2.11, pp. 414–417 (2017: Lemmas 9.6–9.8, pp. 302–305)
book.statement: At a bad point $x$, for a class $\Xi$ of indices with one tangent space $T_xM_i$ there are $i_1, \ldots, i_p \in \Xi$, a partition $\Xi = I^1 \sqcup \cdots \sqcup I^p$ and sequences of good points $x^e_k \to x$ with $x^e_k \in M_i$ iff $i \in I^e$. Lemmas 9.2.9–9.2.11: $L \cap C$ has interior in $L = T_0M_{i_1}$; the $M_i$, $i \in \Xi$, are graphs over a cone around $h_0$; the map $a \mapsto a + B_i(a)$ is injective with invertible derivative and its image contains a cone.

lean.statement: If near $x$ every $n$-dimensional submanifold through $x$ is, in one chart, a graph over a ray (or ball) in its tangent space (`IsGraphChartAt`, `HasGraphChartAt` for all dimensions at once, `HasGraphBallAt`), then for every class $\Xi$ of sheets with one tangent space $L$ at $x$ and every neighbourhood $W$ of $x$ there is a finite slice of points in $W$ meeting each $M_i$, $i \in \Xi$, once and missing the other $M_i$, so that $\sum_{i \in \Xi} \sigma_i = \sum_{y \in F} \Theta(y)$ (`HasTangentSlicesAt`), and the slice can be chosen generic. On $\mathbb R^m$ the graph representation holds at every point and in every dimension, by the inverse function theorem.

diff: Hidden hypotheses: the graph representation on a general M-polyfold.

Proposition 9.2.8 is formalized in slice form, not with the text's subsets $I^e$ and sequences of good points; rays and balls replace the cones around $h_0$; Lemmas 9.2.9–9.2.11 are the hypotheses, proved on $\mathbb R^m$ (gap G.97) (Findings, Chapter 9, item 25).

items.title: Definition 9.2.12 (2017: 9.6), the tangent $T\Theta$

book.label: §9.2, Definition 9.2.12, p. 418 (2017: Definition 9.6, p. 306)
book.statement: There is a well-defined branched ep⁺-subgroupoid $T\Theta : TX \to \mathbb Q^+$, $T\Theta(h) = 0$ for $h \in T_xX$ with $\Theta(x) = 0$ and $T\Theta(h) = \sum_{h \in TM_i} \sigma_i$ over $U(x)$; by the previous discussion it does not depend on the structure, and the local definitions fit together.

lean.statement: Under the independence of V9.13, $T\Theta(h) = \sum_{h \in TM_i} \sigma_i$ for $h$ over $U(x)$, and $0$ over the complement of the support, is well defined, nonnegative and a functor on the tangent ep-groupoid; it is a branched ep⁺-subgroupoid of $TX$ if the $TM_i$ are smooth submanifolds of $TX$ (closedness and the paracompactness of $|\mathrm{supp}(T\Theta)|$ for paracompact $|X|$ are proved), and on $\mathbb R^m$ the $TM_i$ are sub-M-polyfolds of $TX$, retracts of $Ts$.

diff: Hidden hypotheses: that the $TM_i$ are smooth submanifolds of $TX$ (the tangent of the sc⁺-retraction is sc⁺ on $TX$), and the paracompactness of $|X|$, neither discussed in the text.
$h \in TM_i$ is read as $h \in T_{p(h)}M_i$; only the zero functor is a witness of the full hypothesis (gap G.99) (Findings, Chapter 9, item 26).

items.title: Lemma 9.2.13 (2017: 9.9), $d_M(x) = 0$ and reduced tangent position

book.label: §9.2, Lemma 9.2.13, p. 419 (2017: Lemma 9.9, p. 307)
book.statement: For a submanifold $M$ of $X$ and $x \in M$, equivalent: (1) $x \in \partial X$ and $d_M(x) = 0$; (2) $T_xM \subseteq T^R_xX$.

lean.statement: For a smooth submanifold $M$ and $x \in M \cap \partial X$: $d_M(x) = 0$ iff $T_xM \subseteq T^R_xX$ (in every chart, the chart image of $T_xM$ lies in the reduced tangent space). For every $x \in M$: $d_M(x) = 0$ iff $T_xM \subseteq T^R_xX$. As printed, with "$x \in \partial X$" in (1), (2) ⇒ (1) does not hold as we read it at a point $p$ of $\mathbb R^n$, which satisfies (2) and lies off $\partial\mathbb R^n$.

diff: Read with $x \in M \cap \partial X$ as the standing assumption, which is where the text uses it, and proved at every $x \in M$ in the form `subDegIndex_eq_zero_iff`. The converse needs a chart of $M$ without boundary near $x$: by the inverse function theorem on $T_xM$ and the step that the projection is injective on $M$ near $x$ ("the image is $M$ near $0$"), which the text does not spell out; the text's complement $Y$ and map $F$ are not needed (Findings, Chapter 9, items 40, 41).

items.title: Remark 9.2.14 (2017: 9.5), $\partial M$

book.label: §9.2, Remark 9.2.14, p. 419 (2017: Remark 9.5, p. 307)
book.statement: $x \in \partial M$ iff $x \in \partial X$ and $T_xM$ is not contained in $T^R_xX$ (2017: in $C_xX$'s reduced part).

lean.statement: $x \in \partial M$ iff $x \in \partial X$ and $T_xM \not\subseteq T^R_xX$; in particular $\partial M \subseteq \partial X$, and $d_M(x) \ge 1$ at such points.

diff: $\partial M$ is the boundary of the induced M-polyfold structure; the text's "not contained in $C_xX$" is equivalent to the reduced-tangent form (`isReducedTangentAt_iff_subset_partialQuadrant`) (Findings, Chapter 9, item 42).

items.title: Proposition 9.2.15 (2017: 9.4), the boundary weights

book.label: §9.2, Proposition 9.2.15, p. 420 (2017: Proposition 9.4, p. 308)
book.statement: For $x \in \mathrm{supp}(\Theta) \cap \partial X$ and two local branching structures: (1) $\sum_{y \in \partial M_i} \sigma_i$ does not depend on the structure; (2) it vanishes where $d_X(y) = 0$; (3) these sums define a functor $\partial\Theta \ge 0$ supported in $\partial X$.

lean.statement: (1) Under the independence of V9.13, $\sum_{y \in \partial M_i} \sigma_i$ is the same for any two local branching structures whose domains contain $y$. (2) At $y$ with $d_X(y) = 0$ this sum and the corresponding formal sum of tangent spaces vanish, for every structure. (3) $\partial\Theta$, the part of $T_\Theta(y)$ on tangent spaces not contained in $T^R_yX$, is a functor, nonnegative, supported in $\partial X$, and equal to $\sum_{y \in \partial M_i} \sigma_i$ on every structure.

diff: Hidden hypotheses: the independence of Theorem 9.2.1 for (1) and (3).
(1) and (2) need neither $x \in \mathrm{supp}(\Theta) \cap \partial X$ nor that $\Theta$ be branched, and (2) needs no independence (Findings, Chapter 9, item 43).

items.title: Definition 9.2.16 (2017: 9.7), the boundary $\partial\Theta$

book.label: §9.2, Definition 9.2.16, p. 421 (2017: Definition 9.7, p. 309)
book.statement: In view of the preceding proposition the boundary $\partial\Theta$ of $\Theta$ is the functor uniquely characterized by (1) $\mathrm{supp}(\partial\Theta) \subseteq \partial X$ and (2) $\partial\Theta(y) = \sum_{y \in \partial M_i} \sigma_i$ on local branching structures at points of $\mathrm{supp}(\partial\Theta)$.

lean.statement: $\partial\Theta$ satisfies the text's (1) $\mathrm{supp}(\partial\Theta) \subseteq \partial X$ and (2) the local formula at points of $\mathrm{supp}(\partial\Theta)$; a functor that vanishes off $\mathrm{supp}(\Theta)$ and satisfies (2) at the points of $\mathrm{supp}(\Theta)$ equals $\partial\Theta$. As stated, (1) and (2) do not characterize $\partial\Theta$ uniquely as we read them: the zero functor satisfies them for every $\Theta$, and for $\Theta = 1$ on $[0, \infty)$ both $0$ and $\partial\Theta \ne 0$ do.

chips: uniqueness: does not hold as we read it
diff: Hidden hypotheses: the independence of Theorem 9.2.1.

"uniquely characterized" is verified with (2) asked on $\mathrm{supp}(\Theta)$. "In view of Proposition 9.2.13" before the definition (2017: "Proposition 9.9") is presumably Proposition 9.2.15, and "branched ep⁺-groupoid" is "ep⁺-subgroupoid" (possible misprints) (Findings, Chapter 9, items 44, 45).

items.title: Remark 9.2.17 (2017: 9.6)

book.label: §9.2, Remark 9.2.17, p. 421 (2017: Remark 9.6, p. 310)
book.statement: $\partial\Theta$ has in general no particularly nice properties (the text noted before Lemma 9.2.13 that it is in general not the restriction of $\Theta$ to $\partial X$); "in Section 9.5, Definition 9.3.6" the tame branched ep⁺-subgroupoids are introduced, whose boundaries are nice enough for integration and orientation.

lean.statement: $\partial\Theta \le \Theta$; $\partial\Theta$ is in general not the restriction of $\Theta$ to $\partial X$: for the indicator of the corner $0$ of $[0, \infty)$, $\Theta(0) = 1$ and $\partial\Theta(0) = 0$, while for $\Theta = 1$ on $[0, \infty)$, $\partial\Theta(0) = 1$.

diff: Hidden hypotheses: the independence of Theorem 9.2.1, which the witnesses satisfy.
The forward reference "In Section 9.5, Definition 9.3.6" is to §9.3 (possible misprint, also in 2017) (Findings, Chapter 9, items 45, 46).

items.title: the category $\widehat{\mathrm{Gr}}(X)$ and oriented tangent spaces, p. 422

book.label: §9.3, the category $\widehat{\mathrm{Gr}}(X)$, p. 422 (2017 p. 310), and Remark 9.3.1 (2017: Remark 9.7)
book.statement: $\widehat{\mathrm{Gr}}(X)$ is defined like $\mathrm{Gr}(X)$ with oriented finite-dimensional subspaces $(L, o)$ of $T_xX$; forgetting orientations is a functor $\widehat{\mathrm{Gr}}(X) \to \mathrm{Gr}(X)$ over $X^\infty$. Remark 9.3.1 recalls an earlier notion of orientation.

lean.statement: An oriented tangent space at $y$ is a subset $L \subseteq T_yX$ with a set of positive frames, oriented in a chart and then in every chart; every finite-dimensional tangent space has exactly two orientations; morphisms push oriented tangent spaces forward. $\widehat{\mathrm{Gr}}(X)$ is the category of formal sums of oriented tangent spaces over $X^\infty$, with the forgetful functor to $\mathrm{Gr}(X)$ over $X^\infty$.

diff: Frames instead of orientations of vector spaces (gap G.7) (Findings, Chapter 9, item 50).

items.title: Definition 9.3.2 (2017: 9.8), orientations of $\Theta$

book.label: §9.3, Definition 9.3.2, p. 423 (2017: Definition 9.8, p. 311)
book.statement: An orientation of $\Theta$ is a section functor $\hat T_\Theta : X^\infty \to \widehat{\mathrm{Gr}}(X)$ lifting $T_\Theta$ such that near every $x \in \mathrm{supp}(\Theta)$ there is an oriented local branching structure $(M_i, o_i)$, $(\sigma_i)$ with $\hat T_\Theta(y) = \sum_{y \in M_i} \sigma_i\, T_y(M_i, o_i)$ (9.9).

lean.statement: An orientation of $\Theta$ is a natural assignment $\hat T_\Theta$ of formal sums of oriented tangent spaces at smooth points, lifting $T_\Theta$, which near every $x \in \mathrm{supp}(\Theta)$ is $\sum_i \sigma_i\, T_y(M_i, o_i)$ for an oriented local branching structure (continuous orientations $o_i$ of the $M_i$); it defines a section functor of $\widehat{\mathrm{Gr}}(X)$ over $X^\infty$. The zero functor and finite sums of oriented closed submanifolds of $\mathbb R^n$ are oriented.

diff: Hidden hypotheses: the lift condition uses $T_\Theta$, hence the independence of Theorem 9.2.1, discharged on $\mathbb R^m$.
The continuity of $o_i$ is the local constancy of the chart frames (Findings, Chapter 9, item 51).

items.title: Remark 9.3.3 (2017: 9.8), orientations are not unique

book.label: §9.3, Remark 9.3.3, p. 423 (2017: Remark 9.8, p. 311)
book.statement: The local representation (9.9) means exactly that the lift $x \mapsto \hat T_\Theta(x)$ is locally continuous on $\mathrm{supp}(\Theta)$; an orientable $\Theta$ may have more than two orientations, because of its fractional nature.

lean.statement: The indicator of a point of $\mathbb R^n$ has infinitely many orientations, pairwise distinct, $T_q$ for $q \in (0, 1) \cap \mathbb Q$.

diff: Infinitely many, not only more than one (Findings, Chapter 9, item 52).

items.title: Lemma 9.3.4 (2017: 9.10), orientations are determined by good points

book.label: §9.3, Lemma 9.3.4, p. 423 (2017: Lemma 9.10, p. 311)
book.statement: Two orientations $\hat T^1_\Theta$, $\hat T^2_\Theta$ of a branched ep⁺-subgroupoid $\Theta$ which agree at good points are the same.

lean.statement: Two orientations of an $n$-dimensional $\Theta$ that agree at the good points agree at every smooth point, under `HasOrientedGoodPointsAt` on the support, which follows from the ball graph representation `HasGraphBallAt` and the level-1 continuity `HasContinuousLevelOneOn`; on $\mathbb R^m$ without hypothesis. Without equidimensionality the lemma does not hold as we read it: for $\Theta = 1_{\mathbb R \times 0} + 1_{(0,0)}$ on $\mathbb R^2$ two orientations agree at all good points and differ at the origin.

chips: mixed dimensions: does not hold as read
diff: Hidden hypotheses: $n$-dimensional $\Theta$; on a general M-polyfold the graph representation and the continuity of frame fields on level 1.

The proof compares the two structures on one family of slices, applying Proposition 9.2.8 to both families together, and compares frames of different sheets by level-1 continuity; the text takes the good-point sequences from the first structure only, a step that needs an argument it does not give (gaps G.97, G.100) (Findings, Chapter 9, item 53).

items.title: Example 9.3.5 (2017: 9.1)

book.label: §9.3, Example 9.3.5, p. 425 (2017: Example 9.1, p. 313)
book.statement: Four smooth $\beta^{\pm\pm}$ with graphs $G^{\pm\pm}$ define $\Theta$ in two ways; orienting by $\pm(1, 0)$ at the origin gives two orientations which coincide at $(0, 0)$ but are otherwise different; there are four possibilities to orient, and the second structure cannot necessarily be oriented to coincide with the first.

lean.statement: For $\beta^{++} = e(s) + e(-s)$ ($e$ = `expNegInvGlue`), $\beta^{--} = -\beta^{++}$ and the two mixed functions, the graphs define a branched ep⁺-subgroupoid $\Theta$ of the trivial ep-groupoid of $\mathbb R^2$ by two structures; the orientations $\hat T^1$, $\hat T^2$ given by $\pm(1, \beta')$ coincide at the origin, differ at $(s, \beta^{++}(s))$ for $s > 0$, and no sign choice for the second structure reproduces $\hat T^1$ near the origin. They also coincide wherever $x < 0$, and the four sign choices of the first structure give four different orientations, none equal to $\hat T^2$.

diff: Hidden hypotheses: none on $\mathbb R^2$.

"otherwise different" and "four different possibilities" do not hold as we read them (at least five orientations with weights $1$); the classification of all orientations of $\Theta$ is not formalized (gap G.101) (Findings, Chapter 9, item 54).

items.title: Definition 9.3.6 (2017: 9.10), tame $\Theta$

book.label: §9.3, Definition 9.3.6, p. 425 (2017: Definition 9.10, p. 314)
book.statement: $\Theta$ is tame if every $x \in \mathrm{supp}(\Theta)$ has an open $U(x)$ with the natural $G_x$-action and the properness property and a local branching structure on it whose $M_i$ have equivalent tame structures; in particular every $M_i$ is then a manifold with boundary with corners.

lean.statement: $\Theta$ is tame if at every point of its support there is a local branching structure on a domain with the natural $G_x$-action and the properness property all of whose $M_i$ have a tame induced structure; the zero functor and the indicator of a point of $\mathbb R^n$ are tame.

diff: "an equivalent tame structure" is Part I's tame induced structure (Definition 2.5.18); the consequence "in particular every $M_i$ is a manifold with boundary with corners" is not formalized (gap G.102) (Findings, Chapter 9, item 55).

items.title: Lemma 9.3.7, equal tangent spaces have equal degeneracy

book.label: §9.3, Lemma 9.3.7, p. 426 (new in the 2021 edition)
book.statement: If $Y$ is a tame M-polyfold, $M_1$, $M_2$ submanifolds of the same dimension with tame induced structures and $y \in M_1 \cap M_2$, then $T_yM_1 = T_yM_2$ implies $d_{M_1}(y) = d_{M_2}(y)$.

lean.statement: For submanifolds $M_1$, $M_2$ with tame induced structures and $y \in M_1 \cap M_2$, $T_yM_1 = T_yM_2$ implies $d_{M_1}(y) = d_{M_2}(y)$.

diff: Neither "$Y$ tame" nor "of the same dimension" is needed; in the proof "$T_0O \cap C = T^R_0O$" is read through the linearity of the chart image of $T_0M$ (Findings, Chapter 9, item 56).

items.title: Definition 9.3.8 (2017: 9.9), the boundary orientation of an oriented $M$

book.label: §9.3, Definition 9.3.8, p. 427 (2017: Definition 9.9, p. 313)
book.statement: For an oriented $n$-dimensional $(M, o)$ and $y \in \partial M$ with $d_M(y) = 1$, a basis $(a_1, \ldots, a_{n-1})$ of $T_y\partial M$ is positive iff $(e, a_1, \ldots, a_{n-1})$ is positive for $o_y$, $e$ an outward pointing vector; this orients $\partial M$ near $y$.

lean.statement: For an oriented $(M, o)$, a hyperplane $K$ of $T_yM$ and $e \notin K$, the frames $(a_1, \ldots, a_{n-1})$ of $K$ with $(e, a_1, \ldots, a_{n-1})$ positive orient $K$, and the orientation is unchanged under $e \mapsto ce + k$, $c > 0$, $k \in K$; both orientations occur.

diff: $T_y\partial M$ and the outward vector enter as data $K$, $e$; that $T_y\partial M = T^R_yM$ and the outward half-space are determined by $M$ (through the cones $C_yM$) is not formalized (gap G.103) (Findings, Chapter 9, item 57).

items.title: (9.11) and Proposition 9.3.9, the boundary orientation does not depend on the structure

book.label: §9.3, Proposition 9.3.9, p. 428 (new in the 2021 edition), with (9.11), p. 427
book.statement: For two oriented local branching structures the parts of $\hat T_\Theta(y)$ of each degree $\ell = d_{M_i}(y)$ agree (9.11), since tangent spaces of different degree never coincide (Lemma 9.3.7); the definition of $\hat T_{\partial\Theta}$ does not depend on the structure.

lean.statement: For two oriented local branching structures with tame $M_i$ and the same oriented sum at $y$, the parts of degree $\ell = d_{M_i}(y)$ agree for every $\ell$ (9.11); hence (9.12) gives the same value for every structure, and vanishes at smooth points off $\mathrm{supp}(\Theta)$.

diff: The boundary operation $T_y(M, o) \mapsto T_y(\partial M, o_{\partial M})$ is a function `bd` of the oriented tangent space, which is what "the discussion preceding it" provides, given G.103 (Findings, Chapter 9, item 58).

items.title: Definition 9.3.10 (2017: 9.11), the oriented boundary $\hat T_{\partial\Theta}$

book.label: §9.3, Definition 9.3.10, p. 428 (2017: Definition 9.11, p. 314)
book.statement: For an oriented tame $\Theta$, $\hat T_{\partial\Theta}(y) = 0$ off $\mathrm{supp}(\Theta)$ and $\hat T_{\partial\Theta}(y) = \sum_{y \in \partial M_i, d_{M_i}(y) = 1} \sigma_i\, T_y(\partial M_i, o_{\partial M_i})$ on $U(x)$ (9.12).

lean.statement: $\hat T_{\partial\Theta}(y) = 0$ off $\mathrm{supp}(\Theta)$ and $\sum_{d_{M_i}(y) = 1} \sigma_i\, T_y(\partial M_i, o_{\partial M_i})$ on a structure (9.12).

diff: With `bd` as in V9.37; the continuity of $o_{\partial M}$ along $\partial M$ and its extension to the faces (Figure 9.1) are not formalized (gap G.103); Remark 9.3.11 has no formal content (Findings, Chapter 9, item 58).

items.title: Definition 9.4.1 (2017: 9.12), the relative tangent space and essential points

book.label: §9.4, Definition 9.4.1, p. 429 (2017: Definition 9.12, p. 315)
book.statement: For $K \subseteq M$, $M$ a smooth manifold with boundary and corners, $T^K_zM$ is the linear hull of the unit vectors $e = \lim \varphi(z_k)/|\varphi(z_k)|$, $z_k \to z$ in $K \setminus \{z\}$, in a chart centred at $z$, independent of the chart; $z \in K$ is essential if it is a limit of $z_k \in K$ with $T^K_{z_k}M = T_{z_k}M$.

lean.statement: For a subset $K$ of a finite-dimensional manifold with corners, $T^K_zM$ is the span of the limits of unit directions $\varphi(z_k)/|\varphi(z_k)|$, $z_k \to z$ in $K \setminus \{z\}$, in a chart centred at $z$, independent of the chart; $z \in K$ is essential if it is a limit of $z_k \in K$ with $T^K_{z_k}M = T_{z_k}M$. For two crossing lines in $\mathbb R^2$ the essential set is $\{0\}$.

diff: On Mathlib manifolds with corners, the span of Mathlib's tangent cone in a chart (Findings, Chapter 9, item 70).

items.title: Lemma 9.4.2 (2017: 9.11), the essential set is closed

book.label: §9.4, Lemma 9.4.2, p. 430 (2017: Lemma 9.11, p. 315)
book.statement: $K^e$ is closed in $K$, so $K \setminus K^e$ is open in $K$.

lean.statement: $K^e$ is closed in $K$ and $K \setminus K^e$ is open in $K$.

items.title: Property (T) (2017 p. 316)

book.label: §9.4, Property (T), p. 430 (2017 p. 316)
book.statement: (T): if $y_0 \in M_i \cap M_{i'}$, $T_{y_0}M_i = T_{y_0}M_{i'}$ and $o_{i,y_0} = \varepsilon\, o_{i',y_0}$, then $T_y(M_i, o_i) = T_y(M_{i'}, \varepsilon o_{i'})$ for all $y \in M_i \cap M_{i'}$ with $T_yM_i = T_yM_{i'}$. Lemma 9.4.3: (T) holds after restricting to a smaller $U'(x)$.

lean.statement: An oriented local branching structure has Property (T) on $V$ if, whenever two sheets have the same tangent space at a point of $V$ and their orientations there are related by $\varepsilon$, they are related by $\varepsilon$ at every point of $V$ where their tangent spaces agree; the first structure of Example 9.3.5 has it.

diff: Lemma 9.4.3, that (T) holds after shrinking $U(x)$, is not formalized (gap G.104) (Findings, Chapter 9, item 71).

items.title: Lemma 9.4.4 (2017: 9.13), essential in $M_i$ iff essential in $M_{i'}$

book.label: §9.4, Lemma 9.4.4, p. 431 (2017: Lemma 9.13, p. 317)
book.statement: If $z \in K(i, i') = M_i \cap M_{i'}$ is essential for $K(i, i') \subseteq M_i$, it is essential for $K(i, i') \subseteq M_{i'}$; so $K(i, i')^e$, $K(i, i')^{ne}$ do not depend on the reference sheet (proof left to the reader).

lean.statement: For sheets of one dimension the essential points of $K(i, i') = M_i \cap M_{i'}$ do not depend on the reference sheet; this is the field `ess_comm` of a sheet geometry, which exists for smooth graphs in $\mathbb R^2$. For sheets of different dimensions the lemma does not hold as we read it: $\mathbb R \times 0$ is essential in itself as a subset of $\mathbb R$ and has no essential point as a subset of $\mathbb R^2$.

chips: mixed dimensions: not as we read it
diff: Hidden hypotheses: sheets of one dimension.

For M-polyfold sheets, which carry no Mathlib manifold structure, Lemmas 9.4.4 and 9.4.6 are the fields of `SheetGeometry` (gap G.105); the note in Definition 9.4.7 ($i \sim_y i'$ implies $T_yM_i = T_yM_{i'}$) is its field `submanifoldTangent_eq` (Findings, Chapter 9, item 72).

items.title: Definition 9.4.5 (2017: 9.13), sets of measure zero

book.label: §9.4, Definition 9.4.5, p. 431 (2017: Definition 9.13, p. 317)
book.statement: $K \subseteq M_i$ has measure zero if for every smooth chart $\varphi$ of $M_i$ the set $\varphi(U \cap K)$ has Lebesgue measure zero.

lean.statement: $K \subseteq M$ has measure zero if its image in every chart has Lebesgue measure zero; measure zero is monotone and closed under countable unions, can be checked on a cover by charts, and $\mathbb R^2$ itself does not have it.

diff: For Mathlib manifolds with corners (Findings, Chapter 9, item 70).

items.title: Lemma 9.4.6 (2017: 9.14), non-essential points form a null set

book.label: §9.4, Lemma 9.4.6, p. 431 (2017: Lemma 9.14, p. 317)
book.statement: The sets $K(i, i')^{ne}$ have measure zero (by a Lebesgue density argument).

lean.statement: For every subset $K$ of a finite-dimensional manifold, $K \setminus K^e$ has measure zero, by a Lebesgue density argument at points where the relative tangent space is not everything.

diff: Any $K$, not only $K(i, i')$; for M-polyfold sheets it is the field `isNull_diff_ess` of `SheetGeometry` (gap G.105) (Findings, Chapter 9, items 70, 72).

items.title: Definition 9.4.7 (2017: 9.14), $y$-equivalence

book.label: §9.4, Definition 9.4.7, p. 432 (2017: Definition 9.14, p. 318)
book.statement: $i \sim_y i'$ if there is a chain $i = i_0, \ldots, i_k = i'$ in $I_y$ with $y \in K(i_{p-1}, i_p)^e$; then $T_yM_i = T_yM_{i'}$; $P_y = I_y/{\sim_y}$.

lean.statement: $i \sim_y i'$ if a chain of sheets through $y$ links them with $y$ essential in each consecutive intersection; it is an equivalence relation on $I_y$, $y$-equivalent sheets have the same tangent space at $y$, and $\#P_y$ is the number of classes.

items.title: Lemma 9.4.8 (2017: 9.15), points with two classes form a null set

book.label: §9.4, Lemma 9.4.8, p. 432 (2017: Lemma 9.15, p. 318)
book.statement: The set $\{y \in M_U \mid \#(I_y/{\sim_y}) \ge 2\}$ has measure zero.

lean.statement: $\{y \in M_U \mid \#P_y \ge 2\}$ is null in the sheets, and $M_U \setminus M^*_U$ is null.

diff: "measure zero" in $M_U$ is null in every sheet through the point; the last step of the proof uses $K(i, j)^{ne}$ inside $M_i$, while $K(j, j')^{ne}$ is null only in $M_j$ and $M_{j'}$ (reading) (Findings, Chapter 9, item 73).

items.title: Proposition 9.4.9 (2017: 9.5), the decomposition of $M^*_U$

book.label: §9.4, Proposition 9.4.9, p. 434 (2017: Proposition 9.5, p. 319)
book.statement: $M^*_U = \{y \in M_U \mid \#P_y = 1\}$ differs from $M_U$ by a null set and is the disjoint union of the $M^J_U = \{y \in M^*_U \mid I_y = J\}$; on $M^J_U$: (1) $\Theta = \sigma_J$, (2) $T_\Theta = \sigma_J T^J_y$, (3) $\hat T_\Theta = a_J (T^J_y, o^a_J) + b_J (T^J_y, o^b_J)$, (4) $a_J + b_J = \sigma_J$, $o^a_J = -o^b_J$.

lean.statement: For an oriented local branching structure with Property (T), the independence of Theorem 9.2.1 and sheets in a sheet geometry: $M_U \setminus M^*_U$ is null, $M^*_U$ is the disjoint union of the $M^J_U = \{y \in M^*_U \mid I_y = J\}$, and on $M^J_U$: $\Theta = \sigma_J$, $T_\Theta = \sigma_J\, T^J$, $\hat T_\Theta = a_J (T^J, o^a_J) + b_J (T^J, o^b_J)$ with $a_J + b_J = \sigma_J$ and $o^a_J = -o^b_J$.

diff: Hidden hypotheses: the independence of Theorem 9.2.1; the sheet geometry.
The footnote's "Lemma 9.5.2" is a forward reference (Findings, Chapter 9, items 72, 74).

items.title: Proposition 9.4.10 (2017: 9.6), comparing two oriented structures

book.label: §9.4, Proposition 9.4.10, p. 435 (2017: Proposition 9.6, p. 321)
book.statement: For two oriented local branching structures on $U(x)$ with Property (T) and (a) equal weight sums, (b) equal oriented sums at every $y$: $M_U = M'_U$, and there are $M^\dagger_U$ and a finite partition $A_1 \sqcup \cdots \sqcup A_\ell$ with (1) $M_U \setminus M^\dagger_U$ null, (2) $I_y$, $I'_y$ constant and all tangent spaces equal on each $A_p$, (3) equal weight sums, (4) partitions $J_\pm$, $J'_\pm$ with equal oriented tangent spaces, (5) equal oriented weighted sums.

lean.statement: For two oriented local branching structures on the same $U(x)$ with (a) the same weights and (b) the same oriented sums at every point, $M_U = M'_U$ and there are $M^\dagger_U \subseteq M_U$ with null complement in both families and a finite partition $A_1 \sqcup \cdots \sqcup A_\ell$ of $M^\dagger_U$ with (2)–(5) of the text. The two structures of Example 9.3.5 satisfy (a) and (b), and the origin has two classes.

diff: Hidden hypotheses: the sheet geometry.
Property (T) is not needed (Findings, Chapter 9, item 74).

items.title: Definition 9.5.1 (2017: 9.15), sets of measure zero in $S = |\mathrm{supp}(\Theta)|$

book.label: §9.5, Definition 9.5.1, p. 437 (2017: Definition 9.15, p. 322)
book.statement: For an oriented, tame, compact $n$-dimensional $\Theta$ and $S = |\mathrm{supp}(\Theta)|$: $A \subseteq S$ has measure zero if for every $x \in \mathrm{supp}(\Theta)$ and a choice of local branching structure on a suitable $U(x)$ the preimages $A_i \subseteq M_i$ of $A \cap |M_U|$ have measure zero in the sense of Definition 9.4.5.

lean.statement: For a system of null sets in the sheets of a class $\mathcal S$ of submanifolds (a σ-ideal in every sheet, local, the same on the overlap of two sheets of $\mathcal S$, a nonempty sheet not null in itself), $A \subseteq |X|$ has measure zero if at every $x \in \mathrm{supp}(\Theta)$ some tame local branching structure (Definition 9.3.6) with sheets in $\mathcal S$ has preimages $M_i \cap \pi^{-1}(A)$ null in $M_i$; the variants ask this of some local branching structure, or of every structure with sheets in $\mathcal S$. A `SheetMeasureGeometry` is a §9.4 sheet geometry whose null sets are such a system.

diff: "measure zero in $M_i$" is the abstract system `SheetNullSets`, satisfiable by Lebesgue null sets of graphs in $\mathbb R^2$ and of open subsets of $\mathbb R^2$ (V9.53); "a suitable $U(x)$" is a tame structure; compactness and orientation of $\Theta$ are not used (gap G.106) (Findings, Chapter 9, item 80).

items.title: Lemma 9.5.2 (2017: 9.16), measure zero does not depend on the choice

book.label: §9.5, Lemma 9.5.2, p. 437 (2017: Lemma 9.16, p. 322)
book.statement: The notion of a set of measure zero in $S$ does not depend on the choice of the local branching structures; cited from the literature, no proof.

lean.statement: If every point of $\mathrm{supp}(\Theta)$ has a tame local branching structure with sheets in $\mathcal S$, then "null preimages for a choice of tame structures", "for a choice of structures" and "for every structure with sheets in $\mathcal S$" agree; the sets of measure zero form a σ-ideal, and $S \ne \emptyset$ does not have measure zero. The axis $\mathbb R \times 0$ is null in the sheet $\mathbb R^2$ and not null in itself.

chips: across dimensions: does not hold as read
transfer of null sets is a field
diff: Hidden hypotheses: the sheets of all structures compared lie in one class $\mathcal S$ on which two sheets induce the same null sets on their overlap.

This transfer property holds for sheets of one dimension and does not hold across dimensions (`Polyfold.isNull_transfer_mixed_dim`), so the lemma is proved for structures with sheets in one class, as for the $n$-dimensional structures of an $n$-dimensional $\Theta$; for every structure of an $n$-dimensional $\Theta$ it would need Proposition 9.1.12 in general (gaps G.97, G.106) (Findings, Chapter 9, item 81).

items.title: Definition 9.5.3 (2017: 9.16) and the remark after it, the σ-algebra $L(S)$

book.label: §9.5, Definition 9.5.3, p. 438 (2017: Definition 9.16, p. 323), with the remark after it
book.statement: $L(S)$ is the smallest σ-algebra on $S$ containing the Borel σ-algebra $\mathcal B(S)$ and all subsets of measure zero; it is obtained from $\mathcal B(S)$ by adding the sets of measure zero.

lean.statement: $L(S)$ is the smallest σ-algebra on the subspace $S$ containing the Borel sets and the subsets of measure zero; for a σ-ideal $\mathcal N$ the σ-algebra generated by the Borel sets and $\mathcal N$ is $\{A \mid A \,\Delta\, B \in \mathcal N$ for a Borel $B\}$, so, under the standing assumption of V9.50, $K \in L(S)$ iff $K \,\Delta\, B$ has measure zero for some Borel $B$.

diff: The remark that $L(S)$ is obtained by adding the sets of measure zero is read as the completion $K \,\Delta\, B$ null; the form $B \cup N$ would need Borel null hulls (Findings, Chapter 9, item 82).

items.title: Definition 9.5.14 (2017: 9.17) and measure zero in $\partial S$, p. 448

book.label: §9.5, Definition 9.5.14, p. 448 (2017: Definition 9.17, p. 327), with the paragraph before it
book.statement: For $K \subseteq |\partial M_U|$ the preimages lie in the $\partial M_i$, where $(n-1)$-dimensional measure zero makes sense in the faces; this gives a well-defined notion of measure zero in $\partial S = |\mathrm{supp}(\partial\Theta)|$, and $L(\partial S)$ is the smallest σ-algebra containing $\mathcal B(\partial S)$ and the subsets of measure zero.

lean.statement: For a second null-set system on a class of boundaries $\partial M_i$, $K \subseteq |X|$ has measure zero in $\partial S = |\mathrm{supp}(\partial\Theta)|$ if at every point of $\mathrm{supp}(\partial\Theta)$ a tame structure has boundary preimages $\partial M_i \cap \pi^{-1}(K)$ null in $\partial M_i$; then every structure with boundaries in the class has; $\partial S \subseteq S$; $L(\partial S)$ is the σ-algebra generated by the Borel sets of $\partial S$ and these sets.

diff: Hidden hypotheses: the independence of Theorem 9.2.1 (through which $\partial\Theta$ is defined).

$(n-1)$-dimensional measure zero in $\partial M_i$ is an abstract system; its description face by face is not formalized, and no witness with $\partial S \ne \emptyset$ is given (gap G.108) (Findings, Chapter 9, item 83).

items.title: witnesses for §9.5 (not in the book)

book.label: §9.5, witnesses for Definitions 9.5.1 and 9.5.3 (not in the book)
book.statement: Not in the book.

lean.statement: On the trivial ep-groupoid of $\mathbb R^n$ every local branching structure restricts to a tame one. The graph sheets of §9.4 carry a `SheetMeasureGeometry`; for the $\Theta$ of the two graphs $G^{++}$, $G^{--}$ of Example 9.3.5 the touching point $|0|$ is a nonempty set of measure zero, $S$ is not null and $S \in L(S)$; for $\Theta = 1$ on $\mathbb R^2$ with the Lebesgue null sets there is a member of $L(S)$ that is not Borel.

diff: The hypotheses of V9.49–V9.51 are satisfiable, and $L(S)$ is strictly larger than the Borel σ-algebra (Findings, Chapter 9, item 82).

items.title: Lemma 9.5.9 (2017: 9.18), restrictions in the $G_x$-case: the isotropy and set part

book.label: §9.5, Lemma 9.5.9, p. 442 (2017: Lemma 9.18, p. 326)
book.statement: For $U(x)$ with the natural $G_x$-action and a local branching structure, $y \in U(x)$ and a small $V(y)$ with the natural $G_y$-action, $\mu^U_\omega(K) = \mu^V_\omega(K)$ for $K \in L(S)$, $K \subseteq |M_V|$. Proof: $H \cong G_y$, $G = \bigcup_{r \in R} rH$, $V$ invariant under $H$ and disjoint from its other translates, the preimage of $K$ is $\bigcup_r \varphi_r(\tilde K)$, and $\#R = \#G/\#H$.

lean.statement: For a natural representation of $G_x$ on $U(x)$ and $y \in U(x)$ with stabilizer $H$: $\#(G_x/H) \cdot \#G_y = \#G_x$; there is an open $V \ni y$ inside any given neighbourhood with $\varphi_g(V) = V$ for $g \in H$ and $\varphi_g(V) \cap V = \emptyset$ otherwise; for $K \subseteq |M_U \cap V|$ the preimage $M_U \cap \pi^{-1}(K)$ is the union over coset representatives $r$ of $\varphi_r(M_U \cap V \cap \pi^{-1}(K))$, and the union is disjoint.

diff: The equality of the measures $\mu^U_\omega$, $\mu^V_\omega$ is not stated (forms and integrals, gap G.107); the representatives $R$ are `Quotient.out` on $G_x/H$, and the restriction $\tilde M_j = V \cap M_j$ keeps the sheets through $y$ (`restrictAt`) (Findings, Chapter 9, item 84).

items.title: Lemma 9.5.10, the effective orders and (9.23)

book.label: §9.5, Lemma 9.5.10, p. 444, and (9.23), p. 445 (new in the 2021 edition)
book.statement: The same for the effective measures under LUC; the proof uses $T_x = \{g \mid \hat g = \mathrm{id}$ on an open $W\}$, $T_x \subseteq H$, $T_y$ identified with $T_x$, and (9.23) $\#R = \#G^{\mathrm{eff}}_x / \#H^{\mathrm{eff}}_y$.

lean.statement: $\#T_x \cdot \#G^{\mathrm{eff}}_x = \#G_x$; under LUC for $U(x)$, $T_x$ is the kernel of the representation, it lies in the stabilizer of every $y \in U(x)$, it corresponds to $T_y$ under $H \cong G_y$, so $\#T_y = \#T_x$, and $\#(G_x/H) \cdot \#G^{\mathrm{eff}}_y = \#G^{\mathrm{eff}}_x$, which is (9.23).

diff: The equality of the effective measures is not stated (gap G.107); LUC is `NaturalRep.HasLUC` of the given $U(x)$ (Definition 7.2.18) (Findings, Chapter 9, item 84).

items.title: Lemma 9.5.11 (2017: 9.19), morphism invariance: the isotropy and set part

book.label: §9.5, Lemma 9.5.11, p. 445 (2017: Lemma 9.19, p. 326)
book.statement: For a morphism $\varphi : x \to x'$ with local sc-diffeomorphism $\hat\varphi : U(x) \to U(x')$, $\mu^U_\omega(K) = \mu^{U'}_\omega(K)$ for $K \subseteq |M_U| = |M_{U'}|$; likewise for the effective measures under LUC.

lean.statement: For a morphism $\varphi : x \to x'$, $\#G_x = \#G_{x'}$ and $\#G^{\mathrm{eff}}_x = \#G^{\mathrm{eff}}_{x'}$; for local branching structures on $U$, $U'$ and a map $\hat\varphi$ of $U$ onto $U'$ with $|\hat\varphi(z)| = |z|$, $|M_U| = |M_{U'}|$; the maps $\varphi_g$ of a natural representation satisfy these hypotheses.

diff: The equality $\mu^U_\omega(K) = \mu^{U'}_\omega(K)$, "a change of variables", is not stated (gap G.107) (Findings, Chapter 9, item 84).

items.title: Proposition 9.5.13, the normalizing factors

book.label: §9.5, Proposition 9.5.13, p. 446 (new in the 2021 edition)
book.statement: (1) For effective $X$ the branched integral and the effective branched integral agree; (2) under LUC the effective branched integral on $X$ is the branched integral on the reduced ep-groupoid $X_R$. Proof: $T_x = \{1\}$, so the normalizing factors agree.

lean.statement: For effective $X$, $\#G^{\mathrm{eff}}_x = \#G_x$; for the reduced ep-groupoid $X_R$ (with Hausdorff paracompact morphism space), functors and local branching structures of $X$ and $X_R$ coincide and $\#G^{\mathrm{eff}}_x = \#G^R_x = \#(G^R_x)^{\mathrm{eff}}$.

diff: Hidden hypotheses: the morphism space of $X_R$ Hausdorff and paracompact (instances; Hausdorff under LUC).
The equality of the integrals in (1) and (2) is not stated (gap G.107); what is proved is the equality of the normalizing factors on which the proof rests (Findings, Chapter 9, item 84).

items.title: Lemma 9.6.1 and $\dim_\Theta$, the top dimension

book.label: §9.6, Lemma 9.6.1, p. 453 (new in the 2021 edition), and $\dim_\Theta$, p. 454
book.statement: Two local branching structures at $x$ have the same top dimension, by a measure zero argument; this defines $\dim_\Theta(x)$.

lean.statement: Two local branching structures at $x$ with dimension labellings have the same top dimension, which defines $\dim_\Theta(x)$.

diff: The "measure zero" argument is replaced by a topological covering lemma: a nonempty open piece of a $k$-dimensional submanifold is not covered by finitely many submanifolds of smaller dimension; no Lebesgue measure and no Baire argument (Findings, Chapter 9, item 90).

items.title: Lemma 9.6.2, the union of the top-dimensional sheets

book.label: §9.6, Lemma 9.6.2, p. 454 (new in the 2021 edition)
book.statement: On $U \cap U'$ the unions $M^k_U$ and $M^k_{U'}$ of the top-dimensional sheets of two structures agree.

lean.statement: On $U \cap U'$ the unions $M^k_U$ of the top-dimensional sheets of two structures agree.

diff: By the covering lemma of V9.58 (Findings, Chapter 9, item 90).

items.title: Definition 9.6.3, top-good and top-bad points

book.label: §9.6, Definition 9.6.3, p. 455 (new in the 2021 edition)
book.statement: $y \in M^k_U$ is top-good if near $y$ the top-dimensional $M_i$ through $y$ coincide, top-bad otherwise.

lean.statement: $y \in M^k_U$ is top-good if near $y$ all top-dimensional sheets through $y$ coincide; at top-good points the top-dimensional parts $\Theta_k$ of two structures agree, without hypothesis.

items.title: Lemma 9.6.4, top-goodness does not depend on the structure

book.label: §9.6, Lemma 9.6.4, p. 455 (new in the 2021 edition)
book.statement: Being top-good does not depend on the local branching structure; the proof moves the point slightly and argues similarly as for good points.

lean.statement: A point in both domains is top-good for one structure iff for the other, under `TopMultiplicity` (the top weight of a second structure at a point equals the sum of the weights of its sheets there), which holds for $k = 0$, for $k \ge n$ on $\mathbb R^n$, and wherever `HasGraphChartAt` holds, so on $\mathbb R^m$ in all dimensions.

diff: Hidden hypotheses: the graph representation on a general M-polyfold.

The step "similarly as good points" needs that the top weight of the second structure at $y$ is $\sigma$, an argument the text does not give; it is `TopMultiplicityAt`, proved from `HasGraphChartAt` by grouping the sheets of both families by tangent space (gap G.97) (Findings, Chapter 9, item 91).

items.title: Proposition 9.6.5 and the formula on p. 457

book.label: §9.6, Proposition 9.6.5, p. 456 (new in the 2021 edition), and the formula on p. 457
book.statement: At a top-bad $x$, for a class $\Xi$ of top-dimensional indices with one tangent space there are $i_1, \ldots, i_p$, a partition (printed $I_k = I^1 \sqcup \cdots \sqcup I^p$) and sequences of top-good points with $x^e_j \in M_i$ iff $i \in I^e$; then $\Theta_k(x) = \sum_\Xi \sum_e \Theta_k(x^k_e)$ (p. 457).

lean.statement: Under `HasGraphChartAt` at $x$, for every class of top-dimensional sheets with one tangent space at $x$ and every neighbourhood $W$ of $x$ there is a finite top slice in $W$; the top-dimensional part is $\Theta_k(x) = \sum_{\text{classes}} \sum_{y \in \text{slice}} \Theta(y)$, and the class sums agree for any two structures.

diff: Hidden hypotheses: the graph representation on a general M-polyfold.

Slices replace the subsets $I^e$ and the sequences of top-good points; the independence of the right-hand side from the structure, which the text does not show, is proved with one slice for the sheets of both structures. In (1) "$I_k = I^1 \sqcup \cdots \sqcup I^p$" reads as $\Xi = I^1 \sqcup \cdots \sqcup I^p$, the points $x^k_e$ are not introduced, and "This completes the proof of Proposition 9.6.5" refers to Proposition 9.1.12 (possible misprints) (gap G.97) (Findings, Chapter 9, items 91, 92).

items.title: Definition 10.1.1 (2017: 10.1), equivalences and the class $E$

book.label: §10.1, Definition 10.1.1, p. 461 (2017: Definition 10.1, p. 333)
book.statement: An equivalence $F : X \to Y$ of ep-groupoids is an sc-smooth functor which is faithful and full, induces a homeomorphism $|F| : |X| \to |Y|$, and is a local sc-diffeomorphism on objects; $E$ is the class of equivalences.

lean.statement: A structure on an sc-smooth functor with four fields: full, faithful, $|F|$ a homeomorphism, $F$ a local sc-diffeomorphism on objects. The class `EP.equivalences` contains the identities and is closed under composition; an equivalence is essentially surjective, and the functor from the pair groupoid of $\mathbb Z$ to the point is an equivalence.

chips: witness: pair groupoid of ℤ → point
diff: Full and faithful are stated on the sets of morphisms $x \to x'$, as in the text, and shown equal to Mathlib's notions for the underlying functor (Findings, Chapter 10, item 1).

items.title: Lemma 10.1.2 (2017: 10.1) and the remarks around it

book.label: §10.1, Lemma 10.1.2, p. 462 (2017: Lemma 10.1, p. 334)
book.statement: An sc-smooth functor which is a local sc-diffeomorphism on objects and an equivalence of categories is an equivalence; equivalences need not be invertible as functors.

lean.statement: An sc-smooth functor is an equivalence if and only if it is an equivalence of categories and a local sc-diffeomorphism on objects. $|F|$ is injective for $F$ full, surjective iff $F$ is essentially surjective, continuous, and open when $F$ is open on objects; composites of equivalences are equivalences; the equivalence from the pair groupoid of $\mathbb Z$ to the point has no left inverse on objects.

diff: The lemma is proved with its converse; the orbit map is shown bijective, continuous and open. "Not invertible" is witnessed by an equivalence with no left inverse on objects.

items.title: Proposition 10.1.3 (2017: 10.1), the refinement $X_{\mathcal U}$

book.label: §10.1, Proposition 10.1.3, p. 462 (2017: Proposition 10.1, p. 334)
book.statement: For an open covering $\mathcal U$ of the object M-polyfold of $X$, the ep-groupoid $X_{\mathcal U}$ of pairs $(U, x)$ and triples $(U, \varphi, V)$, with the structure induced from $X$ and $\mathbf X$, and the functor $(U, x) \mapsto x$, $(U, \varphi, V) \mapsto \varphi$ is an equivalence.

lean.statement: For a covering of $X$ by open sets $U_i$ indexed by a type $\iota$ and a nonempty object set, $X_{\mathcal U}$ (objects an open subset of $\iota \times X$, morphisms an open subset of $(\iota \times \iota) \times \mathbf X$, discrete $\iota$) is an ep-groupoid and the projection $F : X_{\mathcal U} \to X$ is an equivalence; for $\mathbb Z/2 \ltimes \mathbb R$ and a two-set covering it is not injective on objects.

diff: The covering is indexed by a type; the object set is assumed nonempty for the open-subset M-polyfold structure of Part I (trivial otherwise); the properness is proved with ultrafilters; the printed $(U, \varphi, v)$ is read $(U, \varphi, V)$ (Findings, Chapter 10, item 2).

items.title: Definition 10.1.4 (2017: 10.2), natural equivalence

book.statement: If $f : X \to Y$ is a generalized isomorphism, $X$ is tame face structured if and only if $Y$ is.

lean.statement: For a generalized isomorphism, tame and face structured transfers both ways; for an equivalence $F : X \to Y$, $X$ is tame iff $Y$ is (`isTame_iff`), the new direction through the weak fibred product $X \times_Y Y$.

items.title: Proposition 11.1.8 (2017: 11.3), maps of faces depend only on $|f|$

book.label: §11.1, Proposition 11.1.8, p. 526 (2017: Proposition 11.3, p. 380)
book.statement: If $f, g : X \to Y$ are generalized isomorphisms of tame face structured ep-groupoids with $|f| = |g|$, then $f_* = g_*$ and the induced maps $|F| \to |f_*F|$ agree.

lean.statement: $f_* = g_*$ and $f^* = g^*$ on faces, and $|f|$ and $|g|$ agree on every face $\theta$, mapping it into $g_*\theta$.

items.title: Theorem 11.2.1 (2017: 11.2), sc-differential forms under generalized maps

book.label: §11.2, Theorem 11.2.1, p. 526 (2017: Theorem 11.2, p. 380)
book.statement: $d \circ d = 0$ on $\Omega^*_{ep,\infty}$; generalized maps have pull-backs commuting with $d$, generalized isomorphisms push-forwards inverse to them; under the local regularity property they depend only on the orbit maps.

lean.statement: **Not formalized** (gap G.129): sc-differential forms on ep-groupoids are not in the project (G.74, G.80) (Findings, Chapter 11, item 20).

notFormalized.title: Example 1.1.3 (preprint 1.2): the weighted Sobolev spaces $H^{m,\delta_m}(\mathbb R \times S^1)$
notFormalized.label: §1.1, Example 1.1.3 (preprint 1.2), pp. 6 ff. (preprint pp. 6–7)
notFormalized.book: With $0 = \delta_0 < \delta_1 < \cdots$, the spaces $E_m = H^{m,\delta_m}(\mathbb R \times S^1)$ of $L^2$ functions whose weak derivatives up to order $m$, weighted by $e^{\delta_m|s|}$, are in $L^2$ form an sc-structure on $L^2(\mathbb R \times S^1)$, "using Sobolev's compact embedding theorem for bounded domains and the assumption that $(\delta_m)$ is strictly increasing".
notFormalized.instead: **Not formalized.** Mathlib has no weighted Sobolev spaces and no Rellich–Kondrachov theorem; the exposition proves the example in full (Proposition 1.C). The only examples of sc-Banach spaces built here are the constant structure on a finite-dimensional space, and the sums, shifts, sc-subspaces and quotients of sc-Banach spaces (V1.1, V1.4, V1.6). This example, with the shift map of the 2010 paper, is the project's planned step H2.

notFormalized.title: Remark 1.1.17 (preprint 1.15): partial cones in place of partial quadrants
notFormalized.label: §1.1, Remark 1.1.17 (preprint 1.15), p. 10 (preprint p. 11)
notFormalized.book: Instead of a partial quadrant $C$ one may take a closed convex partial cone $P$ ($\lambda P \subset P$ for $\lambda \ge 0$) with non-empty interior; for $U$ open in $P$, $\mathrm{sc}^1$ is defined as in Definition 1.1.15 (preprint 1.14), with the tangent map on $TP = P^1 \oplus E$, again a closed cone with non-empty interior. Many results should carry over, "but one should check carefully which arguments carry over".
notFormalized.instead: **Not formalized**, as in the exposition, which stays with quadrants. The proofs of §§1.2–1.3 use of the quadrant only the sc-domain property (V1.27: open-in-convex level sets with unique derivatives), so they apply to any $U$ with that property; whether relatively open subsets of partial cones have it is not examined. (Proposition 1.2.4 and Corollary 1.2.5 (preprint Propositions 1.19 and 1.20) under the text's hypothesis, listed here until 2026-10-25, are now proved as stated, V1.18–V1.19.)

notFormalized.title: Definition 1.1.15 (preprint 1.14): $Df$ need not be norm continuous
notFormalized.label: §1.1, after Definition 1.1.15 (preprint 1.14), preprint p. 11
notFormalized.book: "In general, the map $U_1 \to \mathcal L(E_0, F_0)$, defined by $x \mapsto Df(x)$, will not(!) be continuous, if the space of bounded linear operators is equipped with the operator norm."
notFormalized.instead: **Formalized since the first edition of this page** (third addendum; V1.13, V1.34), by an example (the text gives none). $X$ is the sc-Banach space of sequences whose level $m$ consists of the $x$ with $(k+1)^m x_k \to 0$, normed by $|x|_m = \sup_k (k+1)^m|x_k|$: every level is a copy of $c_0$, the inclusion $X_{m+1} \to X_m$ is $\mathrm{diag}(1/(k+1))$, compact, and the finitely supported sequences are smooth points dense in every level. On $E = \mathbb R \oplus X$ the map $f(t, x)_k = \cos(kt)x_k$ is $\mathrm{sc}^1$ with $Df(t, x)(\tau, \xi)_k = -k\sin(kt)x_k\tau + \cos(kt)\xi_k$ (the factor $k$ is absorbed by one level). $(\pi/(n+1), 0) \to 0$ in $E_1$, but $\|Df(\pi/(n+1), 0) - Df(0, 0)\| \ge 2$ (test on the unit vector $e_{n+1}$); since the derivative is unique on $E_1$, no derivative family of $f$ is continuous for the operator norm. Not formalized: that $f$ is sc-smooth (it is), and the shift map of the exposition (§6), which needs Example 1.1.3 (preprint 1.2) (G.1).

notFormalized.title: Proposition 2.1.2 (preprint 2.2): classical smooth retractions have submanifold images
notFormalized.label: §2.1, Proposition 2.1.2 (preprint 2.2), p. 22 (preprint p. 18) (proof §2.7.1 (preprint §2.6.1), preprint pp. 54–55)
notFormalized.book: If $r : U \to U$ is a $C^\infty$ retraction of an open subset of a Banach space $E$, then $O = r(U)$ is a $C^\infty$ submanifold: near each $x \in O$ there are a splitting $E = R \oplus N$ and a diffeomorphism $\psi : V \to W$ with $\psi(O \cap V) = R \cap W$ (the text prints $\psi(0) = x$ for $\psi(x) = 0$).
notFormalized.instead: **Not formalized.** The proposition is classical and is used only as motivation (the contrast with sc-smooth retractions, whose images can change dimension). The exposition proves it in §8.1 with the inverse function theorem; its Lean version would need Mathlib's inverse function theorem for $C^\infty$ maps between Banach spaces and the splitting by the projection $Dr(0)$. Not attempted.

notFormalized.title: Definition 2.1.16 (preprint 2.9): sc-smooth bundle retractions and bundle maps
notFormalized.label: §2.1, Definition 2.1.16 (preprint 2.9), p. 29 (preprint p. 22)
notFormalized.book: A trivial sc-bundle $U \oplus F \to U$; an sc-smooth $R(u, v) = (r(u), \rho(u, v))$, $\rho$ linear in $v$, $R \circ R = R$, is an sc-smooth bundle retraction with bundle retract $B = R(U \oplus F) \to O$; bundle maps $\Phi(u, v) = (a(u), \phi(u, v))$ with \"$p' \circ \Phi = p$\" (read $a \circ p$); the category $\mathcal{BR}$ and the functor $T : \mathcal R \to \mathcal{BR}$.
notFormalized.instead: **Formalized since the first edition of this page, apart from the categories** (V2.92). Bundle retractions and bundle maps are defined by their shape, $R(u, v) = (r(u), \rho(u)v)$ on $U \oplus F$ and $\Phi(u, v) = (a(u), \phi(u)v)$ with $\rho(u)$, $\phi(u)$ continuous linear, so $p' \circ \Phi = a \circ p$; $Tr$ is a bundle retraction covering $r^1$ and $Tf$ a bundle map covering $f^1$, and the transition maps of $TX$ are bundle maps (V2.94). Before, the tangent retraction $Tr$ (V2.8) and the strong bundle retractions of §2.6 (preprint §2.5) (V2.54) were the instances the theory used. The categories $\mathcal R$, $\mathcal{BR}$, $\mathcal{SBR}$ and their functors are still not formalized (Findings, Chapter 2, item 76).

notFormalized.title: $X_m$ as an M-polyfold for $m \ge 2$
notFormalized.label: §2.3 (preprint §2.2), after Definition 2.3.8 (preprint 2.14), preprint p. 25
notFormalized.book: For every $m$, the charts $(V_m, \varphi, (O_m, C_m, E_m))$ form an atlas on $X_m$.
notFormalized.instead: **Formalized since the first edition of this page** (V2.93). For $m \ge 2$ the structure is the iterate $(X^1)^1 \cdots$. For every $m$ the identity of points is a homeomorphism $(X^1)_m \cong X_{m+1}$, and the level-$m$ lift of the level chart $\varphi^1$ is the level-$(m+1)$ lift of $\varphi$ (`MPolyfold.shiftLevelHomeomorph`, `MPolyfold.shift_level_eq`), so each iterate is $X_m$ with its topology and the charts $(V_m, \varphi, (O_m, C_m, E_m))$. Since the fourth addendum the points were known to agree, $(X^1)_m = X_{m+1}$ as sets (Findings, Chapter 5, items 142, 146). Theorem 2.3.10 (preprint 2.16) is proved for every $X_m$ directly (V2.17); Proposition 2.3.17, $T(X^i) \equiv (TX)^i$, for every $i$ is V2.97 (Findings, Chapter 2, item 77).

notFormalized.title: Definition 2.3.14 (preprint 2.18): the linear structure of $T_xX$; Proposition 2.3.19 (3) (preprint 2.21) in $T_aX$
notFormalized.label: §2.3 (preprint §2.2), Definition 2.3.14 (preprint 2.18) and Proposition 2.3.19 (3), (4) (preprint 2.21), pp. 38–44 (preprint pp. 26–30)
notFormalized.book: $T_xX$ is a vector space with $\lambda[(x, \varphi, h_1)] + \mu[(x, \varphi, h_2)] = [(x, \varphi, \lambda h_1 + \mu h_2)]$, a Banach space through $T\varphi$, an sc-Banach space at smooth $x$; Proposition 2.3.19 (3) (preprint 2.21): $T_aA$ has an sc-complement in $T_aX$.
notFormalized.instead: **Not formalized.** $T_xX$ is a set identified with $T_{\varphi(x)}O$ by $T\varphi$ (V2.19); the vector space, Banach and sc-structures on it are not defined. Proposition 2.3.19 (3), (4) (preprint 2.21) are proved in a chart (V2.25), which is how the text proves them; their transport to $T_aX$ is not.

notFormalized.title: Proposition 2.3.15 (2) (preprint 2.19): $p : TX \to X_1$ is open
notFormalized.label: §2.3 (preprint §2.2), Proposition 2.3.15 (2) (preprint 2.19), p. 39 (preprint p. 27)
notFormalized.book: The projection $p : TX \to X_1$ is an open map.
notFormalized.instead: **Not formalized** (not used). Continuity of $p$ is V2.20. The exposition's §8.3 proves openness with the $\mathrm{sc}^0$ property of $Tr$.

notFormalized.title: Remark 2.4.8 (preprint 2.28): $C_xO$ need not be a partial quadrant
notFormalized.label: §2.4 (preprint §2.3), Remark 2.4.8 (preprint 2.28), p. 47 (preprint p. 33)
notFormalized.book: Naively one might expect $C_xO$ to be a partial quadrant in $T_xO$; \"however, this is in general not the case\".
notFormalized.instead: **Settled since the first edition of this page, in the negative** (third addendum; V2.33): the claim is false. At every smooth point of every sc-smooth retract, tame or not, $C_xO$ is a partial quadrant in $T_xO$ (with the sc-structure induced from $E$), of dimension $\dim(T_xO/T^R_xO) \le d_C(x)$; the proof reduces it to Flor's theorem on nonnegative idempotent matrices, proved in the needed case. For a non-tame retract only the equality of that dimension with $d_C(x)$ can fail (Theorem 2.4.12 (preprint 2.31)). The text gives no example, and none exists (Findings, Chapter 2, item 50).

notFormalized.title: Lemma 2.4.9 (preprint 2.29): $T^R_xO$ and $C_xO$ through sc-smooth paths; $T_xO = C_xO - C_xO$
notFormalized.label: §2.4 (preprint §2.3), Lemma 2.4.9 (preprint 2.29), pp. 48–49 (preprint pp. 33–35)
notFormalized.book: For a retract and a smooth $x \in O$: (1) $T^R_xO$ is the closure of the derivatives $\dot\alpha(0)$ of sc-smooth paths $\alpha : (-\varepsilon, \varepsilon) \to O$ through $x$; (2) $C_xO$ the closure of the one-sided derivatives of sc-smooth paths $\alpha : [0, \varepsilon) \to O$; (3) $T_xO = C_xO - C_xO$.
notFormalized.instead: **Not formalized in the path formulation.** Sc-smooth paths would need the constant sc-structure on an interval as a retract and the density of smooth points of $T^R_xO$ and $C_xO$ (the exposition's Lemma 3.A on all levels). The sign arguments that the proof consists of are formalized (V2.34), and Proposition 2.4.10 (preprint 2.30) is proved from them, not from the lemma. (3) is not formalized.

notFormalized.title: Theorem 2.4.12 (preprint 2.31), second statement: equality makes $C_xO$ a partial quadrant
notFormalized.label: §2.4 (preprint §2.3), Theorem 2.4.12 (preprint 2.31), p. 50 (preprint p. 35) (second statement)
notFormalized.book: If $\dim(T_xO/T^R_xO) = d_O(x)$, then $C_xO$ is a partial quadrant in $T_xO$.
notFormalized.instead: **Formalized since the first edition of this page** (third addendum; V2.33, V2.37), without the hypothesis: $C_xO$ is a partial quadrant in $T_xO$ at every smooth point of every sc-smooth retract, whatever $\dim(T_xO/T^R_xO)$ is, and the quadrant has dimension $\dim(T_xO/T^R_xO)$, which is $d_O(x)$ under the hypothesis. The sc-Banach structure of $T_xO$ and $T^R_xO$ as an sc-subspace, which the exposition supplied on paper, are proved without tameness; the smooth lifts come from the columns given by Flor's theorem (V2.33).

notFormalized.title: The extended faces of a partial quadrant, intrinsically
notFormalized.label: §2.5 (preprint §2.4), preprint p. 39
notFormalized.book: $\{e \in C : d_C(e) = 1\}$ has exactly $k$ connected components $A_i$; each lies in a smallest subspace $f_i$ (an extended face), with a half-space $H_{f_i} \supset C$; $\mathcal F(e) = \{f : e \in f\}$ and $d_C(e) = \#\mathcal F(e)$.
notFormalized.instead: **Not formalized as stated.** The formalization works with a presentation $T$ of $C$ and takes the coordinate hyperplanes $f_i = \{\lambda_i = 0\}$ as the extended faces (`coordHyper`); that a connected piece of $\{d_C = 1\}$ lies in one $f_i$ is `subset_coordHyper_of_isPreconnected` (V2.45). That $E_x$ does not depend on the presentation is proved (`minimalSubspaceWith_eq`, V2.39); the count of components, the minimality of $f_i$ and the intrinsic description of the extended faces are not formalized.

notFormalized.title: Definition 2.5.8 (preprint 2.38): $T^R_xX$ and $C_xX$ of an M-polyfold
notFormalized.label: §2.5 (preprint §2.4), Definition 2.5.8 (preprint 2.38), p. 57 (preprint p. 42)
notFormalized.book: For a smooth $x \in X$, $T^R_xX$ and $C_xX$ are the preimages of $T^R_oO$ and $C_oO$ under $T\psi(x)$ for any chart $\psi$; well defined by Proposition 2.4.10 (preprint 2.30). For tame $X$, $C_xX$ is a partial quadrant and $d_X(x) = \dim(T_xX/T^R_xX) = d_{C_xX}(0_x)$.
notFormalized.instead: **Only the local form is formalized**: $T^R_xO$ and $C_xO$ in a chart (V2.32) and their invariance under chart changes (V2.35). The global objects in $T_xX$ are not defined, since $T_xX$ carries no linear structure here (G.7); in a tame chart, $d_X(x) = \dim(T_xO/T^R_xO)$ is V2.42. In a tame chart at a smooth point, $C_oO$ is a partial quadrant in $T_oO$ (V2.42); its transport to $T_xX$ and $d_{C_xX}(0_x) = d_X(x)$ are not formalized.

notFormalized.title: Definition 2.6.1 (preprint 2.47): strong bundle isomorphisms; the category $\mathcal{SBR}$
notFormalized.label: §2.6 (preprint §2.5), Definition 2.6.1 (preprint 2.47) and after Definition 2.6.3 (preprint 2.49), pp. 65–67 (preprint pp. 48–51)
notFormalized.book: A strong bundle isomorphism is an invertible strong bundle map with strong bundle inverse. The category $\mathcal{SBR}$ of local strong bundle retracts and the functors $\mathrm{forget}[i] : \mathcal{SBR} \to \mathcal{BR}$.
notFormalized.instead: **Not formalized.** Strong bundle maps and retractions are V2.54; the transition maps of strong bundle charts are required to be sc-smooth on $[0]$ and $[1]$ in both directions (V2.57), which is the isomorphism property in the form it is used.

notFormalized.title: Lemma 2.7.3 (preprint 2.56) and Proposition 2.7.4 (preprint 2.57): closed locally finite refinements
notFormalized.label: §2.7.2 (preprint §2.6.2), Lemma 2.7.3 (preprint 2.56) and Proposition 2.7.4 (preprint 2.57), p. 74 (preprint p. 56)
notFormalized.book: Lemma 2.7.3 (preprint 2.56) (Michael): a regular Hausdorff space is paracompact iff every open cover has a closed locally finite refinement. Proposition 2.7.4 (preprint 2.57): a regular space with a locally finite cover by closed paracompact subspaces is paracompact.
notFormalized.instead: **Not formalized, because not needed.** The proofs of Theorem 2.3.10 (preprint 2.16) and Proposition 2.3.15(3) (preprint 2.19) avoid them (V2.17, V2.20, V2.62). The text applies Proposition 2.7.4 (preprint 2.57) to $X_m$ and $TX$ without checking that they are regular.

notFormalized.title: Remark 2.1.6: the modified local completeness is strictly weaker
notFormalized.label: §2.1, Remark 2.1.6, p. 23 (new in the 2021 edition)
notFormalized.book: Replacing $\mathrm{cl}_X(V(x))$ by the closure of $V(x)$ in $W(x)$ (and $\mathrm{cl}_X(V(x)) \subseteq W(x)$ by $V(x) \subseteq W(x)$) in Definition 2.1.5 gives a weaker notion.
notFormalized.instead: **Formalized since the first edition of this page** (V2.91). The implication is V2.68. $\mathbb R$ with the K-topology ($K = \{1/(n+1)\}$) is Hausdorff and locally complete in the modified sense, but not regular, hence not locally complete in the sense of Definition 2.1.5 (`remark_2_1_6_strict_2021`); so the notion is strictly weaker, and the remark holds as we read it (Findings, Chapter 2, items 61, 75).

notFormalized.title: Definition 2.5.19: chart independence, "a tame sub-M-polyfold is tame", the examples
notFormalized.label: §2.5, condition (3) of Definition 2.5.19 and the text after it, p. 63 (new in the 2021 edition)
notFormalized.book: Condition (3) of Definition 2.5.19 is stated on $T_yX$; the text remarks that a tame sub-M-polyfold is tame and gives examples in $[0, \infty)^2 \times \mathbb R$: $\{(x, y, 0)\}$ is a tame sub-M-polyfold, the diagonal ray $\{(x, x, 0)\}$ is not, although its induced structure is tame.
notFormalized.instead: **Formalized since the first edition of this page** (V2.99, V2.100, V2.101). Condition (3) is still stated in a chart (V2.78), since $T_yX$ has no linear structure here (gap G.7); it holds in every chart, presentation and for every sub-M-polyfold retraction once it holds in one (`TameSubData.hasReducedComplementAt_of_isChart_2021`); a tame sub-M-polyfold of a tame M-polyfold has a tame induced structure (`IsTameSubMPolyfold.hasTameInducedStructure_2021`); and both examples hold as stated, for any $W$ in place of $\mathbb R$ (`TameSubExample.examples_A_B_2021`) (Findings, Chapter 2, items 72, 81, 82).

notFormalized.title: Proposition 2.7.12 and the characterization after Theorem 2.7.13 for non-centred representatives
notFormalized.label: §2.7.4, Proposition 2.7.12, p. 83, and the characterization after Theorem 2.7.13, p. 84 (new in the 2021 edition)
notFormalized.book: For every pair of admissible triples the transition map $\Phi_{(x', V', \theta')} \circ \Phi_{(x, V, \theta)}^{-1}$ is an sc-diffeomorphism; every $\Phi_{(x, V, \theta)}$ is a homeomorphism and an sc-diffeomorphism onto $\theta$.
notFormalized.instead: **Formalized since the first edition of this page** (V2.104, V2.105). For every representative $\Phi_{(x, V, \theta)}$ is an sc-diffeomorphism of $U(x, V, \theta)$ onto the open subset $\theta \cap V^x$ of $\theta$, which is $\theta$ for $V$ centred at $x$ (`phi_isScDiffeoOn_nonCentred_2021`); Proposition 2.7.12 holds as printed for every pair of representatives (`proposition_2_7_12_scDiffeo_nonCentred_2021`); and the structure of $bX$ is characterized with this image (`tameBoundaryPolyfold_unique_allReps_2021`). "Onto $\theta$" does not hold as we read it for every representative: for the slab triple of V2.85 $\Phi$ is not onto $\theta$ (`not_surjOn_phiTot_2021`) (Findings, Chapter 2, items 73, 83, 84).

notFormalized.title: Theorem 3.1.21 (preprint 3.18): parameterized perturbations
notFormalized.label: §3.1, Theorem 3.1.21 (preprint 3.18), p. 100 (preprint p. 74)
notFormalized.book: For a tame strong bundle and an sc-Fredholm section $f$, $s_1, \dots, s_n \in \Gamma^+(P)$: $(r, x) \mapsto f(x) + \sum r_is_i(x)$ is an sc-Fredholm section of $\pi^*(P) \to \mathbb R^n \times X$.
notFormalized.instead: **Formalized since the first edition of this page** (V3.91, V3.92): $(r, x) \mapsto f(x) + \sum r_is_i(x)$ is an sc-Fredholm section of $\pi^*P$ for any strong bundle (tameness not used), by the text's route: $\tilde f$ is sc-Fredholm in the product chart through the translation charts of $\mathbb R^n$ and the $\mathbb R^n$-extension of the basic germ, $\tilde s$ is sc$^+$, and Theorem 3.1.18 (preprint 3.15). The linearization at $(0, x)$ after Theorem 3.1.22 (preprint 3.19) is V3.92; the form for germ data in tame charts is V3.106.

notFormalized.title: Theorem 3.1.22 (preprint 3.19): implicit function theorem, interior case
notFormalized.label: §3.1, Theorem 3.1.22 (preprint 3.19), p. 100 (preprint p. 74)
notFormalized.book: For $d_X \equiv 0$, $f$ sc-Fredholm, $f(x_0) = 0$: $f'(x_0)$ is sc-Fredholm; if it is onto, the solution set near $x_0$ is a smooth manifold of dimension the index, with $f'(y)$ onto and $\ker f'(y) = T_yS$.
notFormalized.instead: **Formalized since the first edition of this page.** First (V3.68) under the filler condition at the nearby zeros, which was the added hypothesis of Theorem 3.6.8 (1) (preprint 3.54) (V3.82) and is now a theorem (V3.102); with the text's hypotheses (V3.95): for $d_X \equiv 0$, an sc-Fredholm section with tame germ data and $(f, x_0)$ in good position in a tame chart (V3.103), an open $U \ni x_0$ in which every zero is a smooth point in good position in a tame chart and $S(f, U)$ is a sub-M-polyfold equivalent to a $d$-dimensional manifold without boundary; with the hypothesis “$f'(x_0)$ surjective” (V3.101); the dimension is the Fredholm index (V3.97), $\ker f'(y) = T_yS$ in the chart (V3.99), and the first clause, “$f'(x_0)$ is sc-Fredholm”, is Proposition 3.6.5 (preprint 3.52) in sc form, in the chart at $x_0$ and in every chart, with $f'(x_0)$ onto on every level (V3.46, V3.96; third addendum).

notFormalized.title: Theorem 3.1.26 (preprint 3.23) and Corollary 3.1.27 (preprint 3.24): implicit function theorem, boundary case
notFormalized.label: §3.1, Theorem 3.1.26 (preprint 3.23) and Corollary 3.1.27 (preprint 3.24), pp. 102–104 (preprint pp. 77–78)
notFormalized.book: At a zero with surjective linearization whose kernel is in good position to $C_xX$, the local solution set consists of smooth points and is a tame sub-M-polyfold with a unique structure of a manifold with boundary with corners; globally if this holds at every zero.
notFormalized.instead: **Formalized since the first edition of this page.** Theorem 3.1.26 (preprint 3.23) (V3.69): the local solution set consists of smooth points and is a tame sub-M-polyfold equivalent to a $d$-dimensional manifold with boundary with corners, when $x$ and the zeros near it are in good position in tame charts (V3.103; or under the filler condition at the nearby zeros, V3.82), and since the second addendum with the text's hypotheses (V3.95), with the dimension as the Fredholm index (V3.97). Corollary 3.1.27 (preprint 3.24) (V3.70) with the text's hypotheses: good position in a tame chart at every zero gives a sub-M-polyfold with tame induced structure, a manifold with boundary with corners of locally constant dimension.

notFormalized.title: Remark 3.3.8 (preprint 3.36): the quantitative solution germ
notFormalized.label: §3.3, Remark 3.3.8 (preprint 3.36), p. 113 (preprint p. 89)
notFormalized.book: Decreasing sequences $(\varepsilon_i)$, $(\tau_i)$ with: $\delta$ on $\{|a|_0 \le \varepsilon_0\}$ a continuous solution, unique for $|w|_0 \le \tau_0$; $\delta(a) \in W_i$, $|\delta(a)|_i \le \tau_i$ for $|a|_0 \le \varepsilon_i$; $\delta : \{|a|_0 \le \varepsilon_i\} \to W_i$ of class $C^i$.
notFormalized.instead: **Not formalized in quantitative form.** Its content is Theorem 3.3.2 (preprint 3.29) (existence, uniqueness in $O(0)$, $\delta_i(a) \in K(i)$; V3.26) and Corollary 3.3.7 (preprint 3.34) with $m = k = i$ (V3.31), with $\varepsilon_i$ below the radius of $N(2i + 2^i - 1)$.

notFormalized.title: Corollary 3.4.3 (preprint 3.39): composition with a given conjugation
notFormalized.label: §3.4, Corollary 3.4.3 (preprint 3.39), p. 116 (preprint p. 93)
notFormalized.book: If $g$ is equivalent by a strong bundle isomorphism $\Phi$ to a basic germ and $s$ is an sc$^+$-germ, there is $\Psi$ with $((\Psi \circ \Phi)_*(g + s))^1$ basic.
notFormalized.instead: **Formalized since the first edition of this page** (V3.76): for $g$ sc-smooth and conjugated to a basic germ and $s$ sc-smooth into $F^1$ with $s(0) = 0$, $(g + s)^1$ is conjugated to a basic germ on the shifted structures, by the composite of the index raise of the given conjugation and the linear coordinate change of Theorem 3.4.2 (preprint 3.38).

notFormalized.title: Proposition 3.1.10 (preprint 3.10), second statement, on levels $m \ge 1$
notFormalized.label: §3.1, Proposition 3.1.10 (preprint 3.10), p. 95 (preprint p. 68)
notFormalized.book: $Df(a, w) : \mathbb R^n \oplus W_m \to \mathbb R^N \oplus W_m$ is Fredholm of index $n - N$ for $(a, w) \in E_{m+1}$ small in $E_m$, for every $m$.
notFormalized.instead: **Formalized since the first edition of this page** (third addendum; V3.12): for every $m$ there is $\delta > 0$ such that $Df(x)_m : \mathbb R^n \oplus W_m \to \mathbb R^N \oplus W_m$ is Fredholm of index $n - N$ at every $x \in U_{m+1}$ with $|x|_m < \delta$, by the text's proof on level $m$; the input it needed, Lemma 3.1.9 (preprint 3.9) on level $m$ with arbitrary $\varepsilon$, is proved as stated (V3.11).

notFormalized.title: Proposition 3.6.5 (preprint 3.52) as an sc-Fredholm operator on $T_xX$
notFormalized.label: §3.6, Proposition 3.6.5 (preprint 3.52), p. 135 (preprint p. 110)
notFormalized.book: $Tf(x) : T_xX \to Y_x$ is an sc-Fredholm operator.
notFormalized.instead: **Formalized since the first edition of this page** (third addendum; V3.46, V3.96), in charts. In the chart of Definition 3.1.11 (preprint 3.11) centred at the zero, $T_0O = Dr(0)E$ and $K_0 = \rho(0)F$ are sc-subspaces and $Tf(x_0) = Dg(0)|_{T_0O} : T_0O \to K_0$ is sc-Fredholm, of index $n - N$ on every level for every conjugating basic germ; in **every** strong bundle chart around a zero $y$, at the point $z$ over $y$, $\mathrm{Lin}(z) : T_zO \to K_z$ is sc-Fredholm, the levels being transported between charts at smooth points. No tameness is used. $T_xX$ and $Y_x$ themselves carry no linear structure here (G.7), so “an sc-Fredholm operator on $T_xX$” is read in charts.

notFormalized.title: Theorem 3.6.8 (1) (preprint 3.54) with the text's hypotheses: surjectivity of $f'(y)$ at the nearby zeros
notFormalized.label: §3.6, Theorem 3.6.8 (1) (preprint 3.54), pp. 136–139 (preprint pp. 111–114)
notFormalized.book: (1) At every zero $y$ near $x$ the germ $(f, y)$ is in good position, “from Corollary 3.41 and Lemma 3.55”; (2) the solution set near $x$ is a sub-M-polyfold with the structure of a manifold with boundary with corners.
notFormalized.instead: **Formalized since the first edition of this page** (V3.93, V3.94): with the text's hypotheses (tame germ data, good position in a tame chart, V3.103), every zero $y$ near $x_0$ is in good position in a tame chart, in particular $f'(y)$ is onto. The text's argument does not give the surjectivity (it gives that of the filled linearization only; the same step is in the book's arXiv version); it is proved by an implicit function theorem at the nearby zero for $g + \mu\rho(r(\cdot))\lambda$, with Theorem 3.3.3 (preprint 3.30) at the centre for a contraction germ whose regions in $a$ do not depend on $\lambda$ (Findings, Chapter 3, items 180–189). The first form under the filler condition at the nearby zeros (V3.82) is kept; that condition follows from good position (V3.102). (2) is proved from (1) (V3.85, V3.94); the index is locally constant along the solution set (V3.98).

notFormalized.title: Theorem 3.7.1 (preprint 3.58): the basic germ criterion
notFormalized.label: §3.7, Theorem 3.7.1 (preprint 3.58), pp. 140–145 (preprint pp. 116–120)
notFormalized.book: Under (1) $Df(x)$ sc-Fredholm of constant index at smooth points, (2) a splitting $E = B \oplus X$ with a compactness condition, (3) a uniform estimate on $D_2f$: $f - f(0)$ is conjugated near $0$ to a basic germ.
notFormalized.instead: **Formalized since the first edition of this page**, in the coordinates of the text's proof ($E = \mathbb R^n \oplus X$, $F = \mathbb R^N \oplus Y$; V3.89, with the second half of the proof V3.88): under (1)–(3), $f - f(0)$ is conjugated near $0$ to a basic germ. The reduction of a general sc-splitting to these coordinates is not formalized.

notFormalized.title: Lemmas 3.8.1–3.8.3 (preprint 3.62–3.64): extreme rays
notFormalized.label: §3.8.1, Lemmas 3.8.1–3.8.3 (preprint 3.62–3.64), pp. 145–147 (preprint pp. 121–122)
notFormalized.book: A closed convex cone in finite dimensions is the closed convex hull of its extreme rays (3.62); a cone with interior is a quadrant iff it has $\dim N$ extreme rays (3.63, from [21]); a generator $a$ of an extreme ray of $N \cap C$ has $\dim N - 1 \le \#\sigma_a$ (3.64).
notFormalized.instead: **Superseded, not formalized**: the proof of Proposition 3.1.25 (preprint 3.22) (V3.21) avoids extreme rays (a segment argument and Lemma 3.8.8 (preprint 3.65); Findings, Chapter 3, item 18).

notFormalized.title: Lemmas 3.8.9–3.8.11 (preprint 3.66–3.68): the complement $\widetilde N$
notFormalized.label: §3.8.1, Lemmas 3.8.9–3.8.11 (preprint 3.66–3.68), pp. 150–152 (preprint pp. 123–125)
notFormalized.book: $\widetilde N$ is in good position with good complement $(N \cap W) \oplus N^\perp$ (3.66); $C \cap \widetilde N$ is a closed convex cone whose extreme rays satisfy $\dim\widetilde N - 1 = \#\sigma_a = d_C(a)$ (3.67); either $\widetilde N \cap (\mathbb R^{\Sigma^c} \oplus W) = \{0\}$ or $\widetilde N \subseteq \mathbb R^{\Sigma^c} \oplus W$ with $\dim\widetilde N = 1$, $\Sigma = \emptyset$ (3.68).
notFormalized.instead: **Superseded, not formalized as stated**: the normal form of Proposition 3.1.25 (preprint 3.22) (V3.21) treats the three cases $N \cap C = N$, $\Sigma = \emptyset$, $\Sigma \ne \emptyset$ directly; the content of Lemma 3.8.11's (preprint 3.68) second case is `quadrantNormalForm_of_vanIdx_empty`.

notFormalized.title: Definition 3.8.14 (preprint 3.71): class $C^k$ on partial quadrants
notFormalized.label: §3.8.5 (preprint §3.8.4), Definition 3.8.14 (preprint 3.71), p. 164 (preprint p. 135)
notFormalized.book: $f : U \to \mathbb R^m$ on a relatively open subset of a partial quadrant is $C^1$ if it has one-sided derivatives depending continuously on $x$; $C^k$ if $f$ and $Tf$ are $C^{k-1}$.
notFormalized.instead: **Not formalized separately**: the theorems of §§3.8.5–3.8.6 (preprint §§3.8.4–3.8.5) use Mathlib's $C^k$ within the set (`ContDiffOn`), which on relatively open subsets of partial quadrants agrees with sc$^1$ = $C^1$ (`isSc1_iff_contDiffOn_of_isRelOpenInQuadrant`, Chapter 1, V1.35).

notFormalized.title: Lemma 3.8.20 (preprint 3.76): iterated tangent maps
notFormalized.label: §3.8.5 (preprint §3.8.4), Lemma 3.8.20 (preprint 3.76), p. 167 (preprint p. 139)
notFormalized.book: Under the assumptions of Proposition 3.8.17 (preprint 3.73) the iterated tangent maps $T^kf : T^kU \to T^kV$ are smooth homeomorphisms.
notFormalized.instead: **Superseded, not formalized**: the regularity of $f^{-1}$ is proved by bootstrapping $Dg = [Df]^{-1} \circ g$ (V3.59, V3.62; Findings, Chapter 3, item 28).

notFormalized.title: Lemma 3.8.13 (preprint 3.70) and Lemma 3.6.9 (preprint 3.55) in a general presentation of $C$; Theorem 3.2.3 (preprint 3.27) and $d_X$
notFormalized.label: §§3.8.1, §3.8.4 (preprint §3.8.1, §3.8.3), Lemmas 3.8.13, 3.6.9 (preprint 3.70, 3.55); §3.2, proof of Theorem 3.2.3 (preprint 3.27), preprint p. 127
notFormalized.book: Lemma 3.6.9 (preprint 3.55) is stated for any partial quadrant $C \subseteq E$; the proof of Theorem 3.2.3 (preprint 3.27) uses Lemma 3.8.13 (preprint 3.70) to get $d_{N \cap C}(v) = d_X(y)$.
notFormalized.instead: **Lemma 3.8.13 (preprint 3.70) is formalized in the model $\mathbb R^n \oplus W$**; Lemma 3.6.9 (preprint 3.55) in the model, in coordinates for functionals cutting out $C$, and, since the first edition of this page, for any presentation of $C$ and $\sigma$ on a relatively open domain (V3.80). The transport of Lemma 3.8.13 (preprint 3.70) to a general presentation, and hence $d_M = d_X$ on $M$ in Theorem 3.2.3 (preprint 3.27), is not done (Findings, Chapter 3, item 84).

notFormalized.title: Theorem 3.1.22 (preprint 3.19): the dimension is the index; $\ker f'(y) = T_yS$; good position for $d_X \equiv 0$
notFormalized.label: §3.1, Theorem 3.1.22 (preprint 3.19), p. 100 (preprint p. 74)
notFormalized.book: The solution set near $x_0$ is a manifold whose dimension agrees with the Fredholm index of $f'(x_0)$; at its points $\ker f'(y) = T_yS(f, U)$; and for $d_X(x) = 0$ good position is the surjectivity of $f'(x)$.
notFormalized.instead: **Formalized since the first edition of this page** (second addendum).
