The dimension: the dimension $d$ of the solution set near a zero in good position is $\dim\ker f'(y) = \mathrm{ind}\,f'(y)$ at every zero $y$ near it, in every chart (V3.97, with V3.96), also in Theorems 3.1.26, 3.6.11 (preprint 3.23, 3.57), and the index is locally constant along the solution set (V3.98). The kernel: $D\psi$ maps $\ker f'(y)$, read in the chart at $x_0$, onto the tangent space of the solution graph (V3.99); $T_yS$ as a subspace of $T_yX$ is not formalized (Chapter 2 gap G.13). Good position in a tame chart at $d_X(y) = 0$ is surjectivity, for tame germ data (V3.100), so Theorems 3.1.22 and 3.6.10 (preprint 3.19 and 3.56) hold with “$f'(x)$ surjective” (V3.101).

notFormalized.title: The 2021 (untamed) sc-Fredholm germs: tame fillings, and Theorem 3.6.8 for untamed data
notFormalized.label: §3.1 and §3.6, Definitions 3.1.4, 3.6.1 and Theorem 3.6.8, pp. 91, 134–138; with Theorems 3.1.22, 3.1.26, Corollary 3.1.27, Theorems 3.6.10, 3.6.11
notFormalized.book: The 2021 filling asks only for an sc-smooth retraction (no tameness). Theorem 3.6.8 describes the solution set near a zero in good position; its proof (p. 138) uses that the retract is tame. Theorems 3.1.22, 3.1.26, Corollary 3.1.27 and Theorems 3.6.10, 3.6.11 rest on it.
notFormalized.instead: **Open.** Whether every 2021 sc-Fredholm germ has germ data in a tame chart (Findings, Chapter 3, item 353), and Theorem 3.6.8 and the results resting on it for untamed germ data, are not formalized. The proof step on p. 138 does not go through without a tame chart (V3.115). These theorems are verified with tame germ data (V3.85, V3.94, V3.103); the 2021 corollaries whose proofs do not use tameness are V3.111–V3.114.

notFormalized.title: Remark 4.1.3 (preprint 4.3): “$X^1 \ne X$ is possible”
notFormalized.label: §4.1, Remark 4.1.3 (preprint 4.3), p. 176 (preprint p. 148)
notFormalized.book: If $X_0 = X_\infty$, then $X_m = X_0$ as sets for all $m$; "however, it is possible that $X^1 \ne X$ as sc-smooth spaces despite the fact that $(X^1)_m = X_{m+1} = X_i$ as sets".
notFormalized.instead: **Formalized since the first edition of this page** (fourth addendum; V4.6), by an example the preprint and 2017 texts do not give. The 2021 edition (p. 176) adds an example: the space of its Subsection 1.4.4 (a line with a half-plane attached), made an M-polyfold with $X_\infty = X$, for which $1_0^1$ cannot be sc-smooth, since Theorem 4.1.2 (preprint 4.2) would make $X$ a manifold of constant local dimension; that argument holds as we read it and is not formalized (Findings, Chapter 4, item 159). On the weighted sequence space $X$ of V1.13 ($|x|_m = \sup_k(k+1)^m|x_k|$), $L(t)$ is the projection onto $\cos\theta\,e_{n_k} + \sin\theta\,e_{n_{k+1}}$ ($n_k = 2^k$), the angle $\theta$ turning from $0$ to $\pi/2$ with flat ends while $t$ runs through $[1/(k+2), 1/(k+1)]$, and $L(t) = 0$ for $t \le 0$. The retraction $r(t, z) = (t, L(t)z)$ of $\mathbb R \oplus X$ is sc-smooth by a criterion for parameter families of level operators with one level of loss; its retract $O$ consists of smooth points, and the lift $O \to E_1$ is discontinuous at $0$, so $O$ is not an sc⁺-retract (Proposition 4.1.8 (preprint 4.8)), and the M-polyfold $O$ with its single chart has $X_0 = X_\infty$ and $1_0^1$ not sc-smooth. Why an example needs a retraction that loses a level (one with $C^1$ level maps gives none) is an argument, not formalized (Findings, Chapter 4, items 140–146).

notFormalized.title: Lemma 4.1.11 (preprint 4.10): the section $u \mapsto (1 - p)(u - t(u))$ is sc-Fredholm
notFormalized.label: §4.1, Lemma 4.1.11 (preprint 4.10), pp. 179–181 (preprint pp. 151–153)
notFormalized.book: The section $u \mapsto (u, \mathbf f(u))$, $\mathbf f(u) = (1 - p)(u - t(u))$, of the local strong bundle $U \triangleleft Y \to U$ is sc-Fredholm.
notFormalized.instead: **Not formalized, because no longer used**: Proposition 4.1.9 (preprint 4.9), its only use, is proved directly (V4.20–V4.25). It would need $U \triangleleft Y$ as a strong bundle, $Y$ and $Y \cap F$ as sc-subspaces, the sc-isomorphism $E \cong (T_0O \oplus B) \oplus W$ with $B \subseteq Y_\infty$, and at each smooth point the re-centred strong bundle chart (V4.18), filler and conjugation. The text's proof has a sign slip in $D\mathbf f(u)$, calls $D\mathbf f(u)$ an sc⁺-operator, writes $L(T_0O)$ for $L(Y)$, and omits the interior points of $(T_0O \oplus B) \cap C$ (Findings, item 57).

notFormalized.title: Remark 4.2.2 (preprint 4.14): the local form near $\{d_X = 0\}$
notFormalized.label: §4.2, Remark 4.2.2 (preprint 4.14), p. 184 (preprint p. 157)
notFormalized.book: Near points $a \in A$ with $d_X(a) = 0$ the submanifold $A$ is a smooth finite-dimensional manifold in the classical sense.
notFormalized.instead: **Formalized only globally**: if $d_X = 0$ on all of $A$, $A$ has a corner structure, without tameness of $X$ (V4.32). The local statement, for the open piece $A \cap \{d_X = 0\}$ of an arbitrary $A$, is not formalized (Findings, item 61).

notFormalized.title: The open question after Proposition 4.2.3 (preprint 4.15)
notFormalized.label: §4.2, Open Question, preprint p. 159
notFormalized.book: Is a sub-M-polyfold with $A = A_\infty$ and $\dim T_aA$ finite and locally constant a smooth finite-dimensional submanifold? Is the "T" $\{(x, 0) : |x| < 1\} \cup \{(0, y) : 0 \le y < 1\}$ homeomorphic to a retract $O = O_\infty$? Impossible for sc⁺-retracts.
notFormalized.instead: **Not formalized** (a question, not a statement). The last sentence, for a retract without boundary, is V4.32 with $A = O$: an sc⁺-retract in $(O, E, E)$ is a manifold; that the "T" is not a topological manifold is not formalized (Findings, item 65).

notFormalized.title: Theorem 4.2.11 (1) (preprint 4.22): local faces of the chart as global local faces
notFormalized.label: §4.2, Theorem 4.2.11 (1) (preprint 4.22), p. 190 (preprint p. 162)
notFormalized.book: There are precisely $d = d_X(x)$ local faces $F_1, \dots, F_d$ contained in $U$.
notFormalized.instead: **Formalized for the chart model only** (V4.50): $d_X(x) = n$, all coordinates vanish at the centre, and $\psi(x)$ lies in exactly $d_X(x)$ faces of the M-polyfold $O$. The identification of these faces with (germs of) global faces of $X$ (Theorem 2.5.17 (preprint 2.45) in the face-structured case) is not formalized (Findings, items 86, 90). The text's local faces are faces of the neighbourhood $U$ itself (closures in $U$ of the components of $U \cap \{d_X = 1\}$), so (4) is affected as well; the missing step is a local face theorem for small neighbourhoods, believed true for tame $X$ (Findings, Chapter 4, item 130; third addendum).

notFormalized.title: Theorem 4.3.1 (preprint 4.23): chart independence of stratified regularity
notFormalized.label: §4.3, proof of Theorem 4.3.1 (preprint 4.23), p. 194 (preprint p. 166)
notFormalized.book: Regular values of the maps $p_\sigma : A \cap F_\sigma^\circ \to \mathbb R^m$, intrinsic to $A$ and its strata.
notFormalized.instead: **Not formalized.** Stratified regularity is defined in some product chart (V4.53); its independence of the chart is true by the transport argument of V4.39 (the transition maps of product charts are $\mathrm{id} \times \tau$ up to translation) but not formalized. Theorem 4.3.1 (preprint 4.23) is unaffected: it produces $\Sigma$ (Findings, items 102, 108).

notFormalized.title: Definition 4.4.1 (preprint 4.25): sc-differential forms and the directed system
notFormalized.label: §4.4, Definition 4.4.1 (preprint 4.25), p. 195 (preprint p. 167)
notFormalized.book: An sc-differential $k$-form is an sc-smooth $\omega : \oplus^kTX \to \mathbb R$, linear in each argument and skew-symmetric; pull-back along $X^{i+1} \to X^i$ gives a directed system with limit $\Omega^*_\infty(X)$.
notFormalized.instead: **Not formalized.** It needs $\oplus^kTX$ as an M-polyfold, a linear $T_xX$ (gap G.7) and the M-polyfolds $X^i$ for $i \ge 2$ with $(TX)^i \cong T(X^i)$ (gap G.6, closed by Proposition 2.3.17 for every $i$). The text writes $\Omega^*_\infty$ for both the limit and the sum (Findings, item 124).

notFormalized.title: Proposition 4.4.5 (preprint 4.26): the Lie bracket of sc-smooth vector fields
notFormalized.label: §4.4, Proposition 4.4.5 (preprint 4.26), p. 196 (preprint p. 167)
notFormalized.book: (2021) For sc-smooth vector fields $A$, $B$ on $X$ the usual formula defines an sc-smooth section $[A, B]$ of $TX|X^2 \to X^2$, proved in Appendix 4.5 (§§4.5.1–4.5.2, pp. 200–202). The preprint and 2017 texts state an sc-smooth vector field on $X^1$, a section of $T(X^1) \to X^2$, quoted from another paper.
notFormalized.instead: **Formalized since the first edition of this page** (Springer 2021 additions; V4.74–V4.77), on an M-polyfold: $[A, B] : X^2 \to TX$, the bracket of the principal parts in any chart, is sc-smooth and covers the inclusion $X^2 \to X^1$ (`proposition_4_4_5_2021`, V4.76), independently of the chart (V4.75), by Lemma 4.5.1, whose proof the text leaves to the reader and which is proved by the computation of §4.5.2 in a local model (V4.74) and on M-polyfolds for every sc-smooth map (V4.77); the local model is V4.67–V4.72 (gap G.38, closed). "Section of $TX|X^2 \to X^2$" is read as a map $X^2 \to TX$ over the inclusion; the pull-back bundle itself and Lemma 4.5.1 for local sc-diffeomorphisms between open subsets are gap G.92. The sentence of p. 201 that the bracket at $x \in O_2$ lies on level $1$ does not hold as we read it (V4.73) (Findings, Chapter 4, items 155–157, 161, 162).

notFormalized.title: The exterior derivative, Definition 4.4.6 (preprint 4.27) and the relative complex
notFormalized.label: §4.4, pp. 195–199 (preprint pp. 167–168), Definition 4.4.6 (preprint 4.27)
notFormalized.book: $d : \Omega^k(X^{i+1}) \to \Omega^{k+1}(X^i)$ by the usual formula, $d^2 = 0$; $H^*_{sc}(X) = \ker d/\operatorname{im} d$; the relative complex $\Omega^*_\infty(X) \oplus \Omega^{*-1}_\infty(\partial X)$ with $d(\omega, \tau) = (d\omega, j^*\omega - d\tau)$.
notFormalized.instead: **Not formalized.** The direction of $d$ should presumably be $\Omega^k(X^i) \to \Omega^{k+1}(X^{i+1})$ (the bracket lives one level up); $d \circ d = 0$ and $dj^* = j^*d$ are asserted without proof; forms on $\partial X$, a union of faces, are not defined (Findings, items 120–122).

notFormalized.title: Theorem 4.4.7 (preprint 4.28): Stokes' theorem
notFormalized.label: §4.4, Theorem 4.4.7 (preprint 4.28), p. 199 (preprint p. 168)
notFormalized.book: For an oriented compact tame smooth $n$-dimensional submanifold $N$ whose boundary is a union of faces $F$, and an sc-differential $(n - 1)$-form $\omega$, $\int_N d\omega = \sum_F\int_F\omega$.
notFormalized.instead: **Not formalized** (no proof in the text; integration on manifolds with corners of varying dimension is not in Mathlib). The formula writes $\int_M$ for $\int_N$ (Findings, item 123).

notFormalized.title: 2021 §4.4 and Appendix 4.5: sc-differential forms, the exterior derivative, Stokes, the Poincaré lemma
notFormalized.label: §4.4 and Appendix 4.5, pp. 195–208 (2021)
notFormalized.book: Definitions 4.4.1–4.4.2 (forms on the Whitney sum $\oplus_kTX$, the direct limit $\Omega^*_\infty(X)$), the exterior derivative $d : \Omega^k(X^i) \to \Omega^{k+1}(X^{i+1})$ with $d^2 = 0$, Definition 4.4.6 and the relative complex, Theorem 4.4.7 (Stokes), the Poincaré Lemma 4.4.8 (p. 199) and its local form Lemma 4.5.2 (p. 202, proved in §4.5.3).
notFormalized.instead: **Not formalized** (continues G.37–G.40). It needs $\oplus_kTX$ as an M-polyfold bundle, a linear $T_xX$ (gap G.7), the M-polyfolds $X^i$ with $(TX)^i \cong T(X^i)$ for all $i$ (gap G.6, closed), and integration on manifolds with corners. The vector fields of Definition 4.4.3, Lemma 4.4.4 (for every $i$), the bracket of Proposition 4.4.5 and Lemma 4.5.1 are formalized, in a local model (V4.67–V4.72, V4.74) and on an M-polyfold (V4.68, V4.75–V4.79). The 2021 text runs $d$ as G.39 proposed and writes $\int_N$; in the displayed formula for $d\omega$ (p. 197) the sign $(-1)^{\ell+k}$ and the summation index $i$ are possible misprints for $(-1)^{\ell+j}$ and $j$ (Findings, Chapter 4, item 158).

notFormalized.title: Lemma 4.5.1 for local sc-diffeomorphisms between open subsets; the pull-back bundle $TX|X^2 \to X^2$
notFormalized.label: §4.4, Proposition 4.4.5, p. 196, and Appendix 4.5, Lemma 4.5.1, p. 201 (2021)
notFormalized.book: (New in the 2021 edition.) Lemma 4.5.1: a local sc-diffeomorphism $\varphi : X \to X$ that relates two vector fields relates their brackets. Proposition 4.4.5: the bracket is an sc-smooth section of the pull-back $TX|X^2 \to X^2$ of $TX \to X^1$ by the inclusion $X^2 \to X^1$.
notFormalized.instead: **Formalized for every sc-smooth map $f : X \to Y$ of M-polyfolds** (V4.77), with the relations on $X^1$, and with the bracket an sc-smooth map $X^2 \to TX$ over the inclusion (V4.76). **Not formalized:** a local sc-diffeomorphism between open subsets of $X$, which would need open subsets of an M-polyfold as M-polyfolds (it is covered only when it is the restriction of such an $f$), and the pull-back bundle $TX|X^2 \to X^2$ as a bundle object (Findings, Chapter 4, item 163).

notFormalized.title: Corollary 5.2.5 (preprint 5.8) beyond the chart level
notFormalized.label: §5.2, Corollary 5.2.5 (preprint 5.8), p. 213 (preprint p. 173)
notFormalized.book: $f^i$ is an sc-Fredholm section of $P^i : Y^i \to X^i$ with compact solution set ("it is a priori clear that $f^i$ is sc-Fredholm").
notFormalized.instead: **Formalized since the first edition of this page, for each fixed $i$** (fourth addendum; V5.13, V5.14). The shifted strong bundle $P^1 : Y^1 \to X^1$ is built (total space $Y_{1,1}$, the index raises of the strong bundle charts as atlas), and $f^1$ is an sc-Fredholm section of it with compact solution set, with condition (3) of the filling on level $1$ proved for the data of Definition 3.1.11 (preprint 3.11) (by Lemma 3.1.20 (preprint 3.17) and Proposition 3.6.5 (preprint 3.52) in sc form; it does not follow from level $0$ alone); $f^2$ on $P^2 = (P^1)^1$ by iteration, and so every fixed $i$. Not formalized: one statement for a family $P^i$ indexed by $i$ and the tame form of the conclusion (the tameness of the index raises of tame charts) (Findings, Chapter 5, items 140–146). The identification of $(X^1)^1$ with $X_2$ as topological spaces is V2.93 (gap G.6, closed).

notFormalized.title: The metric $\rho$ on $\Gamma^{+,1}_U(P)$
notFormalized.label: §5.3, preprint p. 174
notFormalized.book: $\Gamma^{+,1}_U(P)$ "becomes a metric space with respect to the uniform distance $\rho(s, s') = \sup_xN(s(x) - s'(x))$. The metric space $(\Gamma^{+,1}_U(P), \rho)$ is not complete."
notFormalized.instead: **Formalized since the first edition of this page, with a correction** (fourth addendum; V5.21). $\rho$ is a metric on $\Gamma^{+,1}_U(P)$ for every auxiliary norm ($\rho \le 2$); the density statements $N(s(x) - s'(x)) \le \varepsilon$ of V5.30, V5.39 are $\rho(s, s') \le \varepsilon$. “Not complete” is proved for the trivial bundle $\mathbb R \times \mathbb R \to \mathbb R$ ($N(x, v) = |v|$, $U = \mathbb R$) and is false without a hypothesis: the space is complete for $U = \emptyset$ and over a point with finite-dimensional fibre. Not formalized: a general sufficient condition for non-completeness, and the identification of the metric completion with the sections of Remark 5.3.4 (preprint 5.12) (V5.22) (Findings, Chapter 5, items 150–153).

notFormalized.title: Remark 5.3.6 (preprint 5.14)
notFormalized.label: §5.3, Remark 5.3.6 (preprint 5.14), p. 218 (preprint p. 175)
notFormalized.book: In [21] the fibres were separable sc-Hilbert spaces and auxiliary norms had more properties involving weak convergence; neither is needed here, "due to an improved treatment of the compactness".
notFormalized.instead: **Not formalized** (a comment on [21]). The formalization indeed assumes neither: the fibres are arbitrary and Definition 5.1.1 (preprint 5.1) is as stated (V5.3, V5.10).

notFormalized.title: Remark 5.3.8 (preprint 5.16)
notFormalized.label: §5.3, Remark 5.3.8 (preprint 5.16), pp. 219–220 (preprint pp. 176–177)
notFormalized.book: For transversal $f_0$, $f_1$ joined by a sc-Fredholm arc $(t, x) \mapsto f_t(x)$ with compact solution set, a perturbation $s$ vanishing near $t = 0, 1$ makes the arc transversal, and its solution set is a compact cobordism; "the reader will be able to carry out this construction in more detail".
notFormalized.instead: **Not formalized** (a sketch, left to the reader; it needs the boundary case of Theorem 5.3.12 (preprint 5.19) on $[0, 1] \times X$).

notFormalized.title: A dense form of Theorem 5.3.12 (preprint 5.19)
notFormalized.label: §5.3, Theorem 5.3.12 (preprint 5.19), p. 222 (preprint p. 180)
notFormalized.book: "There exists an arbitrarily small section $s \in \Gamma^{+,1}_U(P)$ satisfying $s(x) = 0$ near $\partial X$" with the properties of the theorem.
notFormalized.instead: **Not formalized in the dense form.** The generic form gives $s_\lambda = \sum\lambda_it_i$ for $\lambda$ off a null set of a small ball, so arbitrarily small as $\lambda \to 0$ (V5.40); density around a given allowable $s'$, as in Theorems 5.3.5 and 5.3.10 (preprint 5.13 and 5.18), is not stated (Findings, Chapter 5, item 89).

notFormalized.title: Finding 88: the parametrized section at the boundary zeros
notFormalized.label: §5.3, proof of Theorem 5.3.12 (preprint 5.19), p. 222 (preprint p. 180)
notFormalized.book: "Then we consider as before the section $(\lambda, x) \mapsto f(x) + \sum\lambda_is_i(x)$, and, for a generic value of $\lambda$ ... the associated section $s_\lambda$ has the desired properties."
notFormalized.instead: **Checked on paper only.** At a zero $(0, x)$, $x \in \partial X$, where all $s_i$ vanish, $\ker F'(0, x) = \mathbb R^m \times \ker f'(x)$ is in good position to $\mathbb R^m \times C_x$ only if $\ker f'(x) + E_x \supseteq T_xX$, a general position condition that good position does not imply ($\mathbb R(1, 1)$ in $[0, \infty)^2$). So "as before" cannot apply Theorem 3.6.8 (preprint 3.54) to $F$ there; the formal proof avoids these points (V5.40) (Findings, Chapter 5, item 88).

notFormalized.title: Remark 5.3.14 (preprint 5.21)
notFormalized.label: §5.3, Remark 5.3.14 (preprint 5.21), p. 223 (preprint p. 181)
notFormalized.book: Instead of $(f|X_i, P|Y_i) = (f_i, P_i)$ one should require that the problems are isomorphic and make this part of the data.
notFormalized.instead: **Not formalized.** Definition 5.3.13 (preprint 5.20) takes the restrictions to $t^{-1}(0)$, $t^{-1}(1)$ as the end problems (V5.41) (Findings, Chapter 5, item 100).

notFormalized.title: Theorem 5.3.15 (preprint 5.22): Morse-type structure
notFormalized.label: §5.3, Theorem 5.3.15 (preprint 5.22), p. 223 (preprint p. 181) (proof pp. 223–228 (preprint pp. 181–186))
notFormalized.book: For a generalized compact homotopy with end problems in general position and $\partial X = X_0 \sqcup X_1$, an arbitrarily small $s_0 \in \Gamma^{+,1}_U(P)$ vanishing near $\partial X$ makes $(f + s_0, x)$ in general position at every zero and $t : S_{f+s_0} \to [0, 1]$ a function with only Morse-type critical points.
notFormalized.instead: **Not formalized.** It needs finite-dimensional Morse theory on manifolds with boundary, the cotangent bundle of the solution set, a parametric Sard theorem and a trivialization $\Phi_\lambda : S \to S_\lambda$ of the family (not "the classical standard implicit function theorem"); its proof also needs $dt(x) \ne 0$ at the critical points of $t|S$, which the preprint and 2017 statements do not assume (V5.42); the 2021 Definition 5.3.13 (3) asks $dt(x)$ onto at every smooth point and so supplies it (`lemma_5_3_16_2021`, V5.69), but the theorem itself is still not formalized. Lemmas 5.3.16, 5.3.17 (preprint 5.23, 5.24) are V5.42–V5.44 (Findings, Chapter 5, items 101, 103, 178).

notFormalized.title: Theorem 5.27 (preprint; not in the 2021 edition): cobordism between good position perturbations
notFormalized.label: §5.3, Theorem 5.27 (preprint), preprint p. 188
notFormalized.book: For a proper homotopy $f_t$ and perturbations $s_0$, $s_1$ putting $f + s_i$ in good position, there is $s(x, t)$ with $s(\cdot, i) = s_i$ such that $f + s$ is in good position at all smooth points; its solution set is a compact manifold with corners meeting $\{i\} \times X$ in $S_0$, $S_1$.
notFormalized.instead: **Not formalized**: "the proof is left to the reader" (Findings, Chapter 5, item 104).

notFormalized.title: Theorem 5.5.5 (preprint 5.32): Bonic–Frampton
notFormalized.label: §5.5 (preprint §5.4.2), Theorem 5.5.5 (preprint 5.32), p. 230 (preprint p. 193)
notFormalized.book: On $L^p$, $\|\cdot\|^p$ is $C^\infty$ for $p$ an even integer, $C^{p-1}$ for $p$ odd, and $C^{[p]}$ for $p$ not an integer.
notFormalized.instead: **Not formalized** (cited from [9], Theorem 1, in the 2021 edition from [25]; deep Banach space geometry, not used on the main line; the preprint statement misses "$p$" in (1), (2), which the 2017 and 2021 statements print) (Findings, Chapter 5, items 117, 120, 179).

notFormalized.title: The $L^p$ and Sobolev remark
notFormalized.label: §5.5 (preprint §5.4.2), pp. 230–231 (preprint pp. 193–194)
notFormalized.book: The usual norms of $W^{k,p}(\Omega)$ have the differentiability of $\|\cdot\|_{L^p}$; $\beta(\|x\|^p)$ is a bump function of $L^p$; $W^{1,4}(\Omega)$ with $E_m = W^{1+m,4}(\Omega)$ admits sc-smooth bump functions, while for $W^{1,3/2}(\Omega)$ the straightforward one is only sc¹ — "does there exist a sc-smooth bump function on $E$?"
notFormalized.instead: **Not formalized.** It needs Sobolev spaces with their sc-structures (gap G.1) and Theorem 5.5.5 (preprint 5.32) (Findings, Chapter 5, item 118).

notFormalized.title: Theorem 5.5.13 (preprint 5.40): Toruńczyk
notFormalized.label: §5.5 (preprint §5.4.2), Theorem 5.5.13 (preprint 5.40), p. 234 (preprint p. 198)
notFormalized.book: A Banach space $E$ admits a $C^k$-partition of unity iff there are a set $\Gamma$ and a coordinate-wise $C^k$ homeomorphic embedding of $E$ into $c_0(\Gamma)$.
notFormalized.instead: **Stated, not proved** (`TorunczykStatement`, V5.59), and not used (cited from [9], Theorem 30) (Findings, Chapter 5, item 117).

notFormalized.title: Theorem 5.5.16 (preprint 5.43): Godefroy–Troyanski–Whitfield–Zizler
notFormalized.label: §5.5 (preprint §5.4.2), Theorem 5.5.16 (preprint 5.43), p. 235 (preprint p. 198)
notFormalized.book: If the WCG space $E$ admits a $C^k$-bump function, then it also admits $C^k$-partitions of unity.
notFormalized.instead: **Stated, not proved** (`GodefroyTroyanskiWhitfieldZizlerStatement`, V5.62; cited from [12] and [9], Theorem 31); it is an explicit hypothesis of Corollary 5.5.17 (preprint 5.44) (V5.63) (Findings, Chapter 5, items 116, 117).

notFormalized.title: Theorem 6.7.1 (preprint 6.43): the invariant $\Psi_{(f,o)}$
notFormalized.label: §6.7 (preprint §6.6), Theorem 6.7.1 (preprint 6.43), p. 277 (preprint p. 231) (proof pp. 277–279 (preprint pp. 231–233))
notFormalized.book: Over a tame $X$ with sc-smooth bump functions, a proper oriented sc-Fredholm section $(f, o)$ defines a linear map $\Psi_{(f,o)} : H^*_{dR}(X, \partial X) \to \mathbb R$ with (1) $\Psi_{(f,o)}([\omega, \tau]) = \int_{S_{f+s}}\omega - \int_{\partial S_{f+s}}\tau$ for every $s$ admissible for $(N, U)$, and (2) $\Psi_{(f_0,o_0)} = \Psi_{(f_1,o_1)}$ for a proper oriented homotopy. For $\partial X = \emptyset$, $\Psi_{(f,o)}([\omega]) = \int_{S_{f+s}}\omega$ on $H^n_{dR}(X)$, $n$ the index (p. 279 (preprint p. 233)).
notFormalized.instead: **Not formalized** (decision D1). It needs the sc-differential forms and their cohomology of §4.4 (gaps G.37–G.40), integration over oriented compact manifolds with boundary with corners and Stokes' theorem, which Mathlib does not have; its proof also uses the homotopy of Remark 5.3.8 (preprint 5.16) (gap G.44). What the theorem rests on is formalized: the perturbations of Theorem 5.3.10 (preprint 5.18) (V5.38, V5.39) and the tangent orientations of Theorem 6.6.18 (preprint 6.41) (V6.61) (Findings, Chapter 6, item 100).

notFormalized.title: §6.7 (preprint §6.6): the sections admissible for $(N, U)$
notFormalized.label: §6.7 (preprint §6.6), p. 276 (preprint p. 230)
notFormalized.book: For a proper oriented $(f, o)$ over a tame $X$ with bump functions and an auxiliary norm $N$, Theorem 5.3.10 (preprint 5.18) gives an open $U \supseteq S$ such that every sc⁺-section supported in $U$ with $N(s(x)) \le 1$ has a compact $S_{f+s}$; the distinguished ones, with $(f + s, x)$ in general position at every zero, have oriented solution sets and are called admissible for $(N, U)$.
notFormalized.instead: **Not formalized** as a notion; it is used only in Theorem 6.7.1 (preprint 6.43) (gap G.54). The facts recalled are formalized: Theorem 5.3.10 (preprint 5.18) (V5.38, V5.39) and the tangent orientations of the solution set (V6.61); the orientation of $S_{f+s}$ for a perturbed $f$ is gap G.69 (Findings, Chapter 6, item 101).

notFormalized.title: The facts on paths recalled on preprint p. 201
notFormalized.label: §6.2 (preprint §6.1), before Proposition 6.2.2 (preprint 6.2), p. 240 (preprint p. 201)
notFormalized.book: An M-polyfold is locally path connected, and any two smooth points in the same path component can be joined by an sc⁺-smooth path $\varphi : [0, 1] \to X$.
notFormalized.instead: **Not formalized** beyond a chart: inside the domain of a chart, nearby smooth points are joined by sc-smooth paths (`exists_nhds_scPath`, V6.49), and "in the same path component" (Definitions 6.6.2, 6.6.14 (preprint 6.27, 6.38)) is read as "joined by an sc-smooth path" (V6.58) (Findings, Chapter 6, item 42).

notFormalized.title: The alternative determinant $\lambda(\ker T) \otimes \lambda(\operatorname{coker}(T)^*)$
notFormalized.label: §6.4 (preprint §6.3), after Definition 6.4.1 (preprint 6.7), p. 246 (preprint p. 208)
notFormalized.book: Some authors use $\det(T) = \lambda(\ker T) \otimes \lambda(\operatorname{coker}(T)^*)$; the two definitions are naturally isomorphic, given a convention identifying $\lambda^*(A)$ and $\lambda(A^*)$.
notFormalized.instead: **Not formalized**, and not used: the chapter's formal statements use Definition 6.4.1 (preprint 6.7) (V6.8); the convention $\iota$ of Definition 6.3.1 (preprint 6.3) is V6.3 (Findings, Chapter 6, item 10).

notFormalized.title: The identification (95) and the maps $V \otimes \lambda(\mathbb R^n) \to V$
notFormalized.label: §6.4 (preprint §6.3), after Proposition 6.4.15 (preprint 6.15), p. 257 (preprint p. 213)
notFormalized.book: Dual to (94), $\mathbb R \to \lambda(\mathbb R^n)$ maps $1$ to the wedge of the standard basis, with inverse (95) $c_1 \wedge \dots \wedge c_n \mapsto \det([c_1, \dots, c_n])$; this gives identifications $V \otimes \lambda(\mathbb R^n) \to V$ and $V \otimes \lambda^*(\mathbb R^n) \to V$ for every finite-dimensional $V$.
notFormalized.instead: **Not formalized**, and not used: the formal statements use (94) only (V6.17, V6.18) (Findings, Chapter 6, item 10).

notFormalized.title: Lemma 6.5.3 (preprint 6.19) in general
notFormalized.label: §6.5 (preprint §6.4), Lemma 6.5.3 (preprint 6.19), p. 259 (preprint p. 216)
notFormalized.book: For finite-dimensional topological vector bundles $E$, $F$ over $X$, the bundles $\lambda(E)$, $\lambda^*(F)$, $E \oplus F$ and $E \otimes F$ have the structure of topological vector bundles in a natural way (a standard lemma, cited from [29]).
notFormalized.instead: **Not formalized** in general: Mathlib has no exterior powers or tensor products of vector bundles. The lemma is applied only to trivial bundles, and Proposition 6.5.4 (preprint 6.20) is proved with explicit frames (V6.22) (Findings, Chapter 6, item 22).

notFormalized.title: $\mathrm{DET}(E, F)$ is not orientable; the classical case
notFormalized.label: §6.5 (preprint §6.4), preprint p. 218; the opening of §6.6 (preprint §6.5), preprint p. 219
notFormalized.book: The text remarks that $\mathrm{DET}(E, F)$ is known to be non-orientable, though orientable over certain subsets. For a classical Fredholm map $f : U \to F$, the determinant line bundle of the $Df(x)$ is a smooth line bundle over $U$, with precisely two orientations if $U$ is contractible.
notFormalized.instead: **Not formalized** (remarks, not used). The orientability over convex sets of Fredholm operators, which is what the chapter uses, is Proposition 6.6.1 (preprint 6.26) (V6.30) (Findings, Chapter 6, item 26).

notFormalized.title: Proposition 6.6.3 (1) (preprint 6.28): sc-smooth contractibility
notFormalized.label: §6.6 (preprint §6.5), Proposition 6.6.3 (1) (preprint 6.28), p. 263 (preprint p. 220); Theorem 6.6.11 (preprint 6.35), Definition 6.6.12 (preprint 6.36), Theorem 6.6.13 (preprint 6.37)
notFormalized.book: The neighbourhood $U(x)$ of Proposition 6.6.3 (preprint 6.28) is sc-smoothly contractible (by $r(ty)$ on $U = r(V')$, $V'$ convex), and Theorem 6.6.11 (preprint 6.35), Definition 6.6.12 (preprint 6.36) and property (∗) of Theorem 6.6.13 (preprint 6.37) ask for sc-smoothly contractible neighbourhoods.
notFormalized.instead: **Not formalized.** As we read it, the proof does not establish (1) for $U$: it needs $r(V') \subseteq V'$, which is not stated. (1′) is proved instead (two sc-smooth paths in $U$ with the same end points are sc-smoothly homotopic in a larger $W$ with the end points fixed) and is what the proofs use (V6.32, V6.48, V6.50, V6.57) (Findings, Chapter 6, items 45, 53, 54, 72).

notFormalized.title: Lemma 6.6.5 (preprint 6.30) as a statement about manifolds
notFormalized.label: §6.6 (preprint §6.5), Lemma 6.6.5 (preprint 6.30), p. 265 (preprint p. 222)
notFormalized.book: The solution set of $F = 0$ near $(t, \varphi(t), 0)$ is a smooth manifold with boundary with corners, $\pi : S \to [0, 1]$ is a submersion, its fibres $S_t$ are manifolds with boundary with corners, and $L$ is a smooth vector bundle over $[0, 1]$.
notFormalized.instead: **Not formalized.** The kernels are formalized as a continuous family of subspaces of the model space (V6.34, V6.42), which is all the continuation of orientations needs (Findings, Chapter 6, item 48).

notFormalized.title: Property (P) of Lemma 6.6.4 (preprint 6.29) for the slices $F_t$
notFormalized.label: §6.6 (preprint §6.5), Lemma 6.6.4 (preprint 6.29), p. 265 (preprint p. 222)
notFormalized.book: (P): for every fixed $t \in [0, 1]$, the section $F_t$ is at $(\varphi(t), 0)$ in general position to the boundary of $X \times \mathbb R^k$.
notFormalized.instead: **Not formalized.** The general position of $F$ at the points $(t, \varphi(t), 0)$, which the text derives from (P) and which Lemmas 6.6.5, 6.6.6 (preprint 6.30, 6.31) use, is proved (V6.33). As we read it, (P) follows, since the tangent vectors of the family of zeros lie in $\ker F'$ and $\mathbb R^n$ has no boundary; this chart computation is not carried out (Findings, Chapter 6, item 47).

notFormalized.title: $\mathrm{Lin}(f, x)$ as sc-Fredholm operators on every level
notFormalized.label: §6.2 (preprint §6.1), Definition 6.2.1 (preprint 6.1), p. 239 (preprint p. 201)
notFormalized.book: The operators in $\mathrm{Lin}(f, x)$ are sc-Fredholm operators $T_xX \to Y_x$, all with the same Fredholm index.
notFormalized.instead: **Not formalized** on every level: at a chart point the members are shown Fredholm on level $0$, with the index $\mathrm{ind}(f, x)$ of V3.98, which is what the determinant lines use (V6.1) (Findings, Chapter 6, item 40).

notFormalized.title: Paths and families on $[0, 1]$; $X \times [0, 1]$ as an M-polyfold
notFormalized.label: §6.6 (preprint §6.5), pp. 263–276 (preprint pp. 220–230)
notFormalized.book: Paths, homotopies and families are sc-smooth maps on $[0, 1]$, $[0, 1]^2$, $[0, 1]^n$, and $X \times [0, 1]$, $[0, 1] \times X \times \mathbb R^k$ are M-polyfolds with boundary (Proposition 6.6.3 (preprint 6.28), Lemmas 6.6.4–6.6.10 (preprint 6.29–6.34), Theorem 6.6.11 (preprint 6.35), Remark 6.6.19 (preprint 6.42)).
notFormalized.instead: **Not formalized** as stated: they are read on $\mathbb R$, $\mathbb R^2$, $\mathbb R^n$ and $\mathbb R^n \times X$, of which only $[0, 1]$, $[0, 1]^2$, $[0, 1]^n$ matters (decision D2), as for Proposition 6.2.2 (preprint 6.2) in Chapter 3 (V3.98); a path that does not extend sc-smoothly to $\mathbb R$ is not covered (Findings, Chapter 6, items 71, 102).

notFormalized.title: Remark 6.6.19 (preprint 6.42) beyond a point
notFormalized.label: §6.6 (preprint §6.5), Remark 6.6.19 (preprint 6.42), p. 276 (preprint p. 230)
notFormalized.book: $\hat f(x, t) = f(x) + s(x, t)$ on $X \times [0, 1]$ has a natural orientation associated with $o$ and the standard orientation of $[0, 1]$.
notFormalized.instead: **Not formalized** beyond a point: that $(t, y) \mapsto \hat o$ is an orientation of $\hat f$ in the sense of Definition 6.6.16 (preprint 6.40) (continuity over the orientable neighbourhoods of $\mathbb R \times X$, independence of the chart of the pull-back bundle), built from an orientation of $f$. At a point the remark is V6.62 (Findings, Chapter 6, item 97).

notFormalized.title: Theorem 6.6.18 (preprint 6.41): the orientation of $S$ as a manifold
notFormalized.label: §6.6 (preprint §6.5), Theorem 6.6.18 (preprint 6.41), p. 275 (preprint p. 229)
notFormalized.book: The solution set $S$ is a smooth compact manifold with boundary with corners possessing a natural orientation.
notFormalized.instead: **Not formalized** as an orientation of the abstract finite-dimensional manifold $S$ (of its tangent bundle in the charts of the induced structure). What is formalized is the tangent orientation at each zero and its continuity along the sc-smooth paths of zeros in a chart (V6.61) (Findings, Chapter 6, item 92).

notFormalized.title: Theorem 6.6.18 (preprint 6.41): tangent orientations read in two charts
notFormalized.label: §6.6 (preprint §6.5), Theorem 6.6.18 (preprint 6.41), p. 275 (preprint p. 229)
notFormalized.book: $T_xS = \ker f'(x)$ is oriented by $o^f_x$, an object the text treats as independent of the chart.
notFormalized.instead: **Not formalized**: the compatibility of the tangent orientations read in two charts at the same zero. $\mathrm{Or}^f_x$ itself is identified between charts (V6.53–V6.55) (Findings, Chapter 6, item 92).

notFormalized.title: The paragraph after Theorem 6.6.18 (preprint 6.41): perturbed solution sets
notFormalized.label: §6.6 (preprint §6.5), after Theorem 6.6.18 (preprint 6.41), pp. 275–276 (preprint pp. 229–230)
notFormalized.book: If $f$ is not generic, a small perturbation $s$ supported near the zero set gives $S_{f+s}$ a natural orientation coming from $o^f$, since $\det((f + s)'(x))$ is oriented from $\mathrm{DET}(f, x)$ for $x \in S_{f+s}$.
notFormalized.instead: **Not formalized**: the perturbation, the orientation of $S_{f+s}$ coming from $o^f$, and the identification $\mathrm{Lin}(f + s, x) = \mathrm{Lin}(f, x)$ for an sc⁺-section $s$ that it uses. The perturbations themselves are Theorem 5.3.10 (preprint 5.18) (V5.38, V5.39) (Findings, Chapter 6, item 93).

notFormalized.title: Proposition 6.4.13 (2017: 6.6), last sentence: continuity in $T$
notFormalized.label: §6.4, Proposition 6.4.13 (2017: 6.6), p. 253 (2017 p. 195)
notFormalized.book: For $T'$ near $T$ with $P, Q \in \Pi_{T'}$, the constructions of $A_{T'}$ and $B_{T'}$ depend continuously on $T'$ (keeping $X$, the equation for $x(e)$ stays uniquely solvable).
notFormalized.instead: **Formalized since the first edition of this page** (V6.69, V6.70). A closed common complement $X$ of the kernels exists (`exists_isClosed_isTopCompl_isTopCompl_of_finrank_eq`), and with it $A_S$ (extended to $E$) and $B_S$ (lifted to $F$) depend continuously on $S$ near $T$ in the operator norm, also jointly with the vector, i.e. on the kernel bundle of Remark 6.4.5; for every such $S$ they are the text's isomorphisms filling the diagram (`proposition_6_4_13_continuity_2021`). The algebraic part is V6.67 (Findings, Chapter 6, items 113, 117).

notFormalized.title: Theorem 6.6.17 (2) without connected smooth neighbourhoods
notFormalized.label: §6.6, Theorem 6.6.17 (2), p. 275 (new in the 2021 edition)
notFormalized.book: For every $x \in X_\infty$ there is an open $U = U(x)$ in $X$ such that $O_f|(U \cap X_\infty)$ has precisely two continuous sections.
notFormalized.instead: **Proved only under `MPolyfold.HasConnectedSmoothNbhds`** (V6.74, V6.75): every smooth point has arbitrarily small open neighbourhoods $U$ in $X$ with $U \cap X_\infty$ connected in $X_\infty$. Every continuous section over $U \cap X_\infty$ is locally one of the two continuous orientations, so (2) needs such a $U$; Part I does not state the fact, and the paths of `exists_nhds_scPath` join the smooth points of a small $V$ only inside a larger $U$. It holds for $\mathbb R^n$ (`rnPolyfold_hasConnectedSmoothNbhds`) and is open in general. The proofs of §7.4 use that $U \cap X_\infty$ is connected for connected open $U$ (`MPolyfold.SmoothConnected`, gap G.85), which, as we read it, gives the hypothesis, M-polyfolds being locally path connected (Proposition 2.3.7). Existence and uniqueness of the Hausdorff topology with (1) and (3) need no such hypothesis (`existsUnique_orientationTopology_2021`) (Findings, Chapter 6, item 120).

notFormalized.title: The remarks after Theorem 6.6.17: the orientation bundle, orientability, $\mathbb Z_2$ and $\det_f$
notFormalized.label: §6.6, after Theorem 6.6.17, p. 275 (new in the 2021 edition)
notFormalized.book: $\pi_f : O_f \to X_\infty$ with the topology of Theorem 6.6.17 is the orientation bundle of $f$; $f$ is orientable iff $\pi_f$ has a global continuous section; $\mathbb Z_2$ acts continuously on $O_f$ by $(x, o_x) \mapsto (x, -o_x)$; $\det_f = \mathbb R \otimes_{\mathbb Z_2} O_f \to X_\infty$ is the determinant bundle of $f$.
notFormalized.instead: **Not formalized.** The topology itself is V6.73–V6.75; the comparison of global continuous sections of $\pi_f$ with the orientations of Definitions 6.6.14–6.6.16 (V6.58–V6.60), the $\mathbb Z_2$-action and the line bundle $\det_f$ are not formalized (Findings, Chapter 6, item 121).

notFormalized.title: Definition 7.1.4 (2017: 7.4): the tangent $T\varphi$ as an sc-isomorphism
notFormalized.label: §7.1, Definition 7.1.4 (2017: 7.4) and the paragraph before it, 2017 p. 227
notFormalized.book: For a smooth morphism $\varphi$, i.e. $\varphi \in \mathbf X_\infty$, there is an associated sc-isomorphism $T\varphi : T_{s(\varphi)}X \to T_{t(\varphi)}X$ defined by $T\varphi := T\hat\varphi(x)$; $T\varphi$ can be defined for $\varphi$ on level at least $1$ and gives a bounded linear isomorphism on level $0$, and only for smooth $\varphi$ is $T\varphi$ an sc-operator. Definition 7.1.4 (2017: 7.4) associates with a smooth morphism $\varphi$ the local sc-diffeomorphism $\hat\varphi$ and its tangent $T\varphi$.
notFormalized.instead: **Not formalized** beyond the definition: `tangentMor` defines $T\varphi$ (V7.5), but that it is well defined, equal to $T\hat\varphi(s(\varphi))$, bijective, a bounded linear isomorphism on level $0$ for $\varphi \in \mathbf X_1$ and an sc-operator for smooth $\varphi$ is not formalized; the linearity needs the linear structure of the tangent spaces, which the project does not have (gap G.7). Not used in Chapter 7; deferred to Chapter 8 (Findings, Chapter 7, items 5, 110). Since 2026-11-07 (Chapter 8): well defined, $T\varphi(Ts(h)) = Tt(h)$ for every $h \in T_\varphi\mathbf X$ (`tangentMor_tSrc`), and functorial, $T(\psi \circ \varphi) = T\psi \circ T\varphi$ for $\varphi \in \mathbf X_1$ (`tangentMor_comp`), with the description of $T\mathbf X$ by the pairs $(T\varphi, a)$ of Remark 8.1.10 (2017: 8.1) (`remark_8_1`); the bijectivity and linearity of $T\varphi$, $T\varphi = T\hat\varphi(s(\varphi))$ and the sc-operator property remain not formalized (V8.12; Findings, Chapter 8, item 112).

notFormalized.title: Proposition 7.2.10 (2017: 7.9) and Proposition 7.10 (2017; rewritten in 2021 as Theorem 7.2.14): $\mathbf X^R$ Hausdorff and paracompact
notFormalized.label: §7.2, Proposition 7.2.10 (2017: 7.9) and Proposition 7.10 (2017), pp. 313–324 (2017 pp. 242–244)
notFormalized.book: Proposition 7.2.10 (2017: 7.9): the reduced morphism set $\mathbf X^R$ has a natural M-polyfold structure. Proposition 7.10 (2017): every ep-groupoid $X$ possesses an associated reduced ep-groupoid $X_R$, and $X_R$ is effective. Since an M-polyfold is a paracompact Hausdorff space (Part I, Definition 2.3.4 (2017: 2.8)), these assert in particular that $\mathbf X^R$, with the quotient topology, is Hausdorff and paracompact, for every ep-groupoid $X$. The 2021 edition rewrites this: Remark 7.2.8 (p. 311) says that in general $(X, \mathbf X^R)$ cannot be made an ep-groupoid, Proposition 7.2.12 (p. 317) proves $T_R$ paracompact for every ep-groupoid, Proposition 7.2.13 (p. 318) makes it an M-polyfold exactly when it is Hausdorff, and Theorem 7.2.14 (p. 318) builds $X_R$ under the hypothesis that $T_R$ is Hausdorff, characterized in Theorem 7.2.22 (p. 323).
notFormalized.instead: **Closed by the 2021 edition**, in its 2021 form. In the 2017 form, for every ep-groupoid, the statement does not hold as we read it: for $\mathbb Z/2$ acting on the dimension-jumping retract of Part I's Remark 4.2.2 (2017: 4.3), $\mathbf X^R$ is not Hausdorff (`Examples.exists_not_t2Space_reducedMor`, formalized after the round-trip audit), and the hypotheses `[T2Space X.ReducedMor] [ParacompactSpace X.ReducedMor]` of `reducedPolyfold` were the project's (V7.39, V7.40). The 2021 text is consistent with this: Remark 7.2.8 announces such examples, Appendix 7.6.3 gives Zhou's, of the same kind (V7.82). Paracompactness is now proved for every ep-groupoid (`paracompactSpace_reducedMor`, an instance, V7.77), which also settles the question, left open here, of paracompactness when $\mathbf X^R$ is Hausdorff; the Hausdorff hypothesis is exactly that of 2021 Theorem 7.2.14 (V7.78), and Theorem 7.2.22 characterizes it by LUC and the closedness of $\mathbf X^T$ (V7.81) (Findings, Chapter 7, items 56, 60, 107, 111, 125, 126, 129).

notFormalized.title: The filtration of $|X|$: the set $|X_\infty|$
notFormalized.label: §7.1, 2017 p. 228
notFormalized.book: Since $ml(x) = ml(y) = ml(\varphi)$ for every morphism $\varphi : x \to y$, the filtration of $X$ induces the filtration $|X| = |X_0| \supset |X_1| \supset \dots \supset |X_\infty| = \bigcap_{k \ge 0} |X_k|$ of the orbit space $|X| = X/\sim$.
notFormalized.instead: **Not formalized** beyond the levels: $|X_k| = \pi(X_k)$ is `orbitLevel k`, and $s$, $t$ preserve the levels (V7.6); the set $|X_\infty|$ and the identity $|X_\infty| = \bigcap_k |X_k|$, immediate as $ml$ is constant on classes, are not stated (Findings, Chapter 7, items 6, 112).

notFormalized.title: The density of $X_\infty$ in $X_k$
notFormalized.label: §7.1, 2017 p. 227
notFormalized.book: The M-polyfolds $X$ and $\mathbf X$ carry the filtrations $X = X_0 \supset X_1 \supset \dots \supset X_\infty = \bigcap_k X_k$; the set $X_\infty$ is dense in every space $X_k$.
notFormalized.instead: **Not formalized**: the text states the density without proof; Part I proves it only for sc-Banach spaces (`ScBanach.denseRange_incl`), and its text does not state it for M-polyfolds or retracts. For a retract $O = r(U)$ it follows from the continuity of $r$ on level $k$ and the density of $U_\infty$ in $U_k$, which for $U$ open in a partial quadrant $C$ needs $C \cap E_\infty$ dense in $C \cap E_k$. Chapter 7 uses the filtration, never the density. Found by the round-trip audit (V7.6) (gap G.73; Findings, Chapter 7, item 116).

notFormalized.title: Theorem 7.6.7: the sc-diffeomorphism $(X^i)_R \cong (X_R)^i$, and $i \ge 2$
notFormalized.label: §7.6, Theorem 7.6.7 and Corollary 7.6.8, p. 351 (new in the 2021 edition)
notFormalized.book: Under (SLUC), the natural set-theoretic identification between $(X^1)_R$ and $(X_R)^1$ is an sc-diffeomorphism between the object spaces and the morphism spaces; for every $i$ there is a similar identification between $(X^i)_R$ and $(X_R)^i$. Corollary 7.6.8: the same under (ZHOU).
notFormalized.instead: **Not formalized** beyond $i = 1$ as sets: under LUC for $X^1$ and the hypothesis that every $x \in X_1$ has a natural representation with $U(x) \cap X_1$ connected in $X^1$ and dense in $U(x)$ (the density is gap G.73), $(\mathbf X^1)^T = (\mathbf X^T)^1$ and $[\varphi]_1 \mapsto [\varphi]$ is a continuous injection $(\mathbf X^1)^R \to \mathbf X^R$ onto $\pi(\mathbf X_1)$ (V7.83). The sc-diffeomorphism needs the M-polyfold $(\mathbf X^R)^1$; $i \ge 2$ needs the lifts of $X_R$ (Findings, Chapter 7, item 131).

notFormalized.title: Appendix 7.6.3: Zhou's retract and its exact non-effective part
notFormalized.label: §7.6, Appendix 7.6.3, p. 348, and §7.4, p. 331 (new in the 2021 edition)
notFormalized.book: Zhou's example: $\mathbb Z/2$ acting on the retract of Part I's Subsection 1.4.4 by $(s, f) \mapsto (s, -f)$; $\mathrm{cl}(\mathbf X^T) \setminus \mathbf X^T$ is one point, so $T_R$ is not Hausdorff and (LUC) fails; the example does not satisfy the Zhou condition (p. 331).
notFormalized.instead: **Not formalized** for Zhou's retract: the analogue `JumpingRetract.X` ($\mathbb Z/2$ on the retract of Part I's Remark 4.2.2 (2017: 4.3)) has a point of $\mathrm{cl}(\mathbf X^T) \setminus \mathbf X^T$, $T_R$ not Hausdorff and LUC failing (V7.82); $\mathbf X^T$ is not computed exactly, and that it fails (ZHOU) is proved given the Part I facts `SmoothRegular` for its object M-polyfold (V7.95) (Findings, Chapter 7, items 130, 139).

notFormalized.title: §7.4 for the index lifts $X^i$, $i \ge 2$: Propositions 7.4.9 and 7.4.18
notFormalized.label: §7.4, Proposition 7.4.9, p. 333, and Proposition 7.4.18, p. 336 (new in the 2021 edition)
notFormalized.book: Proposition 7.4.9: if $X$ satisfies the Zhou condition, so does every $X^i$ (the condition (ZHOU') being the same for $X$ and $X^i$). Proposition 7.4.18: (VSLUC) and (SLUC) are equivalent. Corollary 7.4.11, Theorems 7.4.13, 7.4.24 and Proposition 7.4.16 use them for every $X^i$.
notFormalized.instead: **Formalized since the first edition of this page** (Springer 2021 additions; V7.102–V7.104). The inclusions $X_{m+1} \to X_m$ are continuous and $(X^1)_\infty \to X_\infty$ is a homeomorphism; with Part I's Proposition 2.3.17 for $i = 1$ and the comparison of the natural representations of $X$ and $X^1$, (ZHOU') passes from $X$ to $X^1$, hence to every $X^i$, and Proposition 7.4.9 follows, with Corollary 7.4.11, Theorems 7.4.13 and 7.4.24 for (ZHOU) on $X$ only (V7.102). (VSLUC) and the density of $X_\infty$ pass from $X$ to every $X^i$, giving Propositions 7.4.16 and 7.4.17 (V7.103). Proposition 7.4.18 is proved in both directions, (SLUC) ⇒ (VSLUC) under natural representations with every $U(x) \cap X_m$ connected, which the text takes by construction (V7.104). Not formalized: (ZHOU') from $X^i$ back to $X$, which the proof does not use; the Part I facts stay hypotheses on every level (gap G.85) (Findings, Chapter 7, items 137, 148–150).

notFormalized.title: The Part I facts used in §7.4, and the connectedness of $U(x) \cap X_1$
notFormalized.label: §7.4, Lemma 7.4.4, p. 329, and the proofs of Lemma 7.4.6 to Proposition 7.4.22, pp. 331–340 (new in the 2021 edition)
notFormalized.book: The proofs use facts about M-polyfolds: $X_\infty$ dense in every $X_m$; $U(x) \cap X_\infty$ connected for connected open $U(x)$; tangent vectors approximated by tangent vectors at nearby smooth points; sc-smooth maps agreeing near a smooth point in $X_\infty$ have the same tangent there; $(T_xX)_\infty$ dense in $T_xX$. The proof of Lemma 7.4.4 uses that $U(x) \cap X_1$ is connected in $X^1$ and dense in $U(x)$.
notFormalized.instead: **Not formalized**; explicit, satisfiable hypotheses: `MPolyfold.SmoothRegular` (`DenseSmooth`, gap G.73; `SmoothConnected`; the openness of $p : TX \to X^1$, gap G.8; `TangentDeterminedSmooth`), `MPolyfold.DenseSmoothTangent`, and `HasLevelOneConnectedDenseReps` / `HasConnectedDenseLevelOneReps`, each satisfied by the point ep-groupoid (V7.83, V7.85, V7.86) (Findings, Chapter 7, items 133, 134). Since the second batch of 2021 additions the results for every $X^i$ take these facts on every level: `SmoothRegular` for every $X^i$ (V7.102), `SmoothConnected` for every $X^i$ (V7.103, V7.104); `DenseSmooth` passes from $X$ to every $X^i$ by proof (`EP.denseSmooth_lift`). Proposition 7.4.18 also takes natural representations with every $U(x) \cap X_m$ connected, `NaturalRep.LevelConnected`, the text's "by construction" (V7.104) (Findings, Chapter 7, items 148–150).

notFormalized.title: Definitions 8.2.1, 8.2.2 (2017: 8.2, 8.3): sc-differential forms on ep-groupoids and the sc-de Rham complex
notFormalized.label: §8.2, Definitions 8.2.1 and 8.2.2 (2017: 8.2 and 8.3), pp. 372–375 (2017 pp. 268–270)
notFormalized.book: Definition 8.2.1 (2017: 8.2): an sc-differential $k$-form on the ep-groupoid $(X, \mathbf X)$ is an sc-smooth map $\omega : \oplus^k TX \to \mathbb R$ on the Whitney sum of the tangent of the object M-polyfold, linear in each argument and skew-symmetric, with $(T\varphi)^*\omega_y = \omega_x$ for every morphism $\varphi : x \to y$ in $\mathbf X_1$; $\Omega^k_{ep}(X)$ is the vector space of these forms. A form on $X^i$ is a form on $X^{i+1}$, and $\Omega^*_{ep,\infty}(X)$ is the direct limit of the directed system $\Omega^*_{ep}(X^i) \to \Omega^*_{ep}(X^k)$, $i \le k$. The exterior derivative is $d[\omega] := [d\omega]$, with $d\omega$ compatible with morphisms and $d \circ d = 0$. Definition 8.2.2 (2017: 8.3): $(\Omega^*_{ep,\infty}(X), d)$ is the sc-de Rham complex of the ep-groupoid $X$.
notFormalized.instead: **Not formalized.** It needs the Whitney sums $\oplus^k TX$ as M-polyfolds, the linear structure of $T_xX$ (gap G.7), linear maps $T\varphi$ (gap G.70), the M-polyfolds $X^i$ for $i \ge 2$ (gap G.6, closed since: V2.93, V2.97) and the sc-differential forms, the Lie bracket and the exterior derivative of Part I's §4.4 (gaps G.37–G.39), which are not formalized; the Lie bracket on an M-polyfold is formalized since (V4.76, gap G.38 closed). Nothing else in Chapter 8 depends on it. Definition 8.2.1 (2017: 8.2) writes $T_yY$ for $T_yX$ (possible misprint) (Findings, Chapter 8, item 110).

notFormalized.title: Lemma 8.1.2 (2017: 8.1): $T(\mathbf X\,{}_s{\times}_t\,\mathbf X) = T\mathbf X\,{}_{Ts}{\times}_{Tt}\,T\mathbf X$ and $m_{T\mathbf X} = Tm$
notFormalized.label: §8.1, 2017 p. 259, the identification before Lemma 8.1.2 (2017: 8.1) and Lemma 8.1.2 (2017: 8.1) (also the proof of Lemma 8.1.7 (2017: 8.6), p. 362 (2017 p. 262))
notFormalized.book: The tangent $T(\mathbf X\,{}_s{\times}_t\,\mathbf X)$ of the sub-M-polyfold $\mathbf X\,{}_s{\times}_t\,\mathbf X$ of $\mathbf X \times \mathbf X$ is identified with $T\mathbf X\,{}_{Ts}{\times}_{Tt}\,T\mathbf X \subseteq T\mathbf X \times T\mathbf X$. Lemma 8.1.2 (2017: 8.1): the multiplication (8.5) of $T\mathbf X$ can be written as $(\psi, k) \circ (\varphi, h) = Tm(\psi, \varphi)(k, h) = (\psi \circ \varphi, (Ts(\psi \circ \varphi))^{-1} \circ Ts(\varphi)(h))$, with $k = Ts(\psi)^{-1}(Tt(\varphi)(h))$. The proof of Lemma 8.1.7 (2017: 8.6) notes that the multiplication of $T\mathbf X$ is precisely $Tm$, hence sc-smooth.
notFormalized.instead: **Not formalized** as printed: the identification of the tangent of the fibred product with the fibred product of the tangents, and $m_{T\mathbf X} = Tm$ on it, are not stated. Lemma 8.1.2 (2017: 8.1) is formalized in the form its proof uses: on a sheet $s : W \to V$ with inverse $\sigma$, $k \circ h = Tg(h)$ for $g(\varphi') = m(\sigma(t\varphi'), \varphi')$ (`lemma_8_1`, V8.4); the sc-smoothness of the multiplication of $T\mathbf X$ on $T\mathbf X\,{}_{s_T}{\times}_{t_T}\,T\mathbf X$ is proved from Chapter 7's sheet form (`isScSmoothComp_tangent`, V8.9), so nothing in Chapter 8 depends on the identification (Findings, Chapter 8, items 5, 111).

notFormalized.title: Proposition 8.4.1, (1) ⇒ (2), (3), and Proposition 8.4.3
notFormalized.label: §8.4, Proposition 8.4.1, p. 380, and Proposition 8.4.3, p. 382 (new in the 2021 edition)
notFormalized.book: Proposition 8.4.1: $|X|$, $|W[0]|$ and $|W[1]|$ are paracompact together. Proposition 8.4.3: if $X$ is effective and has the local regularity property (LR) of Definition 7.4.19, every strong bundle over $X$ has the local regularity property of Definition 8.4.2.
notFormalized.instead: **Not formalized**: (1) ⇒ (2), (3) needs $G_x$-equivariant strong bundle charts with invariant metrics and $W[1]$ as an ep-groupoid; Proposition 8.4.3 needs the openness of $P : W \to X$ and the lift of (LR) to the bundle. Formalized: (2) ⇒ (1) (V8.47) and Definition 8.4.2 (V8.48) (Findings, Chapter 8, items 118, 119).

notFormalized.title: Proposition 8.2.3: the Poincaré lemma for sc-differential forms on ep-groupoids
notFormalized.label: §8.2, Proposition 8.2.3, p. 373 (new in the 2021 edition)
notFormalized.book: Poincaré lemma: every object $x$ has saturated open neighbourhoods $V \subseteq U$ such that for every closed $[\omega] \in \Omega^k_{ep,\infty}(U)$, $k \ge 1$, there is $[\sigma] \in \Omega^{k-1}_{ep,\infty}(V)$ with $d[\sigma] = [\omega]$ on $V$; the proof averages a primitive from Lemma 4.4.8 over $G_x$.
notFormalized.instead: **Not formalized**, with the forms of §8.2 (gap G.74), which need the Whitney sums $\oplus^k TX$, the linear structure of $T_xX$ (gap G.7) and the forms of Part I's §4.4 (gaps G.37–G.40) (Findings, Chapter 8, item 123).

notFormalized.title: Proposition 8.1.16 without `TangentZhouReflect`
notFormalized.label: §8.1, Proposition 8.1.16, p. 369 (new in the 2021 edition)
notFormalized.book: Proposition 8.1.16: (ZHOU) for $X$ gives (ZHOU) for $TX$, by differentiating (8.16) and using that $T\tau$ is onto.
notFormalized.instead: **Not formalized** for Proposition 8.1.16: the step $T(g, h) = \mathrm{id} \Rightarrow Tg = \mathrm{id}$ needs the second tangent bundle $T(TX)$ and $T\tau$, and is the hypothesis `TangentZhouReflect` (V8.44). The entry's second part, Proposition 8.1.17 (2) for every $(TX)^i$ (p. 371), which needed $(TX)^i = T(X^i)$ and was proved for $(TX)^0$ (V8.45), is **formalized since the first edition of this page** (Springer 2021 additions; V8.52): Part I's Proposition 2.3.17 gives $T(X^i) \cong (TX)^i$ as ep-groupoids (sc-diffeomorphisms of objects and morphisms commuting with source and target), which transports LUC by Proposition 7.2.21 (Findings, Chapter 8, items 115, 116, 124).

notFormalized.title: Lemma 8.5.10: $F^*V$ with $\mu_{F^*V}$ as a strong bundle over the ep-groupoid $Y$
notFormalized.label: §8.5, Lemma 8.5.10, p. 395 (new in the 2021 edition)
notFormalized.book: The pull-back $F^*V$, with $\mu_{F^*V}(\varphi, (y, v)) = (t(\varphi), \mu_X(F(\varphi), v))$, is a strong bundle over the ep-groupoid $Y$, and $B : W \to F^*V$ is a strong bundle isomorphism over $Y$.
notFormalized.instead: **Not formalized**: that $\mu_{F^*V}$ satisfies the conditions of a strong bundle over an ep-groupoid (Definition 8.3.1 (2017: 8.4)); the lemma is proved with its formula only, $B$ a strong bundle isomorphism $W \to F^*V$ with (8.23) (V8.51) (Findings, Chapter 8, item 122).

notFormalized.title: Remark 9.1.1 on a general M-polyfold: the local constancy of the dimension; the footnote to Definition 9.1.2 and "locally equidimensional"
notFormalized.label: §9.1, Remark 9.1.1, p. 402 (2017: Remark 9.1, p. 291), and Definition 9.1.2, last paragraph and footnote, p. 402
notFormalized.book: The dimension of $T_mM$ is locally constant in $m \in M$; an $n$-dimensional $\Theta$ is not $m$-dimensional for $m \ne n$; locally equidimensional $\Theta$.
notFormalized.instead: **Not formalized** on a general M-polyfold: the local constancy is the hypothesis `HasLocallyConstantDimAt`, proved on $\mathbb R^m$ (`hasLocallyConstantDimAt_rn`); elsewhere the dimensions of the $M_i$ are labellings taken as hypotheses (V9.2). The footnote and "locally equidimensional" are not formalized (Findings, Chapter 9, items 2, 3).

notFormalized.title: Remark 9.1.4: metrizability of paracompact subsets of $|X|$ and the compactness criterion
notFormalized.label: §9.1, Remark 9.1.4, p. 403 (new in the 2021 edition)
notFormalized.book: A paracompact $L \subseteq |X|$ is metrizable (Smirnov); if $|\mathrm{supp}(\Theta)|$ meets every connected component of $|X|$ in a compact set, its paracompactness is automatic (Corollary 7.3.8).
notFormalized.instead: **Not formalized**; the paracompactness of $|\mathrm{supp}(\Theta)|$ is a field of the definition (V9.1) (Findings, Chapter 9, item 7).

notFormalized.title: Proposition 9.1.9 and Remark 9.1.10: natural manifold and orbifold structures on $|\mathrm{supp}(\Theta)|$
notFormalized.label: §9.1, Proposition 9.1.9, p. 405 (2017: Proposition 9.1, p. 294), and Remark 9.1.10 (2017: Remark 9.3)
notFormalized.book: For $X$ with paracompact orbit space, $|\mathrm{supp}(\Theta)|$ carries a natural smooth manifold structure if $\Theta$ is of manifold type and a natural orbifold structure if it is of orbifold type, in the M⁺-polyfold sense (Remark 9.1.10).
notFormalized.instead: **Not formalized**: it needs manifold and orbifold structures on orbit spaces of ep-groupoids, which the project does not define; the types themselves are formalized (V9.8) (Findings, Chapter 9, item 7).

notFormalized.title: Proposition 9.1.11: the global decomposition and a repaired uniqueness
notFormalized.label: §9.1, Proposition 9.1.11, pp. 407–408 (2017: Proposition 9.2, p. 297)
notFormalized.book: The local $\Theta_k$ glue to branched ep⁺-subgroupoids with $\Theta = \sum_k \Theta_k$, locally finite, and the family is unique.
notFormalized.instead: **Not formalized**: the gluing of the local $\Theta_k$ across morphisms, the paracompactness of $|\mathrm{supp}(\Theta_k)|$ and the local finiteness; the uniqueness does not hold as we read it (`not_proposition_9_1_11_rn`) and would need an extra condition. The local construction is verified (V9.9) (Findings, Chapter 9, item 8).

notFormalized.title: The graph representation of Lemmas 9.2.9–9.2.11 on a general M-polyfold, and Proposition 9.2.8 as printed
notFormalized.label: §9.2, Proposition 9.2.8, p. 413 (2017: Proposition 9.3, p. 302), and Lemmas 9.2.9–9.2.11, pp. 414–417 (2017: Lemmas 9.6–9.8); used in Proposition 9.1.12, p. 408
notFormalized.book: Near a bad point the sheets of one tangent class are graphs over a cone in their common tangent space (sc-complements, the mean value formula for sc⁺-retractions, an inverse function argument in a partial quadrant), giving the partition and the sequences of good points of Proposition 9.2.8.
notFormalized.instead: **Not formalized** on a general M-polyfold: Part I has no level-0 sc-calculus in partial quadrants. The graph representation is the hypothesis `HasGraphChartAt` (also `HasGraphChartsAt`, `HasGraphBallAt`), proved on $\mathbb R^m$; Proposition 9.2.8 is formalized in slice form (V9.22). On a general M-polyfold Proposition 9.1.12 (V9.10), the independence in Theorem 9.2.1 (V9.14), Lemma 9.3.4 (V9.32), Lemma 9.6.4 (V9.61) and Proposition 9.6.5 (V9.62) rest on it (Findings, Chapter 9, items 25, 100).

notFormalized.title: Lemma 9.2.7 (2) on a general M-polyfold: invariance of domain
notFormalized.label: §9.2, Lemma 9.2.7 (2), p. 412 (2017: Lemma 9.5 (2), p. 301)
notFormalized.book: Every sheet through a bad point contains good points converging to it; the proof shrinks neighbourhoods inside sheets of one dimension.
notFormalized.instead: **Not formalized** on a general M-polyfold: invariance of domain for equal-dimensional submanifolds is the hypothesis `HasDomainInvarianceAt`, proved on $\mathbb R^m$ (V9.21) (Findings, Chapter 9, item 24).

notFormalized.title: Definition 9.2.12: the $TM_i$ as smooth submanifolds of $TX$
notFormalized.label: §9.2, Definition 9.2.12, p. 418 (2017: Definition 9.6, p. 306)
notFormalized.book: $T\Theta$ is a branched ep⁺-subgroupoid of $TX$ with local branching structures $(TM_i)$, $(\sigma_i)$.
notFormalized.instead: **Not formalized**: that the tangent of the sc⁺-retraction presenting $M_i$ is sc⁺ on $TX$, so that $TM_i$ is a smooth submanifold of $TX$; it is the field `isSmoothSubmanifold` of `TangentBranchingHyp`, also on $\mathbb R^m$, where $TM_i$ is proved a sub-M-polyfold of $TX$ (V9.23) (Findings, Chapter 9, item 26).

notFormalized.title: Lemma 9.3.4 on a general M-polyfold: the level-1 continuity of frame fields
notFormalized.label: §9.3, Lemma 9.3.4, p. 423 (2017: Lemma 9.10, p. 311)
notFormalized.book: The proof compares orientations of different sheets along sequences of good points converging to a bad point.
notFormalized.instead: **Not formalized** on a general M-polyfold: the comparison needs the continuity of chart frames on level 1, the hypothesis `HasContinuousLevelOneOn`, proved on $\mathbb R^m$ (V9.32) (Findings, Chapter 9, item 53).

notFormalized.title: Example 9.3.5: the classification of all orientations of $\Theta$
notFormalized.label: §9.3, Example 9.3.5, p. 425 (2017: Example 9.1, p. 313)
notFormalized.book: There are four possibilities to orient, and the second structure cannot necessarily be oriented to coincide with the first.
notFormalized.instead: **Not formalized** as a classification (it needs the connectedness of the graphs and the continuity of orientations along them); the last claim is proved for the orientations $\pm(1, \beta')$ of the second structure, and at least five orientations with weights $1$ are exhibited (V9.33) (Findings, Chapter 9, item 54).

notFormalized.title: Definition 9.3.6: a tame $M_i$ is a manifold with boundary with corners
notFormalized.label: §9.3, Definition 9.3.6, p. 425 (2017: Definition 9.10, p. 314)
notFormalized.book: In particular every $M_i$ of a tame $\Theta$ has an equivalent structure of a smooth manifold with boundary with corners.
notFormalized.instead: **Not formalized**: the project has no bridge from tame finite-dimensional M⁺-polyfolds to Mathlib manifolds with corners; the definition itself is formalized (V9.34) (Findings, Chapter 9, item 55).

notFormalized.title: Definitions 9.3.8 and 9.3.10: $T_y\partial M = T^R_yM$, the outward direction, the continuity of $o_{\partial M}$ and Figure 9.1
notFormalized.label: §9.3, Definition 9.3.8, p. 427 (2017: Definition 9.9, p. 313), and Definition 9.3.10, p. 428 (2017: Definition 9.11, p. 314)
notFormalized.book: For tame $M$ with $d_M(y) = 1$, $T_y\partial M$ and the outward half-space are given by the cones $C_yM$; the boundary orientation is continuous along $\partial M$ and extends to the closed faces (Figure 9.1); Remark 9.3.11 on the non-tame case.
notFormalized.instead: **Not formalized**: $T_y\partial M$ and the outward vector are data $K$, $e$ in `boundaryFrames`, and the boundary operation is a function `bd` in (9.12) (V9.36–V9.38); the partial cones of submanifolds are not formalized (Findings, Chapter 9, items 57, 58).

notFormalized.title: Lemma 9.4.3: Property (T) after shrinking $U(x)$
notFormalized.label: §9.4, Lemma 9.4.3, p. 430 (2017: Lemma 9.12, p. 316)
notFormalized.book: Every oriented branching structure at a smooth $x$ has Property (T) on a smaller $U'(x)$; the proof uses the continuity of $z \mapsto T_{r_i(z)}M_i$ in charts and a contradiction argument along sequences.
notFormalized.instead: **Not formalized**: it needs the continuity of the change-of-frame determinant of two sheets in charts at points where their tangent spaces agree; Property (T) is a definition, and Proposition 9.4.10 is proved without it (V9.41, V9.48) (Findings, Chapter 9, item 71).

notFormalized.title: Lemmas 9.4.4 and 9.4.6 for sheets in an M-polyfold
notFormalized.label: §9.4, Lemma 9.4.4, p. 431 (2017: Lemma 9.13, p. 317), and Lemma 9.4.6, p. 431 (2017: Lemma 9.14)
notFormalized.book: Essential points of $K(i, i')$ do not depend on the reference sheet; the non-essential points have measure zero; for submanifolds of an M-polyfold, in M-polyfold charts.
notFormalized.instead: **Not formalized** for M-polyfold sheets, which carry no Mathlib manifold structure in the project: they are the fields `ess_comm` and `isNull_diff_ess` of `SheetGeometry`, satisfiable for smooth graphs in $\mathbb R^2$; Lemma 9.4.6 is proved for Mathlib manifolds (V9.42, V9.44) (Findings, Chapter 9, item 72).

notFormalized.title: Definition 9.5.1 and Lemma 9.5.2 with Lebesgue null sets in the sheets of a general M-polyfold, and Lemma 9.5.2 across dimensions
notFormalized.label: §9.5, Definition 9.5.1 and Lemma 9.5.2, p. 437 (2017: Definition 9.15 and Lemma 9.16, p. 322)
notFormalized.book: Measure zero in $S$ through measure zero (Definition 9.4.5) of the preimages in the sheets $M_i$ of a choice of local branching structures; independence of the choice, cited from the literature.
notFormalized.instead: **Not formalized** for the Lebesgue null sets of submanifolds of a general M-polyfold, which carry no Mathlib manifold structure in the project: the null sets are the abstract system `SheetNullSets` (the fields of `SheetMeasureGeometry`), satisfiable on $\mathbb R^2$ (cf. G.105); Lemma 9.5.2 is proved for structures with sheets of one class, and for every structure of an $n$-dimensional $\Theta$ it would need Proposition 9.1.12 in general (G.97) (V9.49, V9.50) (Findings, Chapter 9, items 80, 81).

notFormalized.title: Branched integration: Theorems 9.5.4 and 9.5.5, Definition 9.5.6, (9.21)–(9.22), and the measure identities of Lemmas 9.5.7, 9.5.9–9.5.11, Remark 9.5.8 and Proposition 9.5.13
notFormalized.label: §9.5, Theorem 9.5.4, p. 438 (2017: Theorem 9.2, p. 323), Theorem 9.5.5, p. 438 (new in the 2021 edition), to Proposition 9.5.13, p. 446
notFormalized.book: For an oriented, tame, compact, $n$-dimensional branched ep⁺-subgroupoid there is a unique linear map $\omega \mapsto \mu^{\hat\Theta}_\omega$ from sc-differential $n$-forms to signed measures on $(S, L(S))$, given locally by weighted integrals of $\omega$ over the oriented sheets (Theorem 9.5.5: the effective version under LUC); the proof (Definition 9.5.6, Lemma 9.5.7, (9.21)–(9.22), Lemmas 9.5.9–9.5.11) shows that the local measures agree on overlaps; Proposition 9.5.13 compares the two integrals.
notFormalized.instead: **Not formalized**: it needs the sc-differential forms on ep-groupoids of §8.2 and Part I (gaps G.74, G.80) and integration over the sheets. The σ-algebra $L(S)$ (V9.51), the isotropy orders, (9.23) and the decompositions of the preimages on which Lemmas 9.5.9–9.5.11 and Proposition 9.5.13 rest are formalized (V9.54–V9.57); the combinatorics of Lemma 9.5.7 is Proposition 9.4.10 (V9.48) (Findings, Chapter 9, items 84, 85).

notFormalized.title: $(n-1)$-dimensional measure zero in the boundary faces, and a witness for $L(\partial S)$
notFormalized.label: §9.5, the paragraph before Definition 9.5.14, p. 448
notFormalized.book: For $K \subseteq |\partial M_U|$ the preimages lie in the $\partial M_i$, where, $M_i$ being tame, $(n-1)$-dimensional measure zero makes sense in the boundary faces.
notFormalized.instead: **Not formalized**: measure zero in $\partial M_i$ is a second abstract `SheetNullSets` on the boundaries; the description face by face is not formalized, and no witness with $\partial S \ne \emptyset$ is given (V9.52) (Findings, Chapter 9, item 83).

notFormalized.title: Theorems 9.5.15 and 9.5.16: canonical boundary measures
notFormalized.label: §9.5, Theorem 9.5.15, p. 449 (2017: Theorem 9.3, p. 328), and Theorem 9.5.16, p. 449 (new in the 2021 edition)
notFormalized.book: For an oriented, tame, compact $n$-dimensional $\Theta$ there is a unique linear map $\omega \mapsto \mu^{\partial\hat\Theta}_\omega$ from $(n-1)$-forms to signed measures on $(\partial S, L(\partial S))$, given locally by integrals over the $\partial M_i$ with the boundary orientation (Theorem 9.5.16: the effective version under LUC).
notFormalized.instead: **Not formalized**, with branched integration (gaps G.74, G.80, G.107); $L(\partial S)$ is formalized (V9.52) (Findings, Chapter 9, item 85).

notFormalized.title: Theorems 9.5.17 and 9.5.18: Stokes' theorem, and Remark 9.5.20
notFormalized.label: §9.5, Theorem 9.5.17, p. 449 (2017: Theorem 9.4, p. 328), Theorem 9.5.18, p. 450 (new in the 2021 edition), and Remark 9.5.20, p. 451
notFormalized.book: For $X$ with sc-smooth partitions of unity and $\Theta$ tame, oriented, compact, $n$-dimensional, $\mu^{\partial\hat\Theta}_\omega(\partial S) = \mu^{\hat\Theta}_{d\omega}(S)$ for every $(n-1)$-form $\omega$ (Theorem 9.5.18: the effective version under LUC); Remark 9.5.20, on a translation groupoid with a $\mathbb Z_3$-action, shows that the effective isotropy group of a boundary point depends on whether it is taken in $X$ or in $\partial X$, which enters the normalization in Stokes' formula.
notFormalized.instead: **Not formalized**: it needs the exterior derivative on ep-groupoids (gaps G.74, G.80) and the measures of G.107 and G.109 (Findings, Chapter 9, item 85).

notFormalized.title: the full subcategory $\mathcal{EP}_{lreg}$
notFormalized.label: §10.1, the subcategory $\mathcal{EP}_{lreg}$, p. 461 (new in the 2021 edition)
notFormalized.book: The full subcategory of $\mathcal{EP}$ generated by the ep-groupoids with the local regularity property (Definition 7.4.19).
notFormalized.instead: **Not formalized**: (LR) is Chapter 7's `IsLR`; the subcategory is not built; its stability under equivalences is Proposition 10.1.9, formalized since (V10.62) (Findings, Chapter 10, item 7).

notFormalized.title: Remark 10.1.8 and Appendix §10.6.3, a $\beta$ with $|\beta(y)| = |y|$ not given by the group
notFormalized.label: §10.1, Remark 10.1.8, p. 467 (new in the 2021 edition), with Appendix §10.6.3, p. 519
notFormalized.book: An example, due to Zhou, of a translation groupoid and an sc-smooth map $\beta$ with $|\beta(y)| = |y|$ which is not locally of the form $y \mapsto g * y$; it is built in the appendix on a weighted Sobolev sc-retract.
notFormalized.instead: **Not formalized**: it needs the weighted Sobolev sc-structure and the sc-retraction of the appendix (Findings, Chapter 10, item 7).

notFormalized.title: Proposition 10.1.9, (LR) under equivalences
notFormalized.label: §10.1, Proposition 10.1.9, p. 468 (new in the 2021 edition)
notFormalized.book: If $F : X \to Y$ is an equivalence, $X$ has the local regularity property iff $Y$ has.
notFormalized.instead: **Formalized since the first edition of this page** (V10.62): $Q = \hat\psi \circ F$, the isomorphism $g \mapsto \psi \circ F(g) \circ \psi^{-1}$ and natural representations carried along $Q$ both ways; the printed target $U(y)$ of $\sigma \mapsto \psi \circ \sigma \circ \psi^{-1}$ is read $G_y$ (Findings, Chapter 10, items 7, 16).

notFormalized.title: Proposition 10.1.10, natural families $\alpha_z : F(z) \to G(z)$
notFormalized.label: §10.1, Proposition 10.1.10, p. 470 (2017: Proposition 10.4, p. 340)
notFormalized.book: For equivalences $F, G : X \to Y$ with $|F| = |G|$ and $X$ with (LR): (1) local sc-smooth families $\alpha$ with $\alpha(z) : F(z) \to G(z)$; (2) $|TF| = |TG|$.
notFormalized.instead: **Formalized since the first edition of this page** (V10.63), with (LR) for one of $X$, $Y$ only; the families are in general not natural (V10.65) (Findings, Chapter 10, items 7, 16).

notFormalized.title: Proposition 10.1.19 beyond the reduction to Proposition 10.1.9
notFormalized.label: §10.1, Proposition 10.1.19, p. 477 (new in the 2021 edition)
notFormalized.book: If $F$ is an equivalence, $X$ satisfies (SLR) iff $Y$ does.
notFormalized.instead: **Formalized since the first edition of this page** (V10.16): the reduction with Proposition 10.1.9 (V10.62) for the lifts (Findings, Chapter 10, items 15, 16).

notFormalized.title: Theorem 10.2.2: the structures induced from the triple products
notFormalized.label: §10.2, Theorem 10.2.2, pp. 478–481 (2017: Theorem 10.2, pp. 343–346), the M-polyfold structures
notFormalized.book: The object and morphism sets of $X \times_Y Z$ are sub-M-polyfolds of $X \times \mathbf Y \times Z$ and $\mathbf X \times \mathbf Y \times \mathbf Z$.
notFormalized.instead: **Not formalized**: the structures are the iterated sub-M-polyfold structures of Part I's fibred products (V10.18); their agreement with structures induced from the triple products is not proved, and nothing uses it (Findings, Chapter 10, item 21).

notFormalized.title: the universal property of the localization
notFormalized.label: §10.3, the universal property of $i : \mathcal{EP} \to \mathcal{EP}(E^{-1})$, p. 483
notFormalized.book: The localization at $E$ inverts the equivalences, universally among functors that do.
notFormalized.instead: **Not formalized**: only the inversion is proved (V10.45); the universal property would need that a functor inverting $E$ identifies naturally equivalent sc-smooth functors, through a cylinder ep-groupoid not available here (Findings, Chapter 10, item 36).

notFormalized.title: Proposition 10.3.16 and the (LR), (SLR) parts of Theorem 10.3.21
notFormalized.label: §10.3, Proposition 10.3.16, p. 492 (new in the 2021 edition), and Theorem 10.3.21, p. 495, the parts (LR) and (SLR)
notFormalized.book: (LR) and (SLR) are invariant under generalized isomorphisms.
notFormalized.instead: **Formalized since the first edition of this page** (V10.64, V10.50): Propositions 10.1.9 and 10.1.19 for the legs of a representing diagram, as the text does (Findings, Chapter 10, items 16, 38).

notFormalized.title: Remark 10.3.18: generalized isomorphisms with $\beta' \circ |f| = \beta$ are not unique
notFormalized.label: §10.3, Remark 10.3.18, pp. 492–493 (2017: Remark 10.3, p. 355), the non-uniqueness of $f$
notFormalized.book: A generalized isomorphism $f$ with $\beta' \circ |f| = \beta$ is in general not unique.
notFormalized.instead: **Formalized since the first edition of this page** (V10.60), by the example of Remark 10.5.5: the base classes of $[1_W]$ and $[W \xleftarrow{1} W \xrightarrow{\mathrm{Inv}} W]$ over $\mathbb Z/3 \times \mathbb R \rightrightarrows \mathbb R$ are two distinct generalized isomorphisms with the same orbit map, so with $\beta' = \beta \circ |f|^{-1}$ both satisfy $\beta' \circ |f| = \beta$; the relation itself is V10.48 (Findings, Chapter 10, items 39, 56).

notFormalized.title: Theorem 10.3.19, generalized isomorphisms are determined by their orbit maps under (LR)
notFormalized.label: §10.3, Theorem 10.3.19, p. 493 (2017: Theorem 10.7, p. 355)
notFormalized.book: If one of $X$, $Y$ has (LR) and $f, f' : X \to Y$ are generalized isomorphisms with $|f| = |f'|$, then $f = f'$.
notFormalized.instead: **Formalized since the first edition of this page** (V10.65, V10.66), as a statement that does not hold as we read it: on $\mathbb Z/3 \times \mathbb R \rightrightarrows \mathbb R$ with the trivial action, which has (LR), two generalized isomorphisms with the same orbit map differ; the proof's step on p. 494 uses the families $\alpha_a$ of Proposition 10.1.10 (1) as a natural transformation, which in the example none is. With $Y$ effective the theorem holds (V10.66) (Findings, Chapter 10, items 17, 39, 58).

notFormalized.title: Theorem 10.4.5, the Fred part
notFormalized.label: §10.4, Theorem 10.4.5, p. 501 (2017: Theorem 10.8, p. 362), the sc-Fredholm section functors
notFormalized.book: $\Phi_*$ and $\Phi^*$ map sc-Fredholm section functors to sc-Fredholm section functors.
notFormalized.instead: **Not formalized**: it needs the invariance of sc-Fredholm sections under local strong bundle isomorphisms, of which Part I has chart-level germ statements only; the rest of the theorem is V10.27 (Findings, Chapter 10, item 44).

notFormalized.title: Propositions 10.4.6 and 10.4.7, (LR) and natural families for strong bundles
notFormalized.label: §10.4, Proposition 10.4.6, p. 501 (new in the 2021 edition), and Proposition 10.4.7, pp. 501–502 (new in the 2021 edition)
notFormalized.book: The local regularity property of strong bundles is invariant under strong bundle equivalences (proof left to the reader), and the strong bundle version of Proposition 10.1.10.
notFormalized.instead: **Not formalized**: the ep-groupoid versions are formalized since (V10.62, V10.63); the strong bundle versions need the transport $H_{\hat\psi}$ as a strong bundle isomorphism at levels $0$ and $1$ and the inverse of a strong bundle isomorphism on an open set, which the strong bundle API does not provide (Findings, Chapter 10, item 45).

notFormalized.title: the transitivity of the equivalence of diagrams of strong bundles, the composition in $\mathcal{SEP}(F^{-1})$ and the strong bundle version of Theorem 10.3.10
notFormalized.label: §10.5, p. 504 (2017 p. 364), Definition 10.5.1, p. 506 (2017: Definition 10.14, p. 366), and Remark 10.5.3, p. 506 (new in the 2021 edition)
notFormalized.book: Equivalence of diagrams of strong bundles is an equivalence relation, generalized strong bundle maps compose to a category $\mathcal{SEP}(F^{-1})$, and a generalized strong bundle map is invertible iff it is represented with both legs strong bundle equivalences.
notFormalized.instead: **Formalized since the first edition of this page** (V10.68–V10.71), except the converse half of the strong bundle Theorem 10.3.10. The weak fibred product of strong bundles is the pull-back of $W''$ along $\pi_Z$ (V10.68), the equivalence of diagrams is transitive (V10.69), and the composition makes $\mathcal{SEP}(F^{-1})$ a category (V10.70, V10.55); a diagram with both legs strong bundle equivalences represents an isomorphism (V10.71). Still open: that an isomorphism of $\mathcal{SEP}(F^{-1})$ is represented with both legs strong bundle equivalences, proved for the base functor only; for the strong bundle functor it would need strong bundle versions of the claims (C1), (C2) of Appendix §10.6.2 (Findings, Chapter 10, items 18, 19, 50, 53).

notFormalized.title: (10.24) with generalized vertical maps, and the local expressions $q$, $Q$ of (10.25)
notFormalized.label: §10.5, the symbolic diagram (10.24) and the diagram (10.25), pp. 505–506 (2017 pp. 365–366)
notFormalized.book: With generalized maps as vertical arrows the diagram (10.24) commutes (left to the reader); an equivariant sc-smooth germ $q : O(X, x) \to O(X', x')$ with $q(g * z) = \gamma(g) * q(z)$, and its strong bundle lift $Q$.
notFormalized.instead: **Not formalized**: the text uses no property of them, and $q$, $Q$ depend on the representative; the homomorphism $\gamma$ is formalized (V10.54) (Findings, Chapter 10, items 51, 52).

notFormalized.title: Theorem 10.5.4, the Fred part
notFormalized.label: §10.5, Theorem 10.5.4, p. 508 (2017: Theorem 10.9, p. 367), the sc-Fredholm section functors
notFormalized.book: $[D]_*$ maps $\mathrm{Fred}(P, \mu)$ onto $\mathrm{Fred}(P', \mu')$.
notFormalized.instead: **Not formalized**: it rests on the Fred part of Theorem 10.4.5 (G.121); the rest of the theorem is V10.59 (Findings, Chapter 10, item 55).

notFormalized.title: Proposition 10.5.6 beyond the reduction to Proposition 10.4.6
notFormalized.label: §10.5, Proposition 10.5.6, p. 508 (new in the 2021 edition)
notFormalized.book: The local regularity property passes along generalized strong bundle isomorphisms.
notFormalized.instead: **Not formalized** unconditionally: the reduction to strong bundle equivalences is proved (V10.61); Proposition 10.4.6 is G.122 (Findings, Chapter 10, item 57).

notFormalized.title: Theorem 10.5.7, generalized strong bundle isomorphisms determined by their orbit maps
notFormalized.label: §10.5, Theorem 10.5.7, p. 508 (2017: Theorem 10.10, p. 367)
notFormalized.book: If both strong bundles have the local regularity property and $[D], [D']$ are generalized strong bundle isomorphisms with $|[D]| = |[D']|$, then $[D] = [D']$.
